【0】Background：

【1】Bowel obstruction is a mechanical or functional obstruction of the intestines which prevents the normal move-ment of the products of digestion. Intestinal malrotation is one of the rarest causes of mechanical bowel ob-struction. In adults， the incidence rate is 0.2%， and 15% of all patients with confirmed diagnosis remain as-ymptomatic throughout life. Surgery is generally required when the patient is symptomatic.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 30-year-old man with multiple admissions for chronic intermittent colicky abdominal pain since childhood， was admitted for symptoms suggestive of proximal small bowel obstruction. Tomographic imaging identified a midgut malrotation and a duodenal obstruction by a non-diseased displaced appendix. Laparoscopic libera-tion of the duodenum and the terminal ilium was done successfully.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Intestinal malrotation is infrequently encountered in the adult population， but it should be kept in mind as a differential diagnosis whenever a case of acute intestinal obstruction in an adult presents without any signif-icant past surgical history.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Duodenal Obstruction · Intestinal Obstruction·Upper Gastrointestinal Tract Bowel obstruction is a mechanical or functional obstruction of the intestines which prevents the normal movement ofthe products of digestion. Either the small or large bowel may be affected. Signs and symptoms include abdominal pain， vomiting， bloating， and non-passing of gas. Intestinal malrotation is one of the rarest causes of mechanical bowel obstruction. It is a congenital anomaly that was first reported by William Ladd in 1932. The source of this disease arises in the embryogenic stages when the bowels undergo a partial rotation or even non-rotation in the superior mesenteric artery axis . Rotational anomaly of the midgut is uncommon in adults. The disease is usually symptomatic during the first couple of years， with some even claiming that 90% of patients will seek medical help during the first year of life . However， certain cases are not symptomatic until much later in life， which may cause misdiagnosis . Surgery is required generally when they are symptomatic. About 0.2% of the adult general population is affected， with 15% of diagnosed individuals remaining symp-tom-free . The aim of this case report is to present a rare case of bowel obstruction consisting of duodenal obstruction caused by a displaced non-diseased appendix. This patient came to our hospital with a misdiagnosis and a delay in man-agement， which might have increased the morbidity and mor-tality. We present this case to raise awareness of this rare di-agnosis， thereby preventing delay of definitive diagnosis and management.

【7】Case Report

【8】A 30-year-old man who was a hepatitis B carrier with multiple hospital admissions for chronic recurrent post-prandial pain-less vomiting， was admitted to the hospital for investigations. A gastroscopy was done and was positive for a dilated fluid-filled stomach， without any signs of gastric outlet obstruction.

【9】The patient was then discharged on medical treatment. A few weeks later the patient was admitted again for the same com-plaint but this time it was associated with a new onset of dif-fuse abdominal pain， colicky in nature， most severe in the epigastric area， radiating to the back. The pain increased in severity over the next 2 days and was associated with nau-sea and vomiting. During this admission， we (the general sur-gery team) were consulted for assessment.

【10】His physical exam was unremarkable except for mild general-ized abdominal tenderness and diffuse tympani on a soft ab-domen. There were no signs of peritoneal irritation.

【11】Laboratory tests were requested， including complete blood count， electrolytes， liver function tests， and pancreatic enzymes， and all results were within normal range. Computed tomography(CT) imaging was done and revealed a dilated fluid-filled stomach and duodenum . Along the axis of the superior mesenteric artery， intestinal malrotation was apparent， with a whirlpoo. sign at the level of the proximal jejunum. The patient was prepared for laparoscopic repair.

【12】After establishing pneumoperitoneum and entering the abdom-inal cavity， our exploration showed that almost the entire large bowel was displaced to the left side and the small bowels to the right. The caecum was located to the right upper quadrant next to the dilated duodenum passing beneath it .

【13】The jejunum was also found to be in a defect through the terminal ileum mesentery， without any signs of obstruction. Further dissection showed a band-like structure that was encircling the duodenum， causing its narrowing， which was later found to be the appendix .

【14】After careful dissection， the anatomy was difficult to assess， so the decision was made to convert to laparotomy. After reen-tering the abdomen， the appendix was found to be encircling the duodenum two and a half turns， narrowing it and causing its obstruction， so an appendectomy was done followed by rotating the small bowels anticlockwise back to near-normal anatomy after liberation of the duodenum and terminal ileum. The post-operative course was smooth and unremarkable， with the patient passing flatus and stools on post-operative day 3， and he was then discharged home the following day.

【15】Discussion

【16】Intestinal malrotation is a developmental anomaly of the midgut in which there is failure in rotation of the bowels around the superior mesenteric artery and in their fixation to the perito-neal cavity . Rotational anomalies ofthe midgut are rare in adults， and， according to medical history， most cases are as-ymptomatic and go undiagnosed . Such patients who be-come symptomatic will have an either acute or chronic clinical scenario： acutely， they present with bowel obstruction and ischemia， but chronically， they present with vague abdominal pain and recurrent vomiting .

【17】In our case， changes were acute on top of a chronic congenital condition. The intestinal volvulus encountered was caused by the incorrect placement of the small bowels narrowing the pedicle of superior mesenteric vessels. These chronic vague symptoms increase the likelihood of misdiagnosis， and， more likely than not， the patient will seek medical help from several doctors， who will eventually attribute the complaints to intes-tinal motility or psychiatric illnesses .

【18】Ultrasound can detect the reversal of the normal anatomic relationship between the superior mesenteric vessels， the whirl-pool sign of the midgut volvulus， and the bird-beak appearance of the duodenal obstruction， but with a false-positive rate of up to 21%， but contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen shows intestinal malrotation with the midgut volvulus and anatomic location of small bowels and colon with features of obstruc-tion and gangrene with very high sensitivity and specificity . However， in acute and complicated cases， the diagnosis must be confirmed by surgical exploration .

【19】Regarding treatment， there is no standard of care. Surgical cor-rection of asymptomatic or incidentally discovered disease is controversial. Many clinical scenarios and complications exist because the intestinal malrotation is not a single congenital entity， but rather is a spectrum of rotational anomalies . Elective Ladd procedure is becoming more commonly used for patients with a chronic clinical presentation， and emer-gent laparotomy is still the mainstay for patients with an acute and complicated presentation . There is much debate surrounding asymptomatic patients. Some authors argue that early surgical intervention for an incidentally discovered mal-rotation is warranted because currently there are no modali-ties able to predict which asymptomatic patients will become symptomatic. This will avoid more catastrophic and probably fatal complications such as midgut volvulus . Other au-thors support watchful waiting for asymptomatic patients .

【20】Conventional Ladd procedure remains the most common and effective method to alleviate intestinal malrotation. Currently. the growing number of laparoscopic Ladd procedures per-formed is encouraged by its good results， low morbidity， and short hospital stay .

【21】Conclusions

【22】Intestinal malrotation is infrequently encountered in the adult population； however， it should be considered as a differential diagnosis whenever a case of acute intestinal obstruction in an adult presents without any significant past history.

【0】Background：

【1】Postoperative chylous ascites is a rare complication of retroperitoneal and mediastinal surgery that represents a difficult management problem.

【2】We here present a case of a resected retroperitoneal recurrent liposarcoma with a consecutively infected retroperitoneal chylous fistula refractory to surgical and medical treatment.

【3】Case Report：

【4】A 70-year-old male patient was operated because of retroperitoneal recurrence of a liposarcoma diagnosed during a follow-up CT scan four years after en-bloc tumorectomy.

【5】He developed infected chylous ascites refractory to conservative treatment. Despite revision laparotomy four weeks later and intensive care treatment with broad spectrum antibiotic and antimycotic therapy the fistula persisted in producing two to five liters a day. The patient died two months after revision laparotomy.

【6】Conclusions：

【7】Mindful of the possibility of secondary infection of ascites， especially when drainage is not complete， early reoperation and treatment with broad spectrum antibiotics should be discussed.

【8】Key words： chylous ascites · infection · management

【9】Postoperative chylous ascites is a rare complica-tion of retroperitoneal and mediastinal surgery that represents a difficult management problem due to serious mechanical， nutritional and immunological consequences of the steady loss of fluid， protein， electrolytes， immune cells and the inadequate fat absorption .

【10】To date diagnosis and management are not well estab-lished， not even in cases with secondary infection.

【11】Most patients can be treated conservatively using total parenteral nutrition in combination with soma-tostatin to block intestinal function. Even in cases of refractory chylous ascites that recurs or persists after a surgical attempt to ligate the lymphatic duct， conservative treatment can be successful . Direct surgical repair shows good outcome when the leak is identified.

【12】Retroperitoneal sarcomas are rare malignant tumors with an aggressive course and a high local recurrence rate. Erzen et al. evaluated 155 patients retrospectively and concluded that radical resection is the only op-tion， even when multivisceral resections are neces-sary. Long-term survival can be achieved in patients without microscopic residuum or contamination of the operation field. Until now treatment alternatives such as radio- and/or chemotherapy have been limited. Therefore， aggressive surgery is also recommended for recurrent sarcoma .

【13】We here present a case of a resected retroperitoneal recurrent liposarcoma with a consecutively infected retroperitoneal chylous fistula refractory to surgical and medical treatment.

【14】CASE REPORT

【15】A 70-year-old male patient was operated because of retroperitoneal recurrence of a liposarcoma diagnosed during a follow-up CT scan four years after en-bloc tumorectomy performed in combination with right nephrectomy and adrenalectomy. The new tumor mass was located between the aorta and vena cava close to the left renal vein without vascular or organ infiltration. The tumor was completely removed en-bloc. Additional diagnosis was an artificial mitral valve replaced several years previously.

【16】Initial postoperative course was uneventful and the patient seemed to recover fully. Noteworthy is the fact that the drainage never stopped producing fluid， namely more than 2 liters a day. The fluid appeared milky and contained high triglycerides after having started enteral nutrition. Consequently， total paren-teral nutrition consisting of a high-protein， low-fat， medium-chain triglyceride diet， and intravenous somatostatin therapy were initiated. One week later Staphylococcus aureus was cultivated from the as-cites and specific antibiotic therapy was therefore initiated.

【17】Despite subsequent microbiological surveillance and fluid replacement the patient developed a sepsis-like syndrome a few days later and was transferred to the intensive care unit； he was reoperated the next day after stabilization. The lymphatic leak suspected in the mesenteric trunk could not be localized. The abdomen was then extensi vely lavaged and a rub- ber drain placed where the leak was Dersuspected with the goal of inducing a fibrotic drain channel， which usually closes spontaneously after removal of the drain.

【18】Over the next two months the fistula steadily pro duced two to five liters per day. After eradication of bacteria one month later， antibiotic therapy was discontinued. Furthermore， the patient developed a candida sepsis and endocarditis of the artificial valve confirmed by transesophageal sonography， which never fully resolved despite treatment with last-genera-tion antimycotic medication (caspofungin) and broad spectrum antibiotic combinations.

【19】Ultimately， the patient did not recover from ongoing subtle sepsis triggered by therapy-refractory endo carditis. A mitral valve replacement was discussed， but due to several risk factors it was not performed with the consent of the family.

【20】The patient died two months after revision lapa-rotomy.

【21】DISCUSSION

【22】Major oncologic retroperitoneal resections involve extensive dissection that may disrupt the major retro-peritoneal lymphatic channels and result in chylous collections.

【23】Baniel et al. reported a 1.2% incidence in a series of1，520 patients who underwent retroperitoneallymph node dissection for testis cancer .

【24】On the other hand， abdominal aortic surgery is the most common etiology of postoperative chylous ascites， causing 81% of all chylous complications from retroperitoneal lymphatic glands or cisterna chili .

【25】Common conservative treatment consists of repeat therapeutic paracentesis， a high-protein，low-fat， me-dium-chain triglyceride diet， salt restriction， diuretics and total parenteral nutrition  and， more recently， the administration of somatostatin .

【26】The literature gives no guidelines for the duration of attempted non-operative therapy before the surgical option is raised. Surgery is rarely performed early due to the effectiveness of conservative measures. Since some protracted cases may be resolved only after weeks or months of conservative treatment， a non-operative attempt for at least four to eight weeks is probably warranted before surgical exploration . A risk factor for infections in this period could be the steady loss of proteins and lymphocytes .

【27】Thus， the dilemma is how long is it reasonable to pursue the “wait-and-see”tactic. After four weeks of conservative treatment with constant lymph produc-tion and finally infected chylous ascites， we decided to immediately do a surgical revision laparotomy. The patient s clinical status deteriorated rapidly and there was no time for further diagnostic imaging.

【28】An infected lymphatic fistula is a special entity and if not drained accurately it represents an acute， life-threat-ening disease. In our case the operative revision lapa-rotomy was certainly performed too late. Astonishingly， there were no intraoperative signs of peritonitis.

【29】After revision laparotomy and intensive care treat-ment with broad spectrum antibiotic and antimycotic therapy there were no signs of bacterial infection of ascites in the microbiologic controls. But the fistula persisted in producing two to five liters a day.

【30】The immediate problem to be solved was the continu-ous ascites formation and the ongoing sepsis due to secondary endocarditis. There was no reason to do a second intervention for a non-localized fistula and a past frustrating first reintervention. Moreover，high-volume ascites as well as ongoing endocarditis and subtle sepsis precluded the use of peritoneovenous shunting or fibrin glue.

【31】Mindful of the possibility of secondary infection of ascites， especially when drainage is not complete， early reoperation and treatment with broad spectrum antibiotics should be discussed.

【32】CONCLUSIONS

【33】We have come to the conclusion that a long period of conservative treatment is not always advisable be-cause of the high loss of proteins and immune cells and the elevated risk of infection.

【34】Whether to operate or not in such a situation is a delicate decision and must be made on a case-to-case basis.

【0】ABSTRACT Background： Endotracheal extubation is connected to airway and cardiovascular reactions that can result in tachycardia， hypertension， arrhythmias， myocardial ischemia， coughing， agitation， bronchospasm， increased haemorrhaging and raised intracranial and intraocular pressure， all of which can be life-threatening， especially in weaker patients. These effects are observed to be attenuated by dexmedetomidine， a highly selective 2 adrenoreceptor agonist that provides a smooth extubation. Aim： To evaluate the impact of dexmedetomidine following tracheal extubation on hemodynamic and ventilatory recovery. Methods： 40 patients who matched the inclusion and exclusion criteria and were between the ages of 21 and 46 were divided randomly into two groups of 20 each for this comparative study. 90 ml of NS was given to one group， while 0.4 mg of Dexmedetomidine was given to the other. At various points throughout the entire operation， the hemodynamic parameters of the two groups were compared to check for any variations. Results： Compared to the control group， the study group had better control over mean arterial pressure， systolic blood pressure， diastolic blood pressure， and heart rate. It is the statistical significance (P < 0.002) that the extubation quality score differed between the control and dexmedetomidine groups (2.13 vs 1.23). Cough was present in 14.27% of the study group and 52.38% of the control group. The study population had considerably more Bradycardia and Hypertension. Conclusion： Dexmedetomidine is administered just before extubation to guarantee a smooth procedure and lessen cardiovascular reactions. Additionally， it offers sufficient postoperative sedation.

【1】Introduction

【2】Tracheal intubation is performed during surgery to preserve a patent airway and to make tracheal suctioning easier. Tra-cheal extubation is weaning off mechanical breathing following surgery when the patient is no longer in need. Without anaes-thesia， reflex reactions such as tracheal and laryngeal discomfort might happen during extubation . Laryngospasm， coughing， breath retention， or straining should not occur during extuba-tion . Increased plasma catecholamines， tachycardia， and hypertension that result in increased cardiac contractility and systemic vascular resistance can be connected to weaning from anaesthesia and ventilatory support . As a result of the car-bon dioxide insufflations and pneumoperitoneum necessary for laparoscopic procedures， there may be an increase in plasma renin activity， adrenaline， and nor-adrenaline levels， which could increase pulmonary and systemic vascular resistance， hyperten-sion， tachycardia， and reduced cardiac output.

【3】Further reducing cardiac output during surgery is the reverse Trendelenburg position， which also lowers venous return. At the time of extubation， these hemodynamic alterations put the my-ocardium at risk of ischemia， which could be fatal in susceptible patients . Some theories have been put forth for the abrupt rise in heart rate (HR) and blood pressure (BP) during extubation. Following extubation， the peak alterations start within the first minute and can last up to 10 minutes. The majority of patients tolerate these adjustments without any significant negative ef-fects. These hemodynamic reactions may or may not be tolerated by patients with systemic illnesses such as coronary artery dis-ease， diabetes， and hypertension . Intravenous lignocaine， short-acting opioids like fentanyl and remifentanil， esmolol， la-betalol， dexmedetomidine， diltiazem， verapamil， alfentanil， li-docaine， magnesium sulphate， propofol， and intratracheal local anaesthetic instillation are just a few of the medications being utilised to lessen . A highly selective 2-adrenoreceptor ago-nist， dexmedetomidine， causes analgesia and sedation without changing the patient’s breathing status . It is eight times more effective than clonidine at reducing stress-induced cate-cholamine release . Dexmedetomidine has been observed to significantly lower serum catecholamine levels when given intravenously during the perioperative period. This lowers the patient's hemodynamic response to laryngoscopy， tracheal in- tubation， pneumoperitoneum， and extubation. Additionally， it offers sedation without resulting in respiratory depression， re-ducing the need for post-operative analgesics . It is clear from the literature that there is a considerable drop in catecholamine levels in the blood， which lowers the risk of hypertension and tachycardia. Consequently， this study was started to determine how dexmedetomidine affected hemodynamic variables and recovery responses during and after tracheal extubation.

【7】Methodology

【8】This research is prospective and comparative. Before the study got underway， it received approval from the institution’s ethics committee. Forty patients of both genders， ranging in age from21 to 46， were randomly divided into two groups. Subjects meet-ing the American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I and II and those scheduled for elective general surgical， urological， and gynaecological operations without complications are included in the criteria for inclusion. Patients with severe obesity (body mass index > 30)， renal insufficiency (serum creati-nine > 1.5 mg/dl)，liver dysfunction (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase/serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase values >51% of normal)， difficult airways， cardiorespiratory abnormali-ties， and planned or emergency surgeries in the neck and oral cavity are excluded from the study.

【9】Patients who met the inclusion criteria were informed of their rights and the trial’s purpose， and all study participants provided signed informed consent. All study participants un-derwent a thorough physical examination and detailed history-taking during the pre-anaesthetic assessment. Additionally， rou-tine tests such as complete blood count， urea and serum crea-tinine， and blood grouping/typing were done. Patients were denied oral intake for a period of five hours prior to surgery. All patients received the same premedication of Inj. Glycopyrrolate0.1 mg IM 20 minutes before being transferred to the operating room. A cannula for intravenous access was placed when the patient entered the operating room. The standard anaesthetic methods and medicines applied to both groups were isoflu-rane， fentanyl， propofol， nitrous oxide-oxygen， and vecuronium. Pulse oximetry， non-invasive blood pressure monitoring， and EtCO2 ECG constitute standard monitoring (Spo2). By using the sealed envelope method， subjects were randomly split into two groups of twenty each. One group of participants received 90ml of normal saline (NS) containing 0.4 mcg/kg of dexmedeto-midine for 10 minutes. Only over 10 minutes did the patients in the other group get 90 ml of NS. This was given 20 minutes before the conclusion of the treatment.

【10】Hemodynamic parameters were noted at the beginning of the intravenous NS or drug injection and after 2， 6， 9 and 14minutes. Neostigmine 0.04 mg/kg and atropine 0.01 mg/kg given intravenously break up the remaining neuromuscular inhibition. Once the patient's throat had been suctioned， and he was able to breathe on his or her own and follow simple instructions， the trachea was extubated. The research medicines were hidden from the anesthesiologist conducting the tracheal extubation. After the extubation， parameters were recorded for2， 6，9 and 14 minutes.

【11】A heart rate of under 50 beats per minute was considered bradycardia. Bradycardia must be treated with intravenous atropine if hemodynamic instability is present. A fall in sys-tolic blood pressure of more than 20 mmHg or means arterial pressure of less than 50 mmHg from baseline was considered hypotension. In a few necessary situations， 2 mg of IV mephen-termine was used in addition to intravenous fluids to correct it. A prevalidated and structured five-point like rt scale was used to evaluate the quality of extubation based on the patient’s cough . Another prevalidated and structured 6-point Ram-say Scale was used to evaluate postoperative sedation . In both groups， the hemodynamic parameters were measured and recorded. SPSS was used to examine the data that was entered into Microsoft Excel. In order to compare the mean values of var-ious parameters， the Student T-test was performed. The Fisher exact test was applied to compare the hemodynamic responses and negative outcomes between the groups. A p-value of less than 0.04 was regarded as a statistically significant outcome.

【12】Results

【13】In the dexmedetomidine group， the heart rate， SBP， DBP， and MAP were mainly kept within the normal range； however， in the NS alone group， there was an increase after the sixth minute of withdrawing the inhalational agent. Additionally， from the sixth minute of medication administration to 20 minutes after extubation， there is a statistically significant rise in these val-ues in the control group following extubation compared to the dexmedetomidine group.

【14】Compared to the Dexmedetomidine group， the NS alone group had a mean extubation quality score of 2.13 instead of1.23. In the test group， 65.46% were extubated without having a significant cough. Statistics show that the findings are signif-icant . The study group took longer to extubate and open their eyes than the controls. However， this difference was not statistically significant (2.42 vs 2.18， P>0.04). Compared to28.56% of those in the control group， the majority of people tak- ing dexmedetomidine (61.8%) were sleepy. Additionally， the outcomes had statistical significance (P=0.02). Compared to the control group (80%)， only 9.4% of the dexmedetomidine group experienced elevated blood pressure. 14.27% of the dexmedeto-midine group and 52.38% of the NS alone group reported having a cough. The control group did not experience hypotension， whereas 18% of the study population did. Compared to none in the control group， the study group had bradycardia in a propor-tion of about 9.4%. These outcomes were all statistically notewor-thy. Both groups exhibited low laryngospasm，bronchospasm， desaturation， or excessive sedation . 【16】Discussion

【17】Coughing and hemodynamic changes can occur after extubation. Coughing strain can result in surgical haemorrhage， bron-chospasm， tachycardia， hypertension， increased intracranial and intraocular pressure， and myocardial ischemia . Some respi-ratory problems， including as laryngospasm， airway blockage， and desaturation， may also be brought on by tracheal extubation. Most patients tolerate all of these changes and normally disappear quickly， but some patients may experience negative effects .

【18】Dexmedetomidine's hemodynamic response during extuba-tion， the effectiveness of extubation， the degree of postoperative sedation， the incidence of complications， hemodynamic stability， analgesic effects， and the absence of respiratory depression， as well as its relatively shorter half-life， were all evaluated in the current study. Dexmedetomidine inhibits central sympathetic outflow and noradrenaline turnover while activating medulla vasomotor centre receptors. This has led to the preservation of regular sympathetic activity， including blood pressure and Or heart rate. Furthermore， all hemodynamic indicators after extubation， including blood pressure， mean arterial pressure， and heart rate， were considerably more stable in the study group than in the control group.

【19】Our results align with recent studies that showed intravenous dexmedetomidine administration stabilises vascular hemody-namics， provides smooth extubation and provides a much easier and more comfortable recovery . Dexmedetomidine has sedative and anxiolytic properties that result from activat-ing the parasympathetic division from the locus coeruleus in the brainstem and suppressing sympathetic outflow. Sedation is brought on by activating the 2 A and 2 C receptors in the locus coeruleus. The spinal cord's activation of the 2 A and 2C receptors reduces the transmission of pain by reducing sub-stance P release. Reduced norepinephrine release from the locus coeruleus leads inhibitory neurons， such as those in the g-amino butyric acid pathway， to fire more frequently， leading to suffi-cient sedation and anxiolysis. Patients cooperate during proce-dures and respond to vocal orders under the influence of a 2agonist sedative . Dexmedetomidine-treated patients were slightly sleepy but responded to the Ramsay Sedation Scale 3after being extubated. Calculations revealed that the dexmedeto-midine group's latency between extubation and eye-opening was longer than that of the controls. Due to the factors mentioned above， the dexmedetomidine group also had a better extubation quality score. Identical results were seen in further investigations as well . Dexmedetomidine decreases heart rate by activating 2 adrenoceptors， imidazoline-preferring receptors， or both in the nucleus tractus solitarus (ventrolateral section of medulla) . According to the findings of our study， the dexmedetomidine group experienced considerably more hy-potension and bradycardia than the control group. Other studies also produced comparable outcomes . In research by Goel et al.， 12， the prevalence was equal in the two categories. In their study， Lawrence et al. 13 found that bradycardia only happened during the first and fifth minutes of extubation. As in prior research ， there was no discernible difference in the frequency of vomiting between the two groups. In our re-search， we were coughing and elevated. The blood pressure in the NS alone group and the bradycardia and hypotension in the Dexmedetomidine group were considerably higher. Fewer studies， however， have discovered comparable outcomes . Desaturation，bronchospasm， respiratory depression， coughing， laryngospasm， and excessive sedation were not observed in ei-ther of the two groups， according to a research by Guler et al. 15.

【20】Dexmedetomidine is intravenously administered right before extubation to reduce the hemodynamic reactions. It provides greater sedation and smoother tracheal extubation postopera-tively. In a small number of cases， dexmedetomidine-related hypotension and bradycardia are curable. Using the medication during extubation can help avoid potentially fatal consequences such as bronchospasm，laryngospasm， respiratory depression， and excessive sedation.

【0】Background：

【1】Priapism is rarely reported as a complication in patients with essential thrombocythemia at presentation. We could find very few such cases of essential thrombocythemia while searching the literature. A combined modality of treatment is used in the form of chemotherapy and procedures like repeated aspiration and instil-lation of phenylephrine to treat essential thrombocythemia presenting with recurrent priapism.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 31-year-old man presented to the Urology Department with priapism for the last 24 h. He had previously had multiple similar episodes in the last 20 days and 1 episode of prolonged penile erection 5 months ago. On ex-amination， his penis was erect， swollen， and painful. There was no organomegaly. The priapism was managed with repeated aspiration and instillation of phenylephrine. Routine investigations showed marked thrombocy-tosis. Subsequent investigations done in the Clinical Hematology Department revealed increased megakary-ocytes in bone marrow and presence of JAK2V617F mutation. After confirmation of diagnosis， cytoreductive therapy (hydroxyurea 500 mg twice a day) and acetyl salicylic acid 75 mg once a day was initiated. With this treatment， the platelet count normalized over a period of 2 months and no further episodes of priapism were noted； however， the patient developed erectile dysfunction.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Essential thrombocythemia can present with priapism as the first manifestation. Early suspicion， diagnosis，and management is needed to prevent erectile dysfunction. Erectile dysfunction is usually irreversible after long-standing priapism.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Erectile Dysfunction·Myeloproliferative Disorders· Priapism·Thrombocythemia， Essential Priapism is an unwanted prolonged penile erection without any sexual arousal. It has been reported in patients with var-ious non-malignant and malignant hematological disorders， including myeloproliferative neoplasms. Chronic myeloid leu-kemia (CML) is the most common myeloproliferative neoplasm(MPN) associated with priapism . It is rarely reported as a complication in patients with essential thrombocythemia. We could find only a few cases in the recent literature . A combined modality treatment is being used in the form of chemotherapy and procedures like repeated aspiration and in-stillation of phenylephrine to treat essential thrombocytosis presenting with recurrent priapism .

【7】Case Report

【8】A previously healthy 31-year-old man was admitted to the Urology Department with a history of penile erection that be-gan the previous day. His penis was erect， swollen， and pain-ful. There was no history of any drug intake， sexual activity， masturbation， use of alcohol， or any illicit drug use. The pa-tient gave a history of many similar previous episodes lasting for many hours with spontaneous recovery in the last 20 days. He also had a history of one such episode 5 months ago that was relieved by conservative management. He was referred to the Clinical Hematology Outpatient Department for evalu-ation of abnormal blood test results. The general examination was otherwise unremarkable； there were no pallor， lymphade-nopathy， or hepatosplenomegaly.

【9】Laboratory investigations showed hemoglobin 13 gm/dl， total leucocyte count 18.3x10/L， and platelet count 1424×10°/L. A peripheral blood smear examination revealed thrombocyto-sis with giant platelets . Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy showed increased numbers of megakaryocytes， with giant and bizarre megakaryocytes present in nests . JAK2V617F mutation was detected and BCR-ABL by RT-PCR was negative. Serum biochemical test results were unremarkable.

【10】This patient was managed conservatively by repeated aspira-tion of corpora cavernosa and instillation of phenylephrine in the Urology Department. With repeated aspiration and instil-lation of phenylephrine， the penis become flaccid. After the confirmation of diagnosis， the patient received hydroxyurea500 mg twice a day， and acety! salicylic acid 75 mg once a day was added when platelet count decreased below 1000×10°/L. Subsequent to treatment with hydroxyurea and acety! salicylic acid， no episode of priapism was noted. His platelet count de-creased to below 400x10/L at the end of 2 months. As a con-sequence of prolonged priapism， he developed erectile dysfunc-tion (ED)， which did not improve， even at 6-month follow-up.

【11】Discussion

【12】Priapism is a sustained penile erection in the absence of sex-ual activity. It is generally defined as an unwanted erection lasting more than 4 h . It can be high-flow or low-flow. High-flow priapism is due to increased blood influx into the cavernous bodies， usually due to an arteriocavernosal fistula. It is also called nonischemic， as cavernous blood gases are nei-ther hypoxic nor acidotic. Low-flow priapism has a veno-occlu-sive origin and is known as ischemic priapism because dimin-ished blood efflux from the cavernous bodies causes hypoxic and acidotic cavernous blood gases . Ninety percent of men with ischemic priapism lasting more than 24 h develop erec-tile dysfunction. Ischemia persisting for more than 24-48 h causes endothelial damage and trabecular destruction leading to irreversible fibrosis and calcification， resulting in ED .

【13】Priapism is a urological emergency. Hematological conditions may be associated with major episodes of priapism， as well as stuttering priapism (recurrent temporary episodes of pri-apism). Well-documented hematological conditions causing priapism are hemolytic disorders (e.g.， homozygous sickle cell disease)； myeloproliferative neoplasms (e.g.， chronic myeloid leukemia \[CML\] and polycythemia vera \[PV\])； acute leukemia(e.g.， acute myeloblastic leukemia \[AML\] and acute lympho-blastic leukemia \[ALL\] with high counts)； plasma cell disor-ders (e.g.， myeloma and amyloidosis)； and hypercoagulable states. Sickle cell disease is the most common hematological disorder， while CML is the most common leukemia associat-ed with priapism .

【14】The pathophysiology of priapism in hematological conditions in-cludes hyperleukocytosis leading to aggregates of leukemia cells in the corpora cavernosa in CML and acute leukemias，clogging numbers of large mature megakaryocytes in bone marrow， exclu-sion of CML， PV， and MDS， and presence of JAK-2， CALR， or MPL mutation. Other causes of thrombocytosis must be excluded， including other MPNs . Clinically， ET is characterized by epi-sodes of thrombosis and/or hemorrhage. In ET， priapism is a very rare complication and only a few cases are found in the literature. Table 1 shows the review of similar cases reported in the literature.

Conservative approaches like apheresis and chemotherapy (e.g.， steroids， hydroxyurea， and imatinib) can manage many patients， especially children . Aspiration of corpora cavernosa and instillation of phenyl ephrin can be tried in adults with severe and prolonged symptoms for rapid response and flaccidity of the penis. If these procedures also do not work， surgical correction (e.g.， cavernosa-corpus spon-giosum shunt) can be tried .

【18】Conclusions

【19】Clinicians should consider essential thrombocythemia in pa-tients presenting with recurrent priapism. It should be sus-pected early and investigated promptly. General measures， cytoreduction， and evacuation of the corpora cavernosa should be done early to avoid erectile dysfunction. Once the etiologi-cal diagnosis is confirmed， specific therapies targeting the un-derlying neoplasm can be started.

【0】ABSTRACT Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) is a form of recurrent depressive or bipolar disorder that is characterized by episodes of major depression that tend to recur during winter usually. Vitamin D is important for serotonin synthesis and low serotonin levels are thought to be associated with depression. During the winter， levels of vitamin D are lower， what might precipitate depression symptoms in individuals with SAD， but it might also be relevant for other depressive disorders， such as major depressive disorder or bipolar disorder. Patients with depression may benefit from vitamin D supplements， especially during the late autumn and winter when sunlight-induced vitamin D production is lower， and diet enriched with tryptophan. Vitamin D supplements may be beneficial in depressed patients with high inflammatory biomarkers because studies have shown that inflammation can produce depression in vulnerable individuals by lowering plasma tryptophan and diminishing brain serotonin activity. Vitamin D supplements may also improve the efficacy of SSRIs in these patients.

【1】Introduction

【2】Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) is a form of recurrent depres-sive or bipolar disorder， with episodes that vary in severity . Patients that suffer from SAD have episodes of major depres-sion that tend to recur during specific times of the year， usually winter . Studies of brain serotonin function support the hy pothesis of disturbed activity. The short-allele polyphorphism for serotonin transporter is more common in patients with SAD than in healthy people . About 5% of USA population expe-riences SAD， with symptoms present for about 40% of the year. Light therapy during the autumn and winter can be very useful， but should continue through the end of the winter season until spontaneous remission of symptoms in the spring or summer， in order to avoid relapse. Pharmacotherapy (antidepressants) and cognitive behavior therapy are also appropriate treatment options .

【3】The link between vitamin D， serotonin and depression

【4】Serotonin regulates a wide variety of brain functions and behav-iors. Brain serotonin is synthesized from tryptophan by trypto-phan hydroxylase 2， which is transcriptionally activated by vita-min D hormone . Vitamin D hormone (calcitriol) activates the transcription of the serotonin-synthesizing gene tryptophan hy-droxylase 2 (TPH2) in the brain at a vitamin D response element(VDRE) and represses the transcription of TPH1 in tissues out-side the blood-brain barrier at a distinct VDRE . Low vitamin D hormone levels during fetal and neonatal development could result in poor gene tryptophan hydroxylase 2 (TPH2) expression and subsequently reduced serotonin concentrations in the de veloping brain. The important role of TPH2-mediated serotonin production in shaping brain structure and neural wiring during early neurodevelopment is well known . This mechanism suggests that adequate vitamin D hormone levels during preg-nancy， as well as nutritional intake of tryptophan and vitamin D during early childhood， may have a critical influence on brain serotonin levels and thus， on the structure and neural wiring of the brain . Serotonin hypothesis proposes that diminished activity of serotonin pathways plays a causal role in the patho-physiology of depression . The best evidence that serotonin plays a role in the pathophysiology of depression comes from studies of "tryptophan depletion"， where an acute dietary ma-nipulation is employed to produce a transient lowering in brain serotonin activity through diminishing availability of its pre-cursor amino acid， tryptophan. In healthy participants with no risk factors for depression， tryptophan depletion does not pro-duce clinically significant changes in mood； however， recovered depressed patients free of medication can show brief， clinically relevant， depressive symptomatology . Inflammation can pro-duce depression in vulnerable individuals by lowering plasma tryptophan and diminishing brain serotonin activity. Such an effect could explain the diminished efficacy of SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) in depressed patients with high levels of inflammatory biomarkers . Calcitriol is a well-known endocrine regulator of calcium homeostasis. More recently， lo-cal calcitriol production by immune cells was shown to exert autocrine or paracrine immunomodulating effects. Immune cells that produce calcitriol also express the vitamin D receptor(VDR) and the enzymes needed to metabolize vitamin D3 (1&-，25-， and 24-hydroxylases). Studies of animal models and cell cultures showed both direct and indirect immunomodulating effects involving the T cells， B cells， and antigen-presenting cells(dendritic cells and macrophages)； and affecting both innate and adaptive immune responses. The overall effect is a switch from the Th1/Th17 response to the Th2/Treg profile. The im-munomodulating effects of vitamin D may explain the reported epidemiological associations between low vitamin D status and a large number of autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. Such associations have been suggested by observational studies not only in rheumatoid arthritis，lupus， inflammatory bowel disease， and type 1 diabetes； but also in infections， malignancies，trans-plant rejection， and cardiovascular disease. In animal models for these diseases， vitamin D supplementation has been found to produce therapeutic effects . Vitamin D supplements may improve the efficacy of SSRIs in the depressed patients with high levels of inflammatory biomarkers. Patients with autoim-mune and inflammatory diseases who suffer from depression may benefit from vitamin D supplementation as well. Vitamin D is thought to increase the level of brain serotonin and thus， opposes the effect of inflammation， which lowers tryptophan and consequently， serotonin levels， which means that optimal vitamin D status positively correlates with optimal serotonin levels.

【5】Light therapy

【6】Observations from clinical trials have frequently demonstrated that light therapy can be an effective therapy for seasonal and non-seasonal major depression. It is known that light therapy modulates mood states and cognitive functions， involving cir-cadian and non-circadian pathways from retinas into brain . SAD is prevalent when vitamin D stores are typically low. Broad-spectrum light therapy includes wavelengths between 280-320nm which allow the skin to produce vitamin D . Analysis of pooled data from randomized trials provides evidence for the ef-ficacy of use of bright light therapy ≥ 5，000 lux for periods ≥30minutes when used as augmentation to standard antidepressant pharmacotherapy in the treatment of major depressive disorder and bipolar depression without a seasonal pattern .

【7】1\. Sun light (spectrum 280-320 UVB) is important for vitamin D3 production. Clothing and sun protection creams， espe-cially with high sun protection factor (SPF) prevent vitamin D3 production in the skin. Vitamin D deficiency is iden-tified as a world global problem with approximately 14%of the population with inadequate vitamin D levels . During the winter， levels of vitamin D are lower and thus， may precipitate depression symptoms in individuals with major depressive disorder or bipolar disorder.

【8】2\. Broad-spectrum light therapy that includes wavelengths between 280 and 320 nm， which allow the skin to produce vitamin D， is shown to be useful in patients with SAD， but also in patients with major depressive disorder and bipolar depression without a seasonal pattern.

【9】3\. Low serotonin levels are thought to be associated with de-pression. Serotonin regulates a variety of cognitive func-tions： mood， decision-making， social behavior， excessive worry and impulse control. Vitamin D is important for serotonin synthesis. Brain serotonin is synthesized from tryptophan by tryptophan hydroxylase 2. Tryptophan hy-droxylase is transcriptionally activated by vitamin D hor-mone. Patients with depression may benefit from vitamin D supplements and diet enriched with tryptophan.

【10】4\. Some studies shown that inflammation can produce depres-sion in vulnerable individuals by lowering plasma tryp-tophan and diminishing brain serotonin activity. Such an effect could explain the diminished efficacy of SSRIs in de-pressed patients with high levels of inflammatory biomark-ers. SSRIs are considered as a first line treatment for major depressive disorder， as well as for seasonal depression. Pa-tients with autoimmune and inflammatory diseases may have poorer clinical outcome with SSRIs therapy. Vitamin D is known for its immunomodulatory effects and thus， vitamin D supplements may be beneficial in depressed pa-tients with high inflammatory biomarkers. Vitamin D sup plements may also improve the efficacy of SSRIs in these patients.

【11】To summarize， it would be rationale to measure levels of vita-min D of every patient that suffers from depression， and to treat vitamin D deficiency if present. Nutritional interventions are very important part of multi-modal therapy for all depressive disorders， which also includes light therapy， pharmacotherapy(antidepressant agents)， cognitive therapy， art therapy work therapy， and spiritual support (for religious individuals). Fur-ther pre-clinical and clinical investigation is mandatory in order to better understand the clinical significance of vitamin D status in the context of SAD and other depressive disorders.

【0】ABSTRACT Patients with CKD have an elevated likelihood of acquiring serious COVID-19. In comparison， the mortality rate tends to be higher than in the overall population and is not always specifically related to pulmonary compromise. This is not unexpected， considering that infectious or severe illnesses (e.g. influenza) are correlated with an elevated risk of cardiovascular problems in the overall population and individuals with CKD . In addition， CKD patients also have comorbidities with cardiovascular and diabetes that could be individually predisposed to extreme COVID-19.In the absence of a vaccine or licenced treatment， nephrologists should encourage CKD patients to follow guidelines for social exclusion targeted at high-risk patients. These should be applied to dialysis facilities， where a high suspicion index and COVID-19 monitoring should be added.

【1】KEYWORDS severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)， chronic kidney disease (CKD)， Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2(ACE2)， cytokine storm

【2】Introduction

【3】Situations had drastically altered since the first news of several instances of atypical pneumonia in China in December 2019 and the essential steps taken by the Chinese government to shut down the city of Wuhan (the subject of the issue). A novel coronavirus was identified as the causative agent of this res-piratory illness ， hit by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2(SARS-CoV-2)， and the disease was termed as coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) by the World Health Or-ganization . In 1966，Tyrell and Bynoe， who extracted viruses from patients with common colds， were first identified as coro-naviruses . They are enveloped， positive， single-stranded large RNA viruses that infect not just humans but also a wide variety of animals (bats， pangolins， cats， pigs and birds， among others). The size of the genome ranges between 26 and 32 kb. They were called coronaviruses， based on their morphology as spherical virions with a central shell and surface projections re-sembling a solar corona. Four subfamilies are known at present：a-，b-，c-and d-coronaviruses . SARS-CoV-2 is a member of the B b-coronavirus lineage and is closely related to SARS-CoV. Nucleocapsid protein (N)， spike protein (S)， small membrane protein (SM) and membrane glycoprotein (M) are coded by the key four structural genes， with specific membrane glycoprotein(HE) occurring in HCoV-OC43 and HKU1 b-coronaviruses . The clinical continuum of infection with COVID-19 is extremely complex， ranging from asymptomatic infection， anosmia，ageu-sia or mild upper respiratory tract disease to serious respiratory failure， pneumonia and even death . Diarrhoea， cutaneous and thrombotic symptoms have been identified recently . In elderly patients and those with chronic conditions such as cardiovascular disease， hypertension or diabetes， more serious cases have been identified with increased mortality. However， in previously stable young patients， deaths have also resulted. It is predicted that patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at a greater risk of serious illness since their all-type infec-tion incidence and coronary disease prevalence are higher than the overall population. In CKD patients， pronounced improve-ments in the immune system have been identified， resulting in an immunosuppressed condition and recurrent infectious complications. Similarly， in CKD patients， chronic systemic in-flammation can also lead to higher morbidity and mortality. The pathogenicity of COVID-19， the persistent immuno-logical changes found in patients with CKD， and the risk of COVID-19 and the clinical consequences for patients with CKD are addressed in this study.

【4】Molecules associated kidney dysfunction in SARS-CoV-2 Infection

【5】A dynamic mechanism that remains enigmatic is the viral bind-ing， fusion， and eventual replication of coronavirus in targeted host cells. Even so， one synergistic action of S1 protein binding to receptors on the cell surface and a sequence of proteolysis were discovered to be necessary when the virus was attached to the cell surface. Scientists have estimated that at least three pro-teins， including Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2(ACE2)，type II transmembrane serine proteases (TMPRSS2) and an enzyme called furin are indispensably necessary for this phase. Interest-ingly， these molecules have been shown to be present in kidney tissue， indicating that the target cells attacked by SARS-CoV-2may be kidney tissue .

【6】Role of ACE2 in disease pathogenicity

【7】ACE2 belongs to the dipeptidyl carboxypeptidase class of angiotensin-converting enzymes and is homologous to the hu-man angiotensin-1-converting enzyme. ACE2 has been found to be one of the main receptors mediating the entrance of SARS-CoV-2 into human cells. Research performed by Fan and col-leagues  has shown that the levels of ACE2 mRNA and ACE2protein are also higher in renal cells. The spread of ACE2 expres-sions shows that the possible pathway of infection and direct kidney injury may be caused by SARS-CoV-2 binding to ACE2. Another research by Lin and colleagues based on single-cell analysis  also showed that ACE2 was enriched in proximal tubular cells， suggesting that the kidney is more vulnerable to SARS-CoV-2 infection.

【8】Previous experiments have indicated that in a number of renal tissue cells， ACE2 occurs. In the apical boundary of the proximal tubular cells， expression of ACE2 was highly positive， whereas it was less present in the cytoplasm. Visceral glomeru-lar stains were mild in ACE2， and mesangium and glomerular endothelium were negatives . Caibin Fan et al. have recently searched for literature and analyzed online datasets showing that the level of ACE2 protein expression is significantly greater in the kidney， particularly in renal tubular cells . It can be hypothesised that SARS-CoV-2 can impact the kidney directly by proximal renal tubular injury.

【9】Furin-Like Cleavage Site

【10】Earlier studies have shown that an unusual 'RRAR motif'in SARS-CoV-2 is a furin recognition site capable of being activated by an enzyme named furin . One of the most important distinctions between SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 is the motif-containing of this cleavage site between proteins S1/S2 . Furin is one of the proprotein convertases that can precisely cleave viral envelope glycoproteins， thus enhancing viral fusion into the membranes of host cells. Furin had a high level of expression in the salivary， lachrymal， intestine， liver， and even kidney glands . To date， by increasing the furin-mediated cleavage site， SARS-CoV-2 could use this particular function to become more contagious in the kidney and enhance kidney injury.

【11】Transmembrane Protease Serine 2

【12】Via binding the spike (S) proteins to ACE2 and S protein priming by host cell proteases， SARS-CoV-2 achieves access to a cell. Research performed by Hoffmann and colleagues  has shown that the ACE2 receptor is a SARS-CoV-2 cell receptor and that TMPRSS2 is an S protein priming cell protease， and both ACE2and TMPRSS2 are the central points of human cell infection with SARS-CoV-2. Both ACE2 and TMPRSS2 receptors occur in the kidney J. Which means that the virus is capable of targeting the kidney in this way? A TMPRSS2 inhibitor may also be beneficial for antiviral therapy， including kidney defence.

【13】Direct Virus Infection in Renal Tissue

【14】In the tubular epithelium and podocytes， clusters of coronavirus particles with distinctive spikes were observable under electron microscopic examination. Single-cell RNA sequencing technol-ogy provided cellular evidence that through the ACE2-related pathway， SARS-Cov-2 invaded human kidney tissue through the proximal convoluted tubule， proximal tubule， proximal straight tubule and glomerular parietal cells and used its cellular pro-tease TMPRSS2 for priming . These results revealed clear signs of SARS-CoV-2 penetration into the tissue of the kidneys. Renal target cells targeted by SARS-CoV-2 were also confirmed to be proximal renal tubular cells， compatible with the distri-bution of ACE2 in renal tissue . An up-regulation of the expression of ACE2 on the surface of renal tubular cells was also found. It is illustrated in figure 1.

【15】COVID-19 nephropathy due to cytokine storm in pa-tients

【16】A significant factor contributing to multiple organ injury in COVID-19 patients is also the cytokine wind. Highlevels of pro-inflammatory cytokines can cause heart， liver， and kidney shock and tissue damage， as well as respiratory failure or multiple organ failure . IL1B，IL1RA，IL7，IL8，IL9，IL10， FGF， GCSF， GMCSF， IFNy，IP10，MCP1，MIP1A，MIP1B，PDGF，TNFa， and VEGF were higher for both ICU patients and non-ICU patients than for healthy adults . ICU patients have an even higher degree of IL2， IL7， IL10， GCSF，IP10，MCP1，MIP1A， and TNFa relative to non-ICU patients. In most patients with extreme COVID-19， serum pro-inflammatory cytokines， including IL-6and IL-1B，IL-2，IL-8， IL-17， G-CSF，GM-CSF， IP10， MCP1，MIP1-af (also classified as CCL3)， and TNF were substantially elevated. Moreover， it was observed that the C-reactive protein and D-dimer were abnormally large. In 23 percent of ICU patients， acute kidney injury occurred， while acute kidney injury rarely occurs in non-ICU patients . This suggested that cytokine storm could be associated with kidney injury， and further studies are needed to explore the relationship between inflammatory storm and kidney injury.

【17】In addition to the direct SARS-CoV-2 virulence and cytokine storm， other causes， such as systematic hypoxia， pathological coagulation， and suspected drug-related or hyperventilation-related rhabdomyolysis， are potentially due to acute kidney

【18】Immune dysfunction in COVID 19 associated CKD

【19】SARS-CoV research revealed that AKI was the product of par-ticular pathogenic factors， such as cytokine release syndrome， rather than successful viral replication in the kidney in SARS patients. Flow cytometry was used to research the im-mune phenotype and the role of peripheral blood mononuclear cells in COVID-19 patients， taking into account the analogy be-tween SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 J. Studies have shown that lymphopenia has been documented in patients infected with SARS-CoV-2， mainly due to a significant reduction in ab-solute T cell counts， especially cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CD8+)， augmented neutrophil counts and enhanced proinflammatory cytokine levels. High interleukin (IL)-2， IL-6，IL-10 and inter-feron (IFN)-y levels were found in specific. It has therefore been hypothesised that loss of T cells during viral infection may con-tribute to increased inflammatory responses . It is known that T cells are necessary during viral infection to dampen over-active innate immune responses . In line with this theory， it has been found that the serum levels of IL-2， IL-4， IL-10， tumour necrosis factor (TNF)-af and interferon (IFN)-y reach their peaks when the T cell count decreases . Another significant result is higher serum concentrations of IL-6 and lower IFN-y than mod-erate variants in COVID-19 patients with more serious clinical manifestations. This is primarily attributed to the decline in lym-phocytes of CD4+，CD8+ and NK . The family of cytokines that play a critical role in innate immunity against viruses and other microbial pathogens is interferons (IFN). Binding to the IFN receptor triggers a cascade of gene activation signals coding for proteins with antiviral， antiproliferative or immunomodu-latory properties. The association between the IFN-Y and IL-6/sIL-6R signals normally leads to the mobilisation and eventual clearance of neutrophils， thereby regulating acute in-flammation infection and resolution and affecting the switch between innate and adaptive immunity . In patients infected with SARS-CoV-2， an improved cytokine storm can be associated with a higher IL-6/IFN-y ratio . These findings indicate that AKI may have an inflammatory aetiology induced by a cytokine storm in both SARS patients and patients with COVID-19. The cytokine storm is associated with an inflammatory mechanism that travels through the systemic circulation， starting at a local location. The inflammatory process， particularly when tissue oedema causes an increase in extravascular pressures and a con-sequent decrease in tissue perfusion， may cause organ dysfunc-tion. Corrective repair procedures start shortly after the onset of infection， and they can fully restore tissue and organ function in certain instances. However， when local tissue systems are injured by an extreme inflammatory disorder， healing happens with fibrosis， which may cause irreversible organ dysfunction. The immune system may not destroy SARS-CoV-2 when a cytokine storm happens， but it does kill vast numbers of normal cells and injure organs . In support of the hypothesis that AKI could be the product of inflammatory damage in COVID-19patients， the cohort study found that the kidney CT scan showed decreased density， suggestive of inflammation and oedema . Serious lung infections also require extended ventilatory assis-tance， in addition to being commonly associated with cytokine surge. The occurrence of sepsis， classically characterised by pro-nounced hypotension that involves treatment with inotropic medications， is predisposed to this. In patients with COVID-19 or acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)， it is also possible that chronic inotropic-induced hypotension and vasoconstric-tion could be synonymous with glomerular filtrate decline and resulting in acute tubular necrosis . The theory of a multi-factorial aetiology of renal harm in COVID-19 is verified in the most recent research. Su et al.  showed pigmented casts with elevated levels of creatine phosphokinase， due to rhabdomyol-ysis， in an analysis carried out by examining autopsy kidney samples. In rhabdomyolysis， the huge release of myoglobin can cause kidney dysfunction due to muscle injury. In fact， myo-globin demonstrates its renal toxicity by various mechanisms：renal vasoconstriction associated with hypoperfusion-related hyperactivation of RASS and reduction of nitric oxide levels； de-velopment of intratubular casts； direct toxicity of renal tubular cells. Acute tubular necrosis occurs from these processes . Rhabdomyolysis is hypothetically multifactorial in COVID-19patients. In fact， tissue hypoxia due to hyperventilation or even to drug-induced damage can be secondary to the direct cytotoxic effect of SARS-CoV-2 on the muscle . Presumably， the patho-genesis of AKI could be implicated in COVID-19 patients that experience rhabdomyolysis. Numerous dependent mechanisms raise the risk of acute kidney injury in the COVID-19 setting are illustrated in figure 2.

【20】Thromboembolic events associated with disease pro-gression

【21】Recently， the high frequency of thromboembolic events in pa-tients with COVID-19 indicates that SARS-CoV-2 can play a significant role in coagulopathy induction. A condition of hy-percoagulability arose after examining the haematological pro-file of COVID-19 patients. In particular， high plasma levels of thrombocytopenia-associated reactive protein C， fibrinogen， D-dimer， and ferritin were observed in these patients . The formation of disseminated intravascular coagulation following SARS-CoV-2 infection has recently been verified by clinical and autopsy reports from China and the U.S. with evidence of mi-croangiopathy in multiple organs. In particular， the activation of COVID-19-associated macrophages， the cytokine storm and the damage-associated molecular proteins will induce the release of both tissue factors and the activation of hypercoagulability-predisposing coagulation factors. In some instances， the progres-sion of acute tubular necrosis into cortical necrosis and hence the development of permanent renal injury may be favoured by this state of hypercoagulability. These findings indicate that， in some supportive COVID-19 patients， low back pain and mi-crohematuria observed could be signs of renal infarction . The contribution of SARS-CoV-2 to CKD production could in-clude pathways close to those defined for acute kidney injury. Indeed， a non-trivial portion of patients has been found to de-velop symptoms of tubular or glomerular disruption during the infection. Due to the virus， direct tubule-glomerular cell damage frequently presents with proteinuria and hematuria， which could， in turn， initiate a chronic， non-reversible process. Proteinuria has been shown to have a direct toxic impact on renal tubular cells and， over time， induce renal fibrosis . In conclusion， the renal damage found in patients with COVID-19 is the product of complex pathways directly and indirectly caused by SARS-CoV-2 predisposing patients to renal dysfunc-tion. To better understand the pathophysiological pathways of kidney injury， to establish new clinical approaches capable of minimizing and/or preventing kidney damage and to improve the prognosis of patients with COVID-19， further studies are required.

【22】Clinical Features in Patients with Chronic Kidney Dis-ease (CKD)

【23】The increased risk of serious COVID-19 infection and mortality appears to be associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD). The correlation between markers of renal dysfunction and death in a cohort of 701 COVID-19 patients was examined by Cheng et al. They found that in 14.4% and 13.1% of patients， 43.9% of patients admitted had proteinuria， and 26.7% had hematuria.In14.4% and 13.1% of patients， serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) levels were increased. In 13.1 percent of patients， the average glomerular filtration rate was < 60 mL/min per

【24】1.73 m2 . In general， the authors found that the prevalence of proteinuria was correlated with 4 to 11 times the risk of in-hospital death relative to COVID-19 patients without kidney damage in the univariate study. At the same time， hematuria enhanced the risk of death by 12 times. These hazard ratios (HR) were higher than threat factors such as advanced age (HR： 2.43)， serious disease (HR： 6.10) and remained positively linked with mortality even after adaptation (thus multivariate analysis) by age， gender， the seriousness of the disease， lymphocyte count， comorbidity， indicating that kidney damage measures play a crucial role in assessing the prognosis of COVID-19 . In general， the authors found that the prevalence of proteinuria was correlated with 4 to 11 times the risk of in-hospital death relative to COVID-19 patients without kidney damage in the univariate study hematuria enhanced the risk of death by 12times. These hazard ratios (HR) were higher than threat factors such as advanced age (HR： 2.43)， serious disease (HR： 6.10) and remained positively linked with mortality even after adaptation(thus multivariate analysis) by age， gender， the seriousness of the disease，lymphocyte count， comorbidity， indicating that kidney damage measures play a crucial role in assessing the prognosis of COVID-19. A significant proportion of COVID-19 patients have recently been shown to suffer from other comorbidities， and the majority of these patients are also elderly and male . Among these comorbidities， an individual risk variable for poor prognosis is the involvement of chronic kidney disease.

【25】On the contrary， it is also true that nephropathic patients are mostly affected by hypertension and cardiovascular disease per se， which can contribute to a greater risk of complications with COVID-19 relative to the general public or patients without the renal disease . Patients with cardiovascular disease consid-ered a biomarker of an elevated risk of COVID 19 infection are also nephropathic patients . However， patients infected with other viruses such as the H1N1 flu virus and who developed kidney injury during infection were found to have an elevated chance of death， around 3-8 times， relative to those who did not. In addition， patients with elevated serum creatinine levels entering the hospital were overwhelmingly male and older (me-dian age 73 years). They were more critically ill than patients with normal serum creatinine (median age was 61 years).

【26】In comparison， patients with elevated baseline serum cre-atinine levels have improved leukocyte count with a rise in total leukocyte count and a reduction in the amount of lym-phocytes and platelets. Abnormalities of the coagulation path-way， including extended activated partial thromboplastin du-ration and higher D-dimer， are more common in patients with elevated creatinine baseline serum levels. The prevalence of procalcitonin-increased patients and the plasma levels of aspar-tate aminotransferase and LDH in patients with CKD are both higher relative to those with normal renal function. The fre-quency of in-hospital mortality was observed to be considerably higher in CKD patients than in those patients with typical base-line creatinine serum levels. 【29】To conclude， patients with CKD have an elevated likelihood of acquiring serious COVID-19. In comparison， the mortality rate tends to be higher than in the overall population and is not always specifically related to pulmonary compromise mag-nitude. This is not unexpected， considering that infectious or serious illnesses (e.g. influenza) are correlated with an elevated risk of cardiovascular problems in the overall population and individuals with CKD . In addition， CKD patients also have comorbidities with cardiovascular and diabetes that could be individually predisposed to extreme COVID-19. In the ab-sence of a vaccine or licenced treatment， nephrologists should encourage CKD patients to follow guidelines for social exclu-sion targeted at high-risk patients. These should be applied to dialysis facilities， where a high suspicion index and COVID-19 monitoring should be added. In addition， if the pandemic overwhelms health care services， nephrologists can struggle such that， considering the greater danger， CKD is not deemed comorbidity that weighs down the likelihood of the patient re-ceiving ICU care or a respirator. The effects of SARS-CoV-2on the kidney and the underlying kidney disease in patients are not well characterised. Preliminary evidence suggested that prior kidney failure may represent a risk factor for a more serious disease course， especially in elderly patients. SARS-CoV-2 in-fects the kidneys and can cause acute injuries to the kidneys. Although no particular treatment is currently available， several antiviral and/or anti-inflammatory medications are being stud-ied widely in randomised trials. In order to further understand disease pathology， acute kidney damage correlated with infec-tion， long-term renal effects， and alternative treatments， more research are required. In order to identify the potential risk and the appropriate therapeutic options for addressing COVID-19disease outcomes，rigorously controlled interventional trials and international registry reviews would be critical.

【0】Background： The aim of this case report is to present the results of treatment of end-stage ovarian carcinoma in a 41-year-old women using weight loss therapy Case Report： We describe the case of a female aged 41 years with epithelial invasive ovarian cancer of III-V stage， T N，M.

【1】Concurrent diseases were： abdominal carcinomatosis； hepatomegaly； ascites； condition after laparocentesis and skin-abdominal fistula； condition after 6 courses of neo-adjuvant polychemotherapy； hypertension II stage， risk factor of 3-4； dyslipidemia； and metabolic syndrome. A weight loss method based on a very-low-calorie diet and physical activity was used. Body weight was reduced from 74 kg to 53 due to loss of adipose tissue after 6months of therapy. At the same time， the percentages of water and muscle tissue were increased significantly. While overweight was reducing， clinical， laboratory， and instrumental results were improving. As a result ofthe weight loss therapy， about ≈100 mm-sized ovarian cancer was transformed into smaller-sized ovarian cysts.

【2】Conclusions：

【3】An analgesic effect was also achieved without use of narcotic or non-narcotic analgesics. These cyto-reversible processes were documented by laboratory and instrumental data.

【4】The mechanisms behind these differences remain to be elucidated. Future research with a larger study cohort and longer follow-up is needed to further investigate the role of caloric restriction diet in cancer cell changes in ovarian cancer.

【0】ABSTRACT Hypertrophic olivary degeneration(HOD) is a rare neurological condition resulting from the trans-neuronal damage of the dentato-rubral-olivary pathway. It is more commonly seen sec-ondary to ischemia，haemorrhage， tumour， trauma， infection， or any inflammatory condition， though few rare cases of idiopathic nature have been reported. MRI findings may be seen as early as four months after the initial insult， which may later be accompanied by classic symp-toms of palatal tremors， dentatorubral tremors， ocular myoclonus， or ataxia. Prior knowledge of this condition is required to prevent some misdirected interventions. We aim to discuss the relevant anatomy various patterns， and MRI findings and differential diagnosis of HOD through this case series.

【1】KEYWORDS olivary degeneration， dentatorubral tremors， Holmes tremor， MRI findings

【2】Introduction

【3】Hypertrophic olivary degeneration (HOD) is a rare trans-synaptic degeneration that occurs as a result of damage to the neuronal fibres of the dentato-rubral-olivary pathway (DRO) path-way. It is a circuit connecting the dentate nucleus in the cerebellum of one side to the red nucleus and the inferior olivary nucleus in the midbrain and medulla of the contralateral side， respectively. In 1931， French physicians Georges Guillain and Pierre Mollaret first found out the trilateral connection between these three nuclei， and it is also known as the triangle of Guillain-Mollaret. There are two such triangles in each posterior fossa- the superior end of which is formed by the red nucleus， the inferior end by the inferior olivary nucleus， and the middle end by the contralateral dentate nucleus.

【4】A set of afferent and efferent pathways connect these three nuclei， which are named accord-ing to the structure they con-nect： the dentato-rubral (afferent)， the rubro-olivary path way(afferent)， and the indirect olivo-cerebellar pathway (effer- ent). The dentato-rubral path-way originates in the contralateral dentate nucleus and connects to the ipsilateral red nucleus via the superior cerebellar peduncle. Continuing inferiorly through the midbrain and pons is the rubro-olivary pathway， located in the central tegmental and connects the ipsilateral red nucleus with the ipsilateral inferior olivary nucleus. Finally， indirect efferent fibres from the ipsilateral inferior olivary nucleus cross through the inferior cerebellar peduncle to join the contralateral dentate nucleus (olivary-dentate pathway)

【5】HOD is unique because the degeneration of the involved inferior olivary nucleus causes hy-pertrophy instead of atrophy. This can be explained by the fact that the dentate nucleus's pri-mary function is to inhibit the signals from the inferior olivary nucleus. Therefore， any lesion that causes an interruption in the DRO pathway's afferent route will no longer impede the signal and eventually undergo hypertrophy.

【6】This pathway is associated with fine voluntary movements， and hence disruption classically causes palatal tremors. Less frequently can cause dentatorubral tremor (Holmes tremor) or ocular myoclonus. In some cases， these tremors may also in-volve facial muscles， diaphragm， or muscles of the tongue and larynx. HOD commonly develops secondary to a focal le-sion like haemorrhage， infarction， tumours， infection， inflamma-tory conditions， trauma， or post-surgical. In rare cases，HOD has been documented to be idiopathic.

【7】Three patterns of HOD can be produced depending on the location of the lesions：

【8】1\. CONTRALATERAL HOD： lesions in the dentate nucleus or the dentato-rubral tract in the superior cerebellar peduncle.

【9】2\. BILATERAL HOD： lesions in the midline or paramedian pons due to simultaneous involvement of superior cerebel-lar peduncle and central tegmental tract.

【10】3\. IPSILATERAL HOD： lesion in the brainstem tegmentum disrupts the rubro-olivary pathway in the central tegmental tract.

【11】Interruption of the indirect efferent Olivo-dentate tract does not cause HOD.

【12】Typical MRI findings make the diagnosis of HOD of increased T2 and FLAIR intensity， which may later be accompanied by the enlargement of the inferior olivary nucleus. No diffu-sion restriction， blooming on T2\* and post-contrast enhancement is seen. The evolution of HOD has been described in four stages based on MRI findings.

【13】These MRI stages have been proven to coincide pathologically. Initial hyperintense signals correlate with demyelination and oedema. Olivary enlargement corresponds with the increase in the area of the cell body of astrocytes and vacuolar degeneration of the cytoplasm. How-ever no actual increase in the number of astrocytes has been documented. Later in the atrophic changes， a decrease in some neurons are seen.

【14】Case series

【15】Case 1：

【16】A 52year-old female with a history of stroke one year back came for a follow-up scan. She had no discomfort or any symptoms at the time of presentation. Physical examination was normal. MRI revealed multiple T2 hyperintense foci in the pons， right cerebellar peduncle and right cerebellar hemisphere showing signal drop on FLAIR representing chronic infarcts. On T2 and FLAIR imaging， there are abnormally enlarged and hyperin-tense bilateral inferior oli-vary nucleus showing no diffusion restriction or blooming on SWI.

【17】Case 2：

【18】A 55-year-old male with no significant past medical history presented to the emergency de-partment with a 4 days onset of giddiness and worsening coordination. An MRI was per-formed， and it revealed a T2 hyperintense lesion in the right medulla， which showed no diffu-sion restriction suggesting Hypertrophic Olivary Degeneration. A chronic infarct was noted in the right cerebellum. No lesion was noted， particularly in the Guillain-Mollaret triangle.

【19】Case 3：

【20】A 35-year-old male with a previous history of stroke now pre-sented to the emergency de-partment with a complaint of occa-sional palatal tremors for 15 days. No limb weakness or oph-thalmoplegia was seen on physical examination. MRI revealed multiple non-hemorrhagic infarcts in the central portion of the pons and bilateral cerebellar hemispheres in addition to bilateral almost symmetrical T2 high signal at the anterior olivary nuclei without restricted diffusion or blooming on T2\* representing bilateral hypertrophic olivary degeneration. Only this patient had palatal myoclonus in our case series and was managed conservatively with oral carbamazepine and was relieved of symptoms.
