【23】Post-Operative Course

【24】The patient was extubated to room air on post-operative day(POD) 1. Antibiotic prophylaxis was started for donor cultures positive for Candida glabrata and MRSA. Bronchoscopy on POD18 demonstrated mucosal edema in the left lobes and well-healing bronchial anastomoses with white exudate positive for Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Acinetobacter， which were ap- propriately treated. Other than a left pleural effusion requir-ing drainage and a mild AKl， her hospitalization was otherwise uncomplicated. She was discharged on POD 23.

【25】Notably， the patient had no thromboembolic or coagulopath-ic complications in the perioperative period. Immediate post-operative mean pulmonary artery pressure was 17， briefly reaching a maximum of 24 and a minimum of 11 before the Swan-Ganz catheter was removed on POD 2. She was placed on subcutaneous heparin 5000 U TID for venous thromboem-bolism prophylaxis. Of note， post-operative anti-lla levels dem-onstrated an argatroban level of 0 following transplant. The patient's coagulation profile  remained within normal limits except on the day of transplant， which is reflective of anticoagulation during surgery. Additionally， reagent-modified rotational thromboelastometry  values dur-ing this time period remained within normal limits， suggest-ing that the patient was not excessively anticoagulated. The patient's pulmonary function tests showed marked improve-ment following transplant .

【26】Discussion

【27】The safety of argatroban for organ procurement for transplan-tation has not been extensively evaluate for efficacy or safety. Herein， we report a case in which argatroban appears to have had little impact on the ultimate successful donor preserva-tion and lung transplantation. Throughout the perioperative period， the patient was neither under- nor over-anticoagulat-ed. The INR， PT， and PTT were elevated immediately post-op-eratively but returned to baseline normal by POD 1， without reversal or product administration.

【28】In our case， clotting time was within normal range and it is likely that minimal levels of argatroban， if any， were left in the graft at the time of transplantation， which is consistent with the fact that approximately 10 half-lives occurred between the time of argatroban administration and implantation， as well as the additional Perfadex/heparin flushes on the back-table. Argatroban use in this setting did not affect the recip-ient's ability to form clots based on biochemical and coagu-lation studies， nor did it lead to greater than expected blood loss at the time of surgery.

【29】There is only 1 other case report on the use of argatroban in multiorgan procurement， and it discusses the transfer of co-agulopathy to a graft recipient in the setting of excess do-nor anticoagulation . However， this does not preclude arg-atroban use， but rather enforces the need for careful dosing. Argatroban is initiated at 1 mcg/kg/min in patients without hepatic impairment and adjusted to 0.5 mcg/kg/min in pa-tients with hepatic impairment per our hospital protocol. When used in appropriate doses， argatroban can be used in multior-gan procurement while avoiding unwanted immunological re-actions in HIT-positive recipients.

【30】The effect of argatroban might be more profound if argatro-ban were required in the preparatory phase in addition to the procurement phase. The use of argatroban in back-table flush solutions could leave an organ with a higher concentra-tion of the drug than only systemic administration， as in our case. However， the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) did note that there were no graft dysfunctions reported in the post-operative period for any of the other organ recipients， including the HIT-positive liver recipient. Hence， it is unlike-ly that the additional backflush we used affected the safety， but further data will need to be gathered to ensure that this is indeed safe.

【31】Conclusions

【32】Our patient did well post-operatively with few complications and no clearly identifiable complications due to argatroban. While heparin will likely remain the standard of care for an-ticoagulation in transplantation， the ultimate success of the grafts suggests the use of argatroban in multiorgan procure-ment in the setting of a HIT-positive recipient is safe and ef-fective. In recipients who are HIT-positive， safe and effective use of argatroban enables them to receive organs when tra-ditional protocols would otherwise prohibit this.

【0】Background：

【1】Subacute thyroiditis， myocarditis， and hepatitis are inflammatory disorders that may develop after viral infec-tions， including SARS-CoV-2. These entities may appear after resolution of the respiratory syndrome.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A previously healthy 64-year-old male patient came to the hospital reporting severe chest pain. He had a history of a COVID-19 pneumonia with PCR confirmation 4 weeks before. On admission to the Coronary Care Unit (CCU)， the patient had a negative PCR for SARS-CoV-2； the following tests were performed： total T3 643.4 ng/dl {refer-ence 35-193 ng/dl)， total thyroxine 12.0 ug/dl (reference 4.8-11.7 ug/dl)， free T4 1.85 ng/dl (reference 0.7-1.48ng/d)， TSH 0.01 plU/ml (reference 0.35-4.94 plU/ml)； total bilirubin 0.76 mg/dl (reference 0.0-1.5 mg/dl)， al-kaline phosphatase 185 U/L (reference 40-150 U/L)， alanine aminotransferase 194.6 U/L (reference 6-66 U/L)， aspartate aminotransferase 93.4 U/L (reference 9-55 U/L)； on admission to the CCU high-sensitivity troponin548.3 pg/ml (reference 0.0-34.2 pg/ml)， after 24 h in the CCU 801 pg/ml， and after 11 days (as an outpatient)4.5 pg/ml. A thyroid gammagram revealed absent uptake of the radionuclide. Normal cardiac gammagraphy and cardiac enzymes ruled out myocardial ischemia and infarction. The following diagnoses were made： myo-carditis， subacute thyroiditis， and reactive hepatitis due to SARS-CoV-2 infection.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】COVID-19 has been demonstrated to be a multisystemic inflammatory disorder. The serious illness that devel-oped in our patient after relief of his pulmonary disease underlines this nature. We suggest close follow-up of patients even after apparent clinical resolution， and performing thyroid， myocardial， and liver tests if clinically indicated.

【6】Keywords：

【7】COVID-19·Hepatitis· Myocarditis · Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2·Thyroiditis， Subacute Subacute thyroiditis (SAT) is a self-limited inflammatory dis order of the thyroid gland， more common in females； it devel-ops after a viral infection， such as adenovirus，coxsackievirus， influenza， herpes virus (Epstein-Barr and cytomegalovirus)， measles， parvovirus B19， and rubella， among others . SAT is characterized by 3 stages： 1) thyrotoxicosis， lasting typically2-3 weeks； 2) transient hypothyroidism (may be permanent)；3) recovery period， when the patient becomes euthyroid (usu-ally after 4-6 weeks) . Myocarditis is more common in men， and it has a wide range of clinical presentations， which include fatigue， chest pain， palpitations， cardiogenic shock， and even sudden cardiac arrest； it is also known for a viral prodrome with non-specific symptoms . Liver injury is the most fre-quent complication of SARS-CoV-2 infection outside the re-spiratory system. The most common hepatic injury is acute hepatitis， which can be diagnosed by high levels of aspar-tate aminotransferase (AST)， alanine aminotransferase (ALT)， and total bilirubin. Other types of liver injury include steato-sis， portal inflammation， granulomas， thrombotic bodies，and biliary pathology .

【8】Case Report

【9】We report the case of a previously healthy 64-year-old man， a resident of Mexico City， who arrived at the hospital report-ing he had oppressive chest pain. His illness apparently be-gan 1 month before， when he attended a dinner party with a group of family and friends， of which 12 out of 15 people at-tending were later diagnosed with COVID-19. Four days after the party， our patient developed high fever， productive cough， headache， and extreme fatigue. A PCR for SARS-CoV-2 virus was performed； it came back positive for viral genes N， E，and RdRp. Consequently， a chest computed tomography (CT) scan was performed， which revealed a multifocal pneumonia with ground-glass opacities compatible with a SARS-CoV-2 infec-tion. Our patient was treated with oral steroids， azithromy-cin， and acetaminophen， with a full recovery after 2 weeks of treatment. Three weeks after the first positive PCR test for COVID-19， he developed severe oppressive chest pain， which persisted after taking analgesic drugs； for this reason， he was admitted to the hospital.

【10】On admission to the CCU his vital signs were as follows： blood pressure 140/80 mmHg， heart rate (HR) 120 beats per minute(bpm)， temperature 36.8°C A physical examination revealed a slight distal tremor with evident generalized diaphoresis with-out any other abnormalities； the thyroid gland could not be pal-pated. Table 1 summarizes all blood tests， obtained results， and their respective reference values. Thyroid ultrasound showed a diffusely enlarged micronodular thyroid gland ， thyroid gammagram-single photon emission tomography (SPECT)：ab-sent radionuclide uptake (Tc99m/Pertechnetate)； EKG on arriv-al to the emergency room showed sinus tachycardia， HR 120bpm； no ST-T wave abnormalities were observed nor any other abnormalities. On transthoracic echocardiogram， left ventricle cavity size and wall motion and thickness were normal， with ejection fraction 56%； 24-h Holter monitoring (taking ateno-lol 50 mg twice daily) showed an average HR of 76 bpm with no significant arrhythmias. On SPECT imaging of myocardial perfusion and function， no evidence of ischemia or infarction was found； systolic function was normal.

【11】After these examinations and analyses， the following diagno-ses were made： myocarditis， subacute thyroiditis， and reactive hepatitis after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Patient was treated with beta-blocking agents (atenolol 50 mg twice daily) and predni-sone 50 mg with gradual dosage tapering over the course of 2weeks. Three days after admission， the patient was discharged with full clinical relief. On his last outpatient visit to the en-docrine clinic， he had discontinued steroids. His thyroid tests revealed a slight primary hypothyroidism， which was treated with 100 ng of levothyroxine. The patient is currently asymp-tomatic and without any other sequelae.

【12】Discussion

【13】Since the beginning of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic in December2019， the pathophysiology of this disease has been demon-strated to evolve to a systemic hyperinflammatory state which can involve almost any organ. Tissues expressing angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE-2) protein appear to be more sus-ceptible， including the lungs， heart， and liver. Thyroid follicu-lar tissue also expresses ACE-2 and is therefore susceptible to SARS-CoV-2 inflammatory destruction .SARS-CoV-2uses a Spike protein to attach itself to ACE-2. More recently， ACE-2 mRNA was also detected in thyroid tissue . The first case of COVID-19-related subacute thyroiditis was reported in April 2020 in Italy . The authors described a noticeable elevation of inflammatory markers such as C-reactive protein(CRP)， as well as an increase in T4 and T3， accompanied with low levels of TSH and a thyroid ultrasound with bilateral dif-fuse hypoechoic and variable vascularity. Several COVID-19-related SAT cases have been reported since from all over the world .

【14】In this case， clinical and imaging features were compatible with SAT. Simultaneously， the patient developed myocarditis with-out evidence of ischemia， and reactive hepatitis. Myocarditis was responsible for the patient’s chest pain； both ischemic heart disease and pericarditis were ruled out by diagnostic tests indicating normal myocardial perfusion and no echocar-diogram alterations suggestive of pericarditis. Even throughout the patient's hospital stay， 2 echocardiograms indicated nor-mal diastolic function. In light of the patient's tachycardia on admission， after making sure the patient had no contraindica-tions with normal echocardiogram， beta-blocking agents were administered. Once acute myocarditis was suspected， cardi-ac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was not performed in view of satisfactory clinical resolution of chest pain 24 h af-ter admission， normal echocardiogram， and 24-h Holter mon-itoring with no rhythm alterations， with appropriate clinical response to the beta-blocking agent. At our institution， thy-roid function tests are recommended for all seriously ill pa-tients with tachycardia with no apparent cause. Severe chest pain dominated the clinical picture. The patient was examined in supine position at the CCU， which could have made palpa-tion of the thyroid gland difficult. Moreover， we believe the neck pain could have been masked by the severe chest pain our patient was suffering.

【16】Ashar et al described the following manifestations in patients with COVID-19 and myocarditis： fever， cough， myalgia， fatigue， expectoration， and dyspnea . Myocarditis may be identi-fied with a cardiac MRI showing myocardial edema， elevated inflammatory markers (IL-6， CRP， and procalcitonin)， and el-evated levels of serum high-sensitivity troponin1 . Several COVID-19-related myocarditis cases have been reported from all over the world， which have been treated with corticoste-roids and IL-6 inhibitors . As for liver complications， al-though the pathophysiology underlying liver damage is not yet clear， ACE-2 is also expressed in liver cells and the bile duct. Liver injuries associated with COVID-19 have been transient and reversible， with no need for special treatment. Several COVID-19 related hepatitis cases have been reported from all over the world as well .

【17】Aemaz Ur Rehman et al recently described demographics，clin-ical features， imaging， and laboratory findings in COVID-19related subacute thyroiditis case reports， all compiled in a Sys-tematic review . The median age reported was 40.0±11.3years， ranging from 18 to 69 years； over three-quarters of cas-es were female patients， with only 6 case reports being male. Out of 21 patients， 17 presented fever and neck pain； thyroid function tests most commonly had low TSH and high T3 or T4， or both， with 100% of case reports having ultrasound chang-es suggesting subacute thyroiditis .

【18】The age range， thyroid function tests， and image findings in our case matched those reported in the systematic review . Although the literature reports subacute thyroiditis is more common among women ， it is not exclusively a disease of women， as evidenced by our case and supported by 6 oth-er case reports of male patient . In addition， even though fever and neck pain are the most common clinical features of SAT， 4 out of 21 cases aside from ours did not present fever or neck pain either . In 3 cases， the presenting symptom was tachycardia， while fatigue and palpitations were among the most commonly reported symptoms in other case reports . Based on these findings， we believe that our patient's clinical features help to illustrate the clinical variability of SARS-CoV-2-related subacute thyroiditis.

【19】SAT， myocarditis， and hepatitis were clinically evident once re-spiratory manifestations were resolved and PCR tests for SARS-CoV-2 were negative. Although thyroid function tests， high-sensitivity troponin l， and liver function tests are not always necessary in patients with COVID-19，these potential compli-cations have to be kept in mind as they may aggravate the clinical course， even in apparently resolved cases when SARS-CoV-2 infection is no longer ongoing . To the best of our knowledge， only a single case of subacute thyroiditis has been previously reported in Mexico ， while most reported cases have been described in Italy and Iran . Therefore， we agree with Aemaz Ur Rehman et al's emphasis on assessing SAT in patients with a history of SARS-CoV-2 infection ， since it is possible that SAT cases are being overlooked.

【20】A short course of treatment with steroids promptly relieved our patient's clinical manifestations and allowed rapid dis-charge from the hospital. Other COVID-19-related subacute thyroiditis cases have also had satisfactory clinical outcomes when treated with steroids and anti-inflammatory drugs . Since myocarditis and hepatitis are also inflammatory disor-ders， they usually respond simultaneously to anti-inflamma-tory and supportive measures .

【21】Conclusions

【22】Subacute thyroiditis， myocarditis， and hepatitis must be con-sidered as 3 easily overlooked and serious potential compli-cations in patients with severe COVID-19. Subacute thyroid-itis must be suspected in patients with COVID-19 history who present clinical features of hyperthyroidism， such as tachycar-dia， tremor， or diaphoresis， with no apparent cause. The diag nosis is easily confirmed by absent radionuclide uptake in thy-roid gammagram and ultrasound features including a diffusely enlarged gland. Although neck pain is typical in SAT， SARS-CoV-2-induced SAT does not always present itself with neck pain， as shown in this case， among others. Measurement of serum high-sensitivity troponin I is helpful to identify involvement of the myocardium， and elevated aminotransferases suggest liv-er injury， such as hepatitis. Treatment with a short course of steroids may be considered in many of these cases.

【0】Background：

【1】Currently， it is normal to screen for Strongyloides as part of the workup in pre-transplant patients who have eosinophilia. Given the high mortality rates in Strongyloides hyperinfection， this article illustrates the need to screen all patients with eosinophilia who will be started on immunosuppression.

【2】Case Report： We present here an interesting case of a 76-year-old man with membranous glomerulopathy who developed a severe Strongyloides hyperinfection that required an ICU stay and ultimately led to his death a few weeks af-ter initiation of cyclophosphamide and steroids.

【3】Conclusions： We recommend that a detailed workup to detect or rule out this parasitic infection be conducted prior to the initiation of immunosuppression in any patient with eosinophilia.

【4】MeSH Keywords： Cyclophosphamide· Eosinophilia· Immunosuppression·Strongyloides Manifestations of Strongyloides stercoralis infection in an im-munocompromised host can range from asymptomatic eosin-ophilia to a life-threatening hyperinfection syndrome that in cludes cutaneous， gastrointestinal， and pulmonary symptoms. Therefore， Strongyloides hyperinfection should be suspected in any immunosuppressed patient with unexplained Gl symp-toms who has been exposed to the parasite or who has un-explained eosinophilia . We present here a case report of S. stercoralis hyperinfection in a 76-year-old man with mem-branous glomerulopathy， who was receiving immunosuppres-sion in the form of corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide

【5】Case Report

【6】A 76-year-male patient from Guyana with membranous glo-merulopathy secondary to chronic NSAID use came to the Emergency Department with diarrhea， diffuse abdominal pain， and tenesmus that had started 6 weeks after the initiation of oral cyclophosphamide mg oral tablet twice a day\] and prednisone mg oral tablet daily\]. He was diagnosed with membranous glomerulopathy 2 months prior to admission， proven by renal biopsy. Baseline creatinine was 1.14. Upon admission， his laboratory workup was as indicated in Table 1.

【7】The patient had visited Guyana 10 years previously， but had no other significant travel history. He was admitted with the impression of gastroenteritis/colitis and intravenous hydra-tion and antibiotics (ciprofloxacin and metronidazole) were administered. The suspicion of bacterial gastroenteritis was also entertained， as he was on immunosuppressive therapy. Stool cultures were taken on admission， and were negative.

【8】Gastroenterology was consulted because of a drop in hemo-globin， but the patient went into hypercapnic respiratory fail-ure and required bilevel positive airway pressure \[BiPAP\] be-fore endoscopy/colonoscopy could be performed. A CT chest scan was performed， which showed small bilateral pleural ef-fusions， micronodules， ground glass opacities， and consolida-tions in both lungs. BiPAP improved the gas exchange but the patient's condition continued to deteriorate during his hospi-tal stay， with persistent diarrhea and severe renal failure that eventually required hemodialysis. ELISA testing for HIV and hepatitis B and C panel was negative. HTLV testing was not performed. Strongyloides stercoralis larvae were seen on ex-amination of the stool for ova and parasites. An infectious dis-ease team was consulted， the determination of Stronqyloides hyperinfection syndrome was made， and the patient was started on lvermectin. The patient's respiratoy status began to deteriorate， with desaturation even on BiPAP， and he final-ly required intubation. Antibiotic coverage was broadened to include Vancomycin， Imipenem， and Gentamicin. The patient did not improve and died a few days later with the diagno-sis of Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome complicated by bacterial septicemia. Later， on review of the patient's labo-ratory data， it was found that he had persistent eosinophilia\[WBC 13 with 20% eosinophils\] even prior to the beginning of Cyclophosphamide/steroids. The eosinophilia was attributed to chronic NSAID use \[ibuprofen and naproxen\] and no inves-tigation had been conducted to assess any potential parasitic infestation before initiating immunosuppression.

【9】Discussion

【10】Strongyloides is unique among the commonly occurring hel-minths， as it can complete its life cycle within the human host， thereby allowing it to persist and replicate indefinitely. In the life cycle of other helminths， such as hookworms and round-worms， 1 larva gives rise to only 1 adult worm. Strongyloides infection， in contrast， can lead to autoinfection in which rhab-ditiform larvae can re-penetrate the gastrointestinal mucosa or the perianal skin . Hyperinfection syndrome exacer-bates the gastrointestinal and pulmonary symptoms and in-creased numbers of larvae may be detected in stool and/or sputum . This commonly establishes a latency that results in asymptomatic， chronic autoinfection of the gut， where it can remain undetected for years (the longest latency recorded is approximately 65 years) . The autoinfection， which is reac-tivated during immunosuppression， can result in a life-threat-ening Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome that is charac-terized by increased numbers of filariform larvae in the stool and sputum. Clinical manifestations of the increased para-site burden and migration are gastrointestinal bleeding and respiratory distress with high mortality rates (up to 87%). Inherently， patients with the nephrotic syndrome in membra-nous glomerulopathy are susceptible to infection  due to the impairment of normal defense mechanisms. Several hy-potheses for this susceptibility have been advanced，includ-ing urinary loss of protein  leading to decreased immune globulin G， immunologic defect ， decreased serum fac-tor B ， or lymphocytotoxins associated with certain re-nal diseases . Inhibition of Th2 cell-mediated， humoral， or mucosal immunity with corticosteroid use is the most fre-quent risk factor for hyperinfection syndrome . There is no definitive criterion standard for diagnosing Strongyloides ster-coralis infection. Stool examination is the primary technique used for the detection of strongyloides larva， with a sensitiv-ity of 50% if 3 consecutive daily samples are examined，and sensitivity reaching 100% if 7 consecutive daily stool speci-mens are examined in a specialized laboratory . Serological testing for Strongyloides， like ELISA IgG antibody tests， has an approximate sensitivity of 90% for patients from non-en-demic areas， but has potential false-positive results .Agar plate culture method is a newer method， with infection de-tection rates 2-3 times higher than those estimated by the other methods

【13】Conclusions

【14】Most of the deaths from helminthic infections in United States result from S. stercoralis hyperinfection . Although pre-transplant patients are evaluated routinely for infection，thor-ough assessment for parasitic infections is not conducted in non-transplant patients. Even though it is endemic primarily to tropical and subtropical regions， it is still prevalent in the Unites States due to its long latency periods and the large im-migrant population. Given the high mortality rates  of hy-perinfection syndrome， as well as the preventable nature of the condition， it is vital that a detailed workup for this para-sitic infection is conducted before initiating immunosuppres-sion in any patient with eosinophilia.

【0】Background：

【1】Severe hyperthyroidism， including thyroid storm， can be precipitated by acute events， such as surgery， trauma， infection， medications， parturition， and noncompliance or stoppage of antithyroid drugs. Thyroid storm is one of the serious endocrinal emergencies that prompts early diagnosis and treatment. Early occurrence of multi-organ failure is an ominous sign that requires aggressive treatment， including the initiation of extracorpore-al membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support as a bridge to stability and definitive surgical treatment. Most ad-verse events occur after failure of medical therapy

【2】Case Reports：

【3】We described 4 cases of fulminating thyroid storm that were complicated with multiple organ failure and cardi-ac arrest. The patients， 3 female and 1 male， were between 39 and 46 years old. All patients underwent ECMO support， with planned thyroidectomy. Three survived to discharge and 1 died after prolonged cardiac arrest and sepsis. All patients underwent peripheral， percutaneous， intensivist-led cannulation for VA-ECMO with no complications.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Early recognition of thyroid storm， identification of the cause， and proper treatment and support in the intensive care unit is essential. Patients with thyroid storm and cardiovascular collapse， who failed to improve with con-ventional supportive measures， had the worst prognosis， and ECMO support should be considered as a bridge until the effective therapy takes effect. Our case series showed that， in patients with life-threatening thyroid storm， VA-ECMO can be used as bridge to stabilization， definitive surgical intervention， and postoperative en-docrine management. Interprofessional team management is essential， and early implantation of VA-ECMO is likely beneficial in patients with thyroid storm after failure of conventional management.

【6】Keywords： Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation· Heart · Hyperthyroxinemia·Multiple Organ Failure Thyroid storm is a life-threatening form of severe hyperthy roidism characterized by acute generalized manifestations . National surveys from the United States and Japan reported that the incidence of thyroid storm ranges from 0.20 to 0.76cases per 100000 persons per year， with higher incidence in hospitalized patients (4.8 to 5.6 per 100 000) . Severe hy-perthyroidism can be precipitated by acute events， including surgery， trauma， infection， an acute iodine load (ie，amioda-rone administration)， parturition， and noncompliance or stop-page of antithyroid drugs . The evolution from simple thyrotoxicosis to the crisis of thyroid storm usually necessi-tates an overlaid insult . The diagnosis of thyroid storm de-pends on the presence of serious， and sometimes devastating， presentations including fever， cardiovascular collapse，altered mentation， elevated free T4 and/or T3， and suppressed thy-roid stimulating hormone (TSH) . The precise reason why some patients develop thyroid storm rather than uncomplicat-ed thyrotoxicosis is not fully understood； however， some theo-ries suggest a rapid increase in serum thyroid hormone levels， increased responsiveness to catecholamines， or enhanced cel-lular responses to thyroid hormone . Burch and Wartofsky introduced a scoring system that uses precise clinical criteria to identify thyroid storm. However， this scoring system is like-ly sensitive but not specific . The diagnostic criteria for thy-roid storm include thermoregulatory dysfunction (score 5-30)， central nervous system effects (score 10-30)， gastrointestinal-hepatic dysfunction (score between 10-20)， cardiovascular dys-function (score 5-25 for tachycardia， 10 for atrial fibrillation， and 5-15 for heart failure)， and presence of precipitant histo-ry (0 vs 10). A score of 45 or more is highly suggestive of thy roid storm； a score of 25 to 44 supports the diagnosis .

【7】The principles of therapeutic options typically consist of a cou-ple of medications， each of which has a different mechanism of action. The treatment options are based upon clinical expe-rience and case studies， since there are no prospective studies. The treatment is extrapolated from those used for uncompli-cated hyperthyroidism， with additional drugs such as glucocor-ticoids， iodine solution， and high doses of antithyroid drugs. In addition to specific therapy to inhibit the release and re-duce the synthesis of thyroid hormones， supportive therapy in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) and treating the precipitating factors are essential； however， the mortality rate of thyroid storm is high (10%-30%).

【8】In thyroid storm with hemodynamic instability and cardiogen-ic shock， antithyroid medications can be contraindicated due to multiorgan failure， especially in case of liver involvement. Also， the administration of beta blockers to patients with thy-roid storm can lead to hemodynamic instability and even car-diac arrest . In case of a refractory circulatory collapse， veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support can be used to achieve hemodynamic stability until normalization of the thyroid hormone， and improvement of the signs and symptoms are achieved. In fulminant multiorgan fail-ure (MOF)，therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) can be used as a bridging therapy for reducing the circulating excessive hor-mones and stabilization of patients in preparation for urgent thyroidectomy . The challenges of commencing plasma ex-changes with ongoing ECMO support， dialysis， and timing of thyroidectomy are still to be explored . TPE has shown an additive effect to the continuous renal replacement thera-py (CRRT) in removing the excess thyroid hormones4. Furthermore， the use of 3 extra-corporeal systems together(TPE， CRRT， and VA-ECMO) was reported in a few case reports for thyroid storm management .

【9】Here， we describe 4 cases of life-threatening thyroid storm complicated with circulatory collapse and multiorgan failure and requiring VA-ECMO support， renal replacement therapy， and TPE， with planned urgent thyroidectomy.

【10】Case Reports

【11】Case 1

【12】A 39-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department(ED) with symptoms suggestive of thyroid storm. The patient scored 55 points using the Burch Wartofsky Point Scale for thyroid storm diagnosis. She had atrial fibrillation ， poor left ventricular function， pleural effusion， and ascites. She was not known to have comorbidities. The patient was initial-ly treated with intravenous (i.v.) metoprolol and synchronized cardioversion. Despite these interventions， the patient devel-oped bradycardia followed by cardiac arrest. The patient’s car-diovascular instability and the need for maximum vasopres-sors prompted the decision to initiate ECMO support. After her admission to the ICU， the patient's blood tests confirmed the diagnosis of thyroid storm， with MOF and disseminated in-travascular coagulopathy.Medica. treatment with antithyroid medication was not possible because of MOF， and therefore plasmapheresis was started as a bridging to thyroidectomy. Plasmapheresis helped to optimize her condition so that she could undergo thyroidectomy . Following thyroidecto-my， the patient’s general condition and left ventricular function improved. The patient's TSH increased to 0.74 mlU/L and free T4 decreased to 36.1 pmol/L. She was transferred to the med-ical ward and then was discharged home in a stable condition.

【13】Case 2

【14】A 42-year-old woman presented to the ED with symptoms consistent with thyroid storm. She claimed only a history of a

【15】“thyroid problem” but was not taking any treatment for it. On examination， she was ill with jaundice and cold，clammy skin. Her ECG showed atrial flutter. Briefly after beta blocker admin-istration， she went into cardiac arrest， with pulseless electri-cal activity. She was resuscitated， intubated， and started on vasopressors. Point-of-care ultrasound demonstrated signifi-cantly dilated heart chambers， with markedly reduced ejection fraction and bilateral pleural effusion. The patient's laborato-ry findings were suggestive of thyroid storm， MOF， and dis-seminated intravascular coagulopathy. Her TSH was less than0.01 mlU/L， free T4 was 38.9 pmol/L， and her thyroid perox-idase antibodies were also found to be markedly elevated. Using the Burch Wartofsky Point Scale， the patient scored 70points. The ECMO team was consulted， as she was in cardio-genic shock. Uneventful peripheral percutaneous cannulation and initiation of VA-ECMO allowed for improvement of car-diovascular parameters. On day 2， she was started on CRRT， specifically continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration. A sec-ond plasmapheresis session was conducted on day 3， and a third session on day 4 in the ICU. An uitrasound examination of the thyroid gland demonstrated a diffusely heterogenous thyroid with increased vascularity， suggestive of thyroiditis. Furthermore， a thyroid scan with radioactive iodine uptake was suggestive of Graves’ disease. By day 5 in the ICU， inter-val improvements were noted after the intermittent plasma-pheresis treatments and CRRT.

【16】On day 7， she underwent a total thyroidectomy. The patient underwent decannulation of the VA-ECMO， as her cardiac func-tion significantly improved， with an ejection fraction of 45%. Additionally， her liver enzymes were trending downward. Five days after thyroidectomy， the free T4 returned within the nor-mal range， and she was extubated 2 days later. She was trans-ferred to the medical ward for few weeks and then she was discharged in a stable condition.

【18】A 46-year-old woman presented to the ED with abdominal dis-tension， nausea， exophthalmos， palpitation， and hand trem-ors. She denied any prior comorbidities. 【19】Case 4

【20】A 43-year-old man presented to the ED with dyspnea，palpi-tations， non-productive cough， watery diarrhea， and fever. He had a past medical history of only Graves' disease， which was diagnosed 3 months earlier and was treated with proprano-lol and propy.thiouracil. He was scheduled for radioactive io-dine ablation therapy； however， had stopped taking carbima-zole for the last 2 weeks. The patient scored 65 points on the Burch Wartofsky Point Scale， confirming the thyroid storm sta-tus. On examination， he was found to have an irregular pulse and severe global hypokinesis on bedside echocardiogram. He was given adenosine and metoprolol for supraventricular tachycardia； however， he developed cardiac arrest， with pulse-less electrical activity. Spontaneous circulation was achieved after 14 cycles， and then he was put on VA-ECMO and CRRT to support the failing heart and kidneys. The thyroid storm led to MOF， and therefore he was started on plasmapheresis as a bridging therapy to eventual thyroidectomy and to help remove circulating thyroid hormones and immune media-tors. The patient was clinically and hemodynamically improv-ing； therefore， decannulation of ECMO was performed on day8. He was scheduled for thyroidectomy on the first day after ECMO decannulation. However， the neurology team observed poor neurological responses. The electro-encephalogram dem-onstrated severe hypoxic encephalopathy； therefore， thyroid-ectomy was declined. On day 12， the patient developed sep-sis due to gram-negative bacteremia and went into refractory septic shock and asystole， and eventually died.

【21】Discussion

【22】Thyroid storm is a medical emergency representing the ex-treme manifestation of severe thyrotoxicosis with multiorgan dysfunction/failure . High suspicion and quick diagnosis of the condition lead to prompt initiation of appropriate man-agement and decrease the mortality.

【26】Use of Beta Blockers in Thyroid Storm

【27】In all of our patients， the decision was made by the ED team to control the heart rate with beta blockers. However， the patients started to deteriorate soon after the administration of beta blockers and had to be placed on ECMO， due to life-threatening cardiovascular instability. The mechanism of how hyperthy-roidism induces a hyperadrenergic state and its effects on the cardiovascular system are complex . A systematic review found 9 published reports of beta blocker-induced cardiovas-cular collapse， and case reports addressed the occurrence of cardiovascular collapse after the use of beta blockers .

【30】All of our patients had clinical evidence of heart failure on pre-sentation and low ejection fraction of 20% to 25%. We suggest extreme precaution and/or avoidance of the use of long-act-ing beta blocking agents in those patients. Ultra-short-acting beta blockers that are easy to titrate may be a suitable alter-native in this subset of patients.

【31】Use of ECMO in Thyroid Storm

【32】ECMO is used in critical care when conventional therapies fail to provide enough oxygenation and/or cardiac output. VA-ECMO is a form of extracorporeal life support and tempo-rary mechanical circulatory support， in which blood is with-drawn from a large vein， passes through an oxygenator， and is returned to a major artery. It provides a bridge to recovery， allowing time for the patient’s heart and lungs to heal . In our institution， VA-ECMO is provided in the medical ICU and performed by the intensivist via a percutaneous Seldinger ap-proach， using the femoral vein and artery.

【33】ECMO is not a standard treatment for thyroid storm； however， in very severe and refractory cases of thyroid storm， in which the patient is critically ill， ECMO can be considered as a last-re-sort therapy J.ECMO can provide temporary support for the patient's heart and lung function while the underlying thyroid condition and MOF is treated， which can help to stabilize the pa-tient's condition and improve their chance of survival. However， ECMO is a complex and invasive procedure that requires a high level of expertise and should only be performed in specialized centers. Of note， the use of VA-ECMO support can be deferred if a rapid stabilization of the hemodynamics could be achieved prior to thyroidectomy . Our patients experienced refractory cardiovascular collapse and after multiple resuscitation attempts， and it was decided to initiate ECMO support. The effect of high thyroid hormones can alter the sensitivity or responsiveness of various tissues to catecholamines and can yield the medication less effective . Therefore， in these cases of refractory cardiogenic shock， an early initiation of patient on ECMO might help stabilize the patient until the definitive treatment is deliv-ered. Follow-up echocardiogram demonstrated improvement in the ejection fraction in all patients， who were subsequently weaned and decannulated successfully from ECMO.

【34】Use of Plasmapheresis

【35】Plasmapheresis， or TPE (extra-corporeal blood purification technique)， acts via extracorporeal separation and removal of plasma through centrifugation. This will remove plasma pro-teins with bound T3/T4 resulting in a rapid decrease of thy-roid hormones . In the case of a thyroid storm， plasma-pheresis is not a standard of care， but it can be considered in some cases as an adjunctive therapy to help lower the levels of thyroid hormones as early as possible . Binimelis et al described a 30-fold decrease in total thyroxine levels with plasma exchange as compared with conventional treatment， and this effect was proportional to the serum level of thyrox-ine . Rapid clinical improvement was apparent in our pa-tients after the first 2 plasma exchanges， and there was also improvement in the serum FT3 and FT4 levels .

【36】Thyroidectomy in Thyroid Storm Under ECMO Support

【37】In thyroid storm， surgical intervention is not a first-line treat-ment； however， it can be considered in selected cases， as the mainstay of treatment remains medical management. Our pa-tients went rapidly into cardiorespiratory failure despite maxi-mum medical therapy； therefore， the professional medical team decided to go for urgent thyroidectomy under ECMO support. In thyroid storm， thyroidectomy is associated with an over-all mortality rate of 10%， which is why surgery is not the first choice . However， the criteria to decide when patients with thyroid storm should undergo thyroidectomy are lacking. Therefore， thyroidectomy should only be considered as a treat-ment option for thyroid storm on case-by-case basis， provid-ed that the benefits outweigh the risks and that the patient is not responding to other treatments.

【0】Background：

【1】Geographic tongue manifests as lingual lesions of well demarcated areas of erythema surrounded by a white keratotic border. Its causes remain unknown.

【2】Case report：

【3】We report the case of a young female with geographic tongue that occurred around the periovulatory time of her spontaneous menstrual cycle. This is the first such case report in the literature showing a relationship between the menstrual cycle and occurrence of cyclic oral lesions. We were also able to follow and describe the effects of assisted reproductive techniques and pregnancy on the patient's stomatitis.

【4】Conclusion：

【5】Although there is a relationship between the periovulatory time period and onset of lesions， the various hormonal effects on the geographic tongue remain to be clearly defined.

【6】Key words：

【7】erythema migrans · geographic stomatitis · ectopic geographic tongue · stomatitis areata migrans · migratory stomatitis· erythema circinata migrans · annualus migrans · ovulation· periovulatory· hormonal changes · spontaneous cycle Geographic stomatitis was first described in 1955under the term erythema migrans . Other terms were used to describe this lesion including ectopic geographic tongue， stomatitis areata migrans， migra-tory stomatitis， erythema circinata migrans， and ban-nualus migrans. The incidence of geographic tongue appears to run between 2.2% and 16% in various populations It has been reported to occur more commonly in men than women and can manifest itself in multiple sites within the oral mucosa. Lesions are described as flattened， circinate， erythematous areas surrounded by a keratotic border. The etiology of geographic tongue remains largely unknown. It oc-curs more frequently in patients with psoriasis . An increased frequency of geographic tongue has also been reported in patients with atopy . In this report we describe the case of a young woman with cyclic oral lesions suggestive of geographic tongue that occurred around her periovulatory period in multiple menstrual cycles.

【8】CASE REPORT

【9】This is a case of a 27-year-old female gravida 2， para1-0-1-1. She first noted lesions on her tongue in 1995. These lesions were later diagnosed by a dermatologist as geographic tongue. No etiology for her lesions was found. At that time， the patient was not particularly concerned about its occurrence， or its timing in rela-tion to her normal monthly menstrual cycles. Her past medical history was unremarkable. She was allergic to penicillin， which caused a rash. The review of sys-tems revealed mild dysmenorrhea that responded to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents when taken at the onset of her menstrual cycle. Particularly， she did not have a history of psoriasis or atopy.

【10】In 1997， the patient was diagnosed with subfertility and began to attempt pregnancy aggressively. While keeping basal body temperature charts， she noted that the geographic tongue appeared one or two days before her temperature elevation and persisted for four or five days. She noticed that her oral lesions occurred regularly around the time of ovulation in multiple cycles. The geographic tongue occurred nearly every cycle while under our care . It also occasionally occurred prior to her menstrual cycle and continued for approximately three to five days. She reported that acidic food (tomato sauce， spicy foods) were particularly irritating. At one point in her fertility treatment， she received human chorionic gonadotropin to trigger ovulation， and the geographic tongue occurred approximately 48 hours later. Her physical examination was normal other than the notation of geographic tongue associated with ovulation that was been documented by exami-nation over four consecutive cycles.

【11】As a result of her fertility treatment， the patient achieved a pregnancy. The geographic tongue re-solved during the course of the pregnancy and did not re-occur until 4 months post-partum. The geo graphic tongue developed only on the left side and was preceded two days prior with a left sided facial paralysis later diagnosed Bell’s palsy. The geographic tongue lasted for 2 weeks while the facial paralysis persisted.

【12】The family history revealed the occurrence of geo-graphic tongue in her brother at 12 years of age，and a cousin who also was known to have geographic tongue. There was no history of geographic tongue in either parent. There was no known history of pso riasis or atopy in the family

【13】DISCUSSION

【14】The histopathologic evaluation of geographic sto-matitis shows a flattened mucosal surface with ir-regular rete pegs due to loss of filiform papillae. The erythematous area demonstrates parakera-tin desquamation， epithelial degeneration， and microabcess formation near the epithelial surface. Immunohistochemistry of the lesions shows T-cells to be the predominant subepithelial cellular infiltrate， followed by monocytes and macrophages. B-cells are occasionally observed in the subepithelial infiltrate21.

【15】Our case of geographic tongue gives a unique view of possible hormonal causes of geographic tongue occurring in spontaneous cycles and in cycles of controlled ovarian stimulation. Since the lesion occurred just prior to ovulation and occurred with an exogenous HCG injection， possible candidate hormones include lutienizing hormones or one of its downstream effectors. However， as the lesions resolved during pregnancy it is evident that a more complex relationships exists than what can be de-scribed by effects of a specific hormone or hormones. The literature suggested that geographic tongue can be triggered by hormonal changes. The only such report was by Waltimo et al who reported a case of geographic tongue in a 23 year old female student who had an isolated geographic tongue and was on oral contraceptives. The phase of her oral contra-ceptive cycle appeared to have a marked effect on the initiation and duration of the circinate lesions. The tongue changes were most severe on the seven-teenth day of the birth control pill cycle . Other dermatologic lesions related to hormonal changes are described in the literature including progesterone and estrogen dermatitis . These skin conditions are exacerbated in the luteal and the premenstrual phases of the cycle as opposed to the periovulatory period. A case of stomatitis was also described in association with progesterone dermatitis but not as an isolated finding . It does not appear that our patient had either one of these dermatitis expressed as an isolated mucosal lesion on her tongue.

【16】In our report， the lesions disappeared during pregnan-cy and reappeared 4 month post partum associated with Bell’s palsy. Contrary to our case， Diaz-Guzman et al showed that the incidence of geographic tongue increased during pregnancy . On the other hand， the only association that we found between facial nerve palsy and tongue lesion was the Melkersson-Rosenthal syndrome. This disorder is characterized by a triad of facial nerve palsy， orofacial edema， and congenital fissured tongue. Our patient did not meet the criteria of this syndrome .

【17】CONCLUSIONS

【18】Geographic tongue is a benign process which tends to resolve with expectant management. Its onset during the periovulatory period is suggestive of an effect of steroid hormones， as well as numerous inflammatory mediators and interleukins known to circulate in the periovulatory period. Further investigation focusing on steroid hormones and inflammatory mediators and their subsequent effects on geographic tongue are indicated.

【0】Background：

【1】Pilomatrixoma is a solitary tumor and usually occurs in a single location. Its etiology is not clear. Surgical excision and histopathologic evaluation are necessary to iden tify the management of this tunior.

【2】Case Report：

【3】We present an instance of pilomatrixoma in both of the forearms of a pediatric patient， their oc-currence separated by an interval of 3 years. The tumor was superficial， well-defined， and freely mobile. The patient underwent surgical excision. The histopathological examination revealed pi-lomatrixoma. No recurrence was observed in 3 years of follow-up. However， 3 years after the first operation， another tumor was detected in the contralateral forearm demonstrating the same prop-erties. The same procedure was also performed for this tumor. This patient was observed without evidence of recurrences for 3 years.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】The management of pilomatrixoma is surgical excision， and diagnosis should be confirmed by his-tapathologic evaluation. It is usually seen as a single tumor； however， it is rarely multiple. Our case is of importance， since we observed pilomatrixoma in both forearms， but at different time intervals.

【6】key words： pilomatrixoma-surgery· calcifying epithelioma of Malherbe· pediatric patient Pilomatrixoma was first described in 1880 by Malherbe and Chemantais as a calcified tumor originating from a seba-ceous gland and was renamed as pilomatrixoma by Forbes and Helwig in 1961 . Pilomatrixoma is considered as an epithelioma of the hair follicles with cytodifferentiation to-wards cells of the hair matrix， the hair cortex， and cells of the inner sheath. This tumor usually appears as a benign， subcutaneous calcified mass，less than 3 cm in size.

【7】We present an instance of pilomatrixoma in both forearms in a pediatric patient， occurring 3 years apart. The clinical pre-sentation， tumor behavior， and outcomes are also reviewed.

【8】CASE REPORT

【9】A 10-year-old boy presented with a superficial， rock-hard nodule in the left forearm. This tumor was less than 2 cm diameter and freely mobile . The overlying skin was normal in appearance， and no evidence of ulceration or discoloration was seen. Routine laboratory tests and metabolic findings were found to be within normal limits. Results of chest and abdominal radiographs and electro-cardiogram were normal. Ultrasonography demonstrated a well-defined， round， hyperechogenic mass with a posteri-or dense acoustic shadow. The patient underwent surgical excision with a direct approach by making the incision over the tumor. The histopathological examination revealed pi-lomatrixoma： proliferation of cells resembling basal cells of the epidermis and a rather predominant component of ghost (shadow) cells. Calcification was present . No recurrence was observed in 3 years of follow-up. Three years after the first operation， another tumor was seen in the contralateral forearm， demonstrating the same prop-erties. The same procedure was also performed for this tu-mor. The patient was then observed for 3 years without ev-idence of recurrences.

【10】DISCUSSION

【11】Pilomatrixoma is a benign epithelial neoplasm with hair cell differentiation， which may have a familial transmission， al-though its cause remains unclear. In our patient no familial history was found. Approximately half of all pilomatrixoma occur in the head and neck， with the remainder occurring in decreasing frequency in the upper extremity， trunk， and lower extremity . As this tumor is located superficial-ly， routine radiologic evaluation is unnecessary， except for ultrasonographic examination . The curative therapy is surgical excision， and diagnosis should be confirmed by histopathologic evaluation . Pilomatrixoma usually oc-curs as a single tumor， and multiple tumors accur in 2-3%of cases . However， in our case， we detected the same tu-mor in both forearms， but 3 years apart. This condition is not common in the literature.

【12】CONCLUSIONS

【13】Although this tumor has a benign structure， it is impor-tant remember that it may accur at different locations at different times.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Preoperative assessment of various anatomic and clinical features helps identify potentially difficult laryngoscopy and intubation in advance， allowing the anaesthetist to be prepared for such a scenario. Though"Short Neck" is a commonly used term in airway assessment indicating the possibility of a difficult airway. There is a lack of clarity regarding the cut-off value and the association of different neck lengths (Anterior， Posterior and Lateral) to the laryngoscopic view. AIM： Evaluation of anterior， posterior and lateral neck length in neutral and extended positions and correlation of each measurement with the prediction of difficult laryngoscopic view. Materials and Methods： This prospective observational study was conducted on 150 patients belonging to the American Society of Anesthesiologists(ASA) grade 1/11， aged 18-65 years with body mass index (BMI) 18 to 35 kg/m， scheduled to undergo elective surgeries under general anaesthesia with endotracheal intubation. Each subject’s anterior， lateral and posterior neck lengths (ANL， LNL， PNL) were measured preoperatively. Direct laryngoscopy was done to achieve the best Cormack Lehane(CL) grade using manoeuvres (Backward upward rightward manoeuvre(BURP)/OELM/Change of Blade/Change of pillow height/RAMP positioning) when indicated and the same compared to the measured neck lengths. Result： The incidence of difficult laryngoscopy was 18 per cent in our study population. Anterior neck length in a neutral position was the best predictor of difficult laryngoscopy， with a threshold of less than or equal to 9 cm. Noparticular neck length correlated with BMI and age. However， all the neck lengths showed a positive correlation with the height of the subject Conclusion：ANL with a cut-off criterion of less than or equal to 9 cm in a neutral position can be used objectively when measuring neck length. All neck lengths showed significant change with neck mobility. The rate of change of both PNL and LNL with head extension position showed significant change in difficult laryngoscopy subjects.

【1】KEYWORDS Neck length， neutral， extension， mobility， laryngoscopic view

【2】Introduction

【3】Airway management remains one of the most important respon-sibilities of an anesthesiologist. Amongst all the oxygenation/ventilation devices available， tracheal intubation remains the gold standard in securing the airway since it ensures optimal ventilation and oxygenation while reducing the risk of aspiration. A proper airway assessment is pivotal in predicting a difficult airway and preventing airway-related adverse effects. Preop-erative assessment of various anatomic and clinical features helps us identify potentially difficult laryngoscopy in advance， thus allowing the anaesthetist to be prepared for such a sce-nario. For example， Laryngoscopy and subsequent intubation are considered difficult in patients with a laryngoscopic view of Cormack-Lehane(CL) grade 3 or 4 .

【4】Neck length is one criterion that is simple to assess and re-quires minimal patient cooperation to be performed properly.“Short Neck" is a commonly used term when assessing a pa-tient's airway， which indicates the possibility of a difficult air-way and certainly would influence the management. However no specific cut-off is mentioned in the literature for a short neck. Lack of clarity surrounding the association of different neck lengths (Anterior， Posterior and Lateral) to laryngoscopic view despite its relevance in airway management necessitated our study. Adequate neck mobility， part of Wilson’s score， is a pre-requisite for head elevation or the sniffing position ideal during laryngoscopy . However， few studies are available that quote the relationship between neck length and neck mobility.

【5】Also， the majority of studies of difficult laryngoscopy and intubation have been performed in the American or European population . Anthropometrically， Indians are different com-pared toAmericans or Europeans. Differences in patient charac-teristics due to race or ethnicity may influence the incidence of difficult laryngoscopy and difficult intubation. Adequate data of normal values in a given population may help the clinician identify patients outside the normal range， which is potentially challenging.

【6】To address these issues， we undertook a prospective study to determine：

【7】1\. Anterior， posterior， and lateral neck length in neutral and extended positions and correlate each measurement with the prediction of a difficult laryngoscopic view.

【8】2\. To assess the correlation of the neck length measurements with patients' sex， weight， and height.

【9】3\. Evaluate the degree of neck mobility and correlate it with the grading of the laryngoscopic view.

【10】Methodology

【11】After obtaining approval from the local ethics committee and written informed consent from patients， 150 adult patients of ei-ther gender with ASA physical status I or 2 scheduled for elective surgery under general anaesthesia requiring tracheal intubation were included in this prospective observational study. Standard airway assessment parameters like Modified Mallampati Grad-ing (MMPG)， mouth opening， dentition and jaw subluxation were noted. Patients with an obvious structural abnormality of the airway， those at increased risk of aspiration， pregnant pa-tients， severely obese with BMI >35kg/m² and unstable cervical spine were excluded from the study.

【12】The following airway characteristics were assessed preopera-tively by one investigator to reduce inter-observer variability：

【13】1\. Neck length 

【14】(a) Anterior neck length (ANL)： upper margin of the hy-oid bone to jugular notch 

【15】(b) Posterior neck length (PNL)： perpendicular distance between the external occipital protuberance and the tip of 7th cervical vertebra ， (C)ILateral neck length (LNL)： the distance between the tip of the mastoid to the meeting point between the neck and the shoulder (inflexion point)， all three neck lengths in a neutral head position .

【16】3\. Anterior， posterior， and lateral neck lengths in head ex-tended position.

【17】All patients fasted overnight and received oral alprazolam0.25 mg/0.5 mg (< or>50 kg body weight， respectively) the night before and on the morning of surgery. In the operating (a)

【18】(b)

【19】(C)

【20】room， standard monitoring was established (electrocardiogram， non-invasive blood pressure， pulse oximetry， capnography). A difficult airway cart was kept at hand. The plane of the patient’s face was kept at the level of the xiphisternum of the anaesthe-siologist performing laryngoscopy and intubation by adjusting the height of the operating table. The patient's head was kept in the "sniffing position" withan appropriately sized pillow below the head. After pre-oxygenation with 100% oxygen for 3 min， anaesthesia was induced with fentanyl 2mic/kg and propofol2.5 mg/kg or thiopentone 5mg/kg. After induction， mask ven-tilation was checked， and rocuronium 1 mg/kg was given to facilitate tracheal intubation. During mask ventilation， anaes-thesia was maintained with isoflurane up to 1MAC and oxygen and nitrous mixture.

【21】An Anaesthesiologist with an experience of a minimum of 50laryngoscopies and intubation and blinded to the preoperative measurements performed the laryngoscopy and intubation. Ap-propriately sized Macintosh blade (3 or 4) was used according to the patient's size (size 3 for medium-sized and size 4 for large-sized adults) and as per the clinical judgment of the intubating person. The Cormack- Lehane grading system assessed and graded the laryngoscopic view. The difficult laryngoscopic view was defined as CL grade 3 or 4 under direct laryngoscopy with an appropriate-sized blade without applying external pressure or manoeuvre in the sniffing position.

【22】If the laryngoscopic view was difficult， manoeuvres like BURP， external laryngeal pressure， blade change， positioning(change of pillow height or placement of a ramp below shoul-ders)， or change of the anesthesiologist was tried， and the change in view was noted.

【23】Statistical Analysis

【24】Assuming an incidence of difficult laryngoscopy of 9.7% and an error of 6 %， a sample size of 94 patients would be required to find significant differences between patients with easy and difficult laryngoscopy . Therefore， we included 150 patients in our study.

【25】Categorical variables were presented in number and percent-age (%)， and continuous variables were presented as mean ± SD and median. The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test tested the normality of data. If the normality was rejected， then a nonparametric test was used.

【26】1\. Quantitative variables were associated using the Unpaired t-test/Mann-Whitney Test (when the data sets were not normally distributed) with easy and difficult laryngoscopy

【27】2\. Qualitative variables were associated using Chi-Square test/Fisher's exact test.

【28】3\. The receiver operating characteristic curve was used to find the area under the curve of the parameter for predicting difficult laryngoscopy. A p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant.

【29】The data was entered into the MS EXCEL spreadsheet and analysed using Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) version 25.0.

【30】Results

【31】Our study included a total of 150 adult patients of either gender. The demographic and anthropometric parameters are presented in tables . In 82% of patients (123 out of 150)， laryngoscopy was easy，and in the rest 27 patients (18%) the view was difficult， necessitating various manoeuvres for better glottic visualization.62 (41.33%) patients had a CL grade 1， followed by 61(40.67%) with a grade of 2A. 2B grade was present in one patient with3A and 3B in 23 and 3 patients， respectively. In the majority(22(81.48%)) of patients， the type of manoeuvre used was BURP to improve the laryngoscopic view. Burp+ Bougie followed this in 3(11.11%)， External laryngeal pressure in 1(3.7%) and Burp +change to Mc Coy blade in 1(3.7%).

【32】In the majority (101(67.33%)) of patients， neck movement (de-gree) was >80. Neck movement (degree) was <80 in only 49 out of 150 patients (32.67%). The distribution of neck movement (de-gree) was comparable with difficult laryngoscopy(>80：-66.67%in easy laryngoscopy group vs 70.37% in difficult laryngoscopy group respectively，<80：-33.33% in easy laryngoscopy group vs 29.63% in difficult laryngoscopy group respectively) (p value=0.71).

【33】A significant association was seen in ANL in both neutral and extension positions with difficult laryngoscopy. (p-value<.05)Mean± SD of ANL (neutral) (cm)， ANL (extension) (cm) in easy laryngoscopy was 11.29±1.68，12.84±1.92 respectively， which was significantly higher as compared to in patients with difficult laryngoscopy (8.67±2.37(p-value<.0001)，10.29±2.7(P value<.0001)) respectively. No significant association was seen in the rate of change of ANL (p value=0.546) with difficult laryn-goscopy. The mean ± SD of the rate of change of ANL in easy laryngoscopy was 1.72± 0.5 cms， and in difficult laryngoscopy was 1.66 ± 0.54 cms with no significant association between them.

【34】A significant association was seen in PNL (neutral)， PNL(extension)， and rate of change of posterior neck length with difficult laryngoscopy (p-value <.05) Mean ±SD of posterior neck length (neutral)， posterior neck length (extension)， rate of change of posterior neck length in easy laryngoscopy was15.95±1.75，12.34±1.55， 3.68±0.83 respectively which was sig-nificantly higher as compared to difficult laryngoscopy (13.59±2.6(p value<.0001)，10.51±2.12 (p value=0.0002)，3.17±0.85(p value=0.005)) respectively.

【35】A significant association was seen in LNL (neutral)， LNL (ex-tension)， and rate of change of lateral neck length with difficult laryngoscopy. (p-value <.05) Mean ±SD lateral neck length (neu-tral)， lateral neck length (extension)， rate of change of lateral neck length (cm) in easy laryngoscopy was 13.47±1.68，12.52±1.59， 0.99±0.27 respectively which was significantly higher as compared to difficult laryngoscopy (11.26±2.31(p value<.0001)，10.45 ±2.18(p value<.0001)， 0.85±0.23(p value=0.01)) respec-tively.

【36】The receiver operating characteristic curve was used to find the cut-off point of airway assessment parameters and neck length for predicting difficult intubation . The discrimi-natory power of anterior neck length (neutral) (AUC 0.815；95%CI： 0.743 to 0.873) was excellent. Furthermore，among all the parameters， Anterior neck length (neutral) was the best predic-tor of difficult laryngoscopy at the cut-off point of ≤9 cm with an 81.50% chance of correctly predicting difficult laryngoscopy.

【37】Pearson correlation coefficient was used to correlate age， weight， height and body mass index with neck lengths . No correlation was seen between age with anterior neck length (neutral)， anterior neck length (extension)， rate of change of anterior neck length， lateral neck length (neutral)， lateral neck length (extension)， rate of change of lateral neck length with a correlation coefficient of 0.078，0.034，0.014，0.057，0.058，0.004 re-spectively. A non-significant mild positive correlation was seen between age with posterior neck length in neutral and extension with a correlation coefficient of 0.084 and 0.116， respectively. A non-significant mild negative correlation was seen between age with the rate of change of posterior neck length with a correlation coefficient of -0.094.

【38】A significant positive correlation was seen between weight(kg) with anterior neck length (neutral)， anterior neck length(extension)， lateral neck length (neutral)， and lateral neck length(extension) with correlation coefficients of 0.24， 0.185，0.209， and 0.226 respectively. As far as height was concerned， there was a significant positive correlation with anterior neck length(neutral)， anterior neck length (extension)， lateral neck length(neutral)， lateral neck length (extension)， posterior neck length (neutral)， posterior neck length (extension) with a correlation co-efficient of 0.336，0.277，0.342，0.349，0.322， 0.274 respectively. No significant association was seen between anterior neck length and lateral neck length with gender. However， posterior neck length in extension showed a significant association with gender.(p-value <.05) Mean ±SD of posterior neck length (extension)(cm) in males was 12.3 ±1.82， which was significantly higher as compared to females (11.7±1.74(p value=0.042)).

【47】Discussion

【48】The incidence of difficult airways varies from 1 to 18 per cent in the general population. The incidence of difficult laryngoscopy(CL grade 3-4) differs in various studies； Smita et al. and Hon-armand et al. reported an incidence of 9.7% and 14.7 per cent， respectively， in their studies . The incidence of difficult laryngoscopy was 18 per cent in our research of 150 patients， which is higher than prior studies' findings. This difference could have resulted from ethnic and anthropometric differences in our study population.

【49】Findings of a short neck are assumed to be associated with a reduced ability to extend the head on the atlantooccipital joint， which impedes the adequate view of the larynx. As the neck length reduces，neck movement becomes increasingly restricted. Consequently， a short neck makes cord visualization difficult. Many published articles we reviewed focused on limited neck movement but did not refer to the Short Neck as a possible cause of difficult laryngoscopy . A short neck was found in about 15% of cases and was highly significantly associated with subsequent difficulty at tracheal intubation .

【50】In day-to-day practice， only the anterior neck length is as-sessed subjectively and categorized as short neck or normal.In the present study， we also looked at lateral and posterior neck lengths， which are simpler to evaluate in obese and paediatric groups or those with a short anterior neck. Our study of various neck lengths in neutral and head extension positions concluded that in the prediction of difficult laryngoscopy， the rate of change of anterior neck length had the lowest sensitivity of 25.93%. On the other hand， specificity was highest for posterior neck length(extension)， which was 91.06%， followed by anterior neck length (neutral) (86.18%)， lateral neck length (neutral) (84.55%)， rate of change of anterior neck length (83.74%). In the prediction of dif-ficult laryngoscopy， the rate of change of lateral neck length had the lowest specificity of 64.23%. The highest positive predictive value was found in posterior neck length (extension) (54.20%)， and the highest negative predictive value was found in anterior neck length (extension) (93.30%). There is always a trade-off between sensitivity and specificity (any increase in sensitivity will be accompanied by a decrease in specificity)， so we choose that variable as best in which combination of sensitivity and specificity gives the maximum predictive value so overall ante-rior neck length (neutral) in cm was the best predictor of difficult laryngoscopy， with a threshold of less than or equal to 9cm. This is comparable to the pilot work of Jafar et al.， which discovered an 8 cm cut-off value . However， it solely described lateral neck length.

【51】Neck mobility is the sum of adequate neck length and degree of extension. The neck must be flexed with the head extended during intubation which is a complicated manoeuvre whose accurate measurement is challenging . X-ray data suggests that atlantooccipital joint restriction may be the cause of diffi-cult intubation . Research has shown that increasing head and neck elevation improves laryngeal exposure . In the event of difficult laryngoscopy， Schmitt and Mang proposed that elevating the head and neck beyond the sniffing posture may increase the vision of the glottic structures， resulting in superior intubation performance . Our findings are comparable to those of Smita et al.， who found that neck mobility of fewer than80 degrees may predict difficult laryngoscopy.

【52】Neck mobility was positively associated with the rate of change of all neck lengths. In addition， there was a significant relationship between the rate of change in lateral and posterior neck length and difficult laryngoscopy. The scientific rationale is that most of the extension produced by direct laryngoscopy occurs at the occipital-Atlanta-axial complex， which includes both posterior and lateral neck length. In contrast， the sub-axial cervical segments are minimally displaced during laryngoscopy.

【53】In our study， no particular neck length correlated with BMI and age. A study by Savva also did not report any difference in age， sex， weight， or height between easy and difficult laryn-goscopy groups . However， all the neck lengths positively correlated with the subject’s height. Perhaps the height- to-neck length ratio may have a better predictive value than Neck length alone， as patient size would be considered. Posterior neck length in extension was significantly higher in males (12.3+1.82) com-pared to females (11.7±1.74)， suggesting greater neck mobility amongst female patients. This finding is comparable to a study by Smita et al.， where a significant proportion of difficult tracheal intubations has been found in males， attributed to differences in neck fat deposition between the sexes . Our study also found a positive correlation between anterior neck length and lateral neck length in both neutral and extension positions to the subjects' weight. In our study， all the neck lengths positively correlated with the subject’s height， suggesting the difference in cut-off value with varying anthropometric measurements. Hence， the height-to-neck length ratio may have a better pre-dictive value than neck length alone， as patient size would be considered.

【54】Regarding limitations， our study excluded specific patient groups like pediatric and obstetric populations， severely obese individuals， and those with structural airway difficulty. Hence the results of our study cannot be extrapolated to those popula-tions.

【55】Secondly， neck length does not consider the relative tongue and pharyngeal size， mandibular space， overriding maxilla， en-larged incisors， decreased temporomandibular joint mobility， or a narrow high arched palate. Therefore， neither of the neck lengths described in our study can be used alone to predict diffi-cult laryngoscopy. Nevertheless， measurement of neck length can be usefully added to other preoperative airway assessment tests such as inter incisor gap， MMPG and thyromental distance.

【56】Conclusion

【57】The present study was designed to compare different neck mea-surements and their correlation with the prediction of difficult laryngoscopy in the Indian population. The study was con-ducted on 150 patients， aged between 18-65 years， of either sex， belonging to ASA grades I and I， undergoing elective surgi-cal procedures requiring general anaesthesia with endotracheal intubation.

【58】ANL in a Neutral position was the best predictor of difficult laryngoscopy among all the neck length measurements. All neck lengths showed significant change with neck mobility. The rate of change of both PNL and LNL with head extension position showed significant change in difficult laryngoscopy subjects.

【59】ANL with a cutoff criterion of less than or equal to 9 cm in a neutral position can be used objectively when measuring neck length. However， this finding needs to be verified with larger studies and amongst different population subtypes. Also， because the aetiology of a difficult airway is multifactorial， integration of Anterior Neck Length with other commonly used predictive tests would help improve the chances of prediction of a difficult airway.

【0】ABSTRACT Background： Dengue fever has recently been an important public health problem. Hepatic involvement in Dengue ranges from elevated liver enzymes to fulminant hepatic failure. The present study was carried out to evaluate liver dysfunction in patients with dengue infections and the correlation between liver function tests & platelet count. Methods： Hospital-based case-control study was conducted on 141 hospitalized with Dengue infection (NS 1 and IgM positive). Dengue Seropositive patients were selected and subjected to complete blood count and liver function tests. Results： The participants were found to have elevated levels of SGOT， SGPT levels and lower levels of serum albumin and platelet count compared to control on evaluation. A significant negative correlation was noted between SGOT/ SGPT levels， and baseline platelet counts. The Pearson correlation between platelet count and SGOT showed r=-0.185 and p-value <0.01， which proves that when platelet count decreases， and the SGOT levels increases. Similarly， the correlation between platelet count and SGPT showed r=-0.166 and <0.01 which proves that when platelet count decreases， the SGPT levels increase. Conclusion： Statistically significant correlation was observed between liver enzymes with platelet count. Furthermore， the severity of dengue infection predicted the severity of liver derangements. Therefore， it is recommended that Patients with dengue infections be screened for hepatic dysfunction. As hepatic dysfunction in dengue is transient and reversible， early identification of the same would help reduce life-threatening complications.

【1】KEYWORDS SGOT， SGPT， Liver enzyme

【2】INTRODUCTION

【3】Dengue fever is generally self-limiting， but its symptoms can be debilitating and cause considerable incapacitating morbidity， which has significant health and economic toll on society. There is currently no specific antiviral therapy or vaccine available for DF or DHF/DSS.1

【4】Hepatic dysfunction is a crucial feature seen in DENV infec-tion. Hepatocytes and Kupffer cells are prime targets for DENV infection， as confirmed in biopsies and autopsies of fatal cases. An eventual outcome of hepatocyte infection by DENV is cellu- lar apoptosis， a phenomenon demonstrated both in vivo and in vitro. After apoptosis， what stays in the cells are the Councilman Bodies. The various pathways involved in this apoptotic process include viral cytopathy， hypoxic mitochondrial dysfunction， the immune response and accelerated endoplasmic reticular stress. Expression of DENV-induced TRAIL and TNF-a and Fas sig-nalling have also been implicated in this process. Activation of the mitochondrial cell death pathway stems from the func-tional and morphological defects of these mitochondria. The present study aimed to evaluate liver dysfunction in patients with dengue infections and the correlation between liver func-tion tests & platelet count.
