【38】DISCUSSION

【39】The number of patients included in this study was ten people who received ROM treatment. In this study， all patients are male(100%). This is consistent with the literature which suggests that This study showed that the most affected age group was ≥ 49years (40%). Leprosy can affect all ages， in a study on the age variation of patients between 11-75 years old， most were found in 20-30 years’ age group followed by 60-70 years' age group. The high incidence in adulthood and elderly may be caused by the length of the incubation period， with an average duration of 2-7 years. Another explanation is that leprosy in adult populations whose living in endemic areas is often reinfection or superinfection from other subclinically infected persons but which undergo a decreases in the immune response against leprosy as time progress.

【40】In this study， it appears that the number of bacilli patients ranged from +1 to +3， indicating that these patients were in the form of borderline leprosy under leprosy immunologic spec-trum， with an unstable immune system. The spectrum of leprosy， which consists of fixed chronic polar and borderline forms. At the tuberculoid pole (TT)， a highly cell-mediated immune (CMI) system against M.leprae is characterised by a T-helperl response with interferon-gamma secretion that results in a slight bacterial load /number， fewer skin lesions， and the ab-sence or slight antibodies produced. The lepromatous pole (LL) is characterised by the low or absence of CMI-mediated specific immunity to M.leprae， but the production of many antibodies， high bacterial load /amount， and skin lesions are widespread. The borderline intermediary form (borderline tuberculoid， bor-derline and borderline lepromatous) may indicate immunologic changes towards one of the poles.

【41】The subjects of the study were patients diagnosed with MB or lepromatous type leprosy. In lepromatous leprosy， resistance is very low to withstand significant bacilli proliferation， but still capable enough to induce tissue damage by inflammation， especially on the nerve. Lepromatous leprosy is characterized by low cell-mediated immunity with the type of humoral im-mune response is Th-2， and mRNAs mainly producing IL-4， IL-5， and IL-10 cytokines that are thought to play a role in the non-responsiveness of immunity and failure activation of macrophage in lepromatous type leprosy， so it cannot limit the growth of bacteria.

【42】Interleukin-4 is first recognised as a cytokine that plays an important role in the development of Th-2 response. The ability of IL-4 to provide inhibitory effects on T-cell responses and the preferential expression of IL-4 mRNA in LL patient has been well-documented. In this study， there was no significant difference between IL-4 levels before and after ROM therapy even though there was a significant increase. A slightly different result from this study was obtained by Budiani S who studied the effect of ROM therapy three months after therapy in IL-12and IL-4 levels. Also， a study by Bandjar FK， which examined the effect of MDT MB therapy after three months on IL-12 and IL-4. This may be caused by several factors.

【43】First， in this study， the patient’s slit skin smear ranges from+1 to +3 indicating that the patient is in borderline type with an unstable immune system. Leprosy is a disease with an unstable immune system. At one extreme pole (TT) the patient exhibits a strong cellular immunity to M.leprae which effec- tively limits bacterial growth through the production of local Th-1cytokines， i.e. IL-12 and IFN-y. At the other extreme poles(LL)， characterised by widespread multibacillary disease and lack of response to M.leprae， Th2 cell activation inhibits Th1 cells， which causes defects in cellular immunity specific to M.leprae. Between the two stable polar forms， there is a borderline form with an uncertain immunological status.  Another factor is that in this study， the subjects may have a mixed Th0 cytokine pattern. In the study by Hu and salgame using Clone of Th0 shows that Th0 also produces IFN-y and IL-4. Lastly， mast cell and basophil cell activity. In addition to having a role in IgE formation in some diseases such as bronchial asthma， allergic rhinitis， and parasite infections. The mast cells and ba-sophils also produce interleukin four so that the above statement may have an effect on increased IL-4 levels after treatment even though the number of bacteria decreases.

【44】The same is true for IL-12 levels which showed a significant decrease between before and after ROM therapy. Interleukin-12is a major cytokine and is essential in response to intracellular pathogens through IFN-c production and promotion of cell-mediated immunity.

【45】Several possibilities may explain the IL-12 decline in this study： First， leprosy has two polar forms， lepromatous leprosy tuberculoid leprosy， with a contrast cytokine profile. Interferon-gamma interleukin type-1(IFN-g)， interleukin-2 (IL-2)， and IL-12dominate tuberculoid poles， but the Th2-like cytokine profile occurs at the lepromatous pole. Between the two polar forms is an unstable clinical and immunological form， borderline tuber-culoid (BT) and borderline lepromatous (BL). In this study obtained bacilli patients ranged from +1 to +3 indicating that the patient is in type borderline with an unstable immune sys-tem. Inhibition of IL-12 by other cytokines， especially by IL-10. Whereas if IL-10 is elevated then， IL-12 will show a decrease. IL-10 is a strong inhibitor of IL-12 production by inhibiting tran-scription of the IL-12 encoding gene as well as the induction of synthesis of a special protein. Some conditions such as chronic inflammation of the intestine may also support the pro-duction of IL-10 by B cells.  The coinfected condition between Mycobacterium tuberculosis and leishmaniasis， especially in the endemic areas of Mycobacterium may show no response to IL-12. Monocyte non-responsiveness in lepromatous patients， so even though stimulated by IFN-y， monocytes still cannot produce IL-12； and lastly， the probability of IL-12 inhibitionby prostaglandin E2 (PGE2). PGE2 has been shown to have the abiRrostaghnuce .i0 ant ability to induce IL-10 and suppress the production of many proinflammatory cytokines. There are some limitations in this study. The sample size was limited in number due to the limited number of patients in our hospitals with previous data on IL-12 and IL-4levels. Also， our population was not examined for other possible coexisting conditions such as parasitic infesta-tions， allergic rhinitis， asthma， and atopic dermatitis that might also affect the cytokines examined in this study. Thus， future studies with larger sample size and screening for other systemic diseases， especially those that might affect IL-12 and IL-4 levels， need to be conducted.

【0】ABSTRACT Introduction： Osteochondromas are benign neoplasms arising from small cartilage nodules within the periosteum. They can be pedunculated or sessile and are more common in the extremities. They rarely develop in flat or small bones like scapula， feet， hands， and pelvis. Management of the lesion is by en-bloc excision. Solitary osteochondroma carries 1% life long risks of malignant transformation. There has been no other case reported of osteochondroma of inferior pubic ramus has been reported in the literature. Case report： We present a very rare case of a55-years-old male who was incidentally found to have bony growth in the inferior pubic ramus on x-ray and CT scan. The MRI showed a cartilaginous cap of 7mm. An excision biopsy was planned， as the patient wanted it to be removed due to a strong family history of cancer. A medial approach was used for en-bloc excision. The post-operative histology confirmed it to be osteochondroma. There has been no recurrence with a 2year follow-up. Conclusion： When evaluating mass in the pelvis， Osteochondroma of the pelvis should be kept in mind as a rare differential diagnosis. These don't always have to be removed as they are benign however some situations such as symptomatic， cosmetic reasons， and in our case strong family history of cancer. The treatment for osteochondroma is surgical resection.

【1】KEYWORDS osteochondroma， pelvis， inferior pubic ramus

【2】Introduction

【3】Osteochondroma is the most common benign bone tumour. It is defined as a benign， cartilaginous neoplasm found in any bone that undergoes enchondral bone formation in its development. Most commonly， it occurs between the ages of 10 to 30. However， it may occur at any age. Males and females are equally affected. The cause of osteochondroma is still unknown. Patients with osteochondromas are often asymptomatic. Symptomatic patients usually present with symptoms like painless hard mass， one limb longer than the other， pressure with exercise， soreness of muscles lying close to osteochondromas. They can easily be diagnosed on x-rays， CT scans， MRI. Management of the lesion is by en-bloc excision. Biopsy confirms the diagnosis.

【4】The most commonly  arise from the appendicular skeleton， especially around the knee： Lower limb comprises 50% of all cases with distal Femur， the most common site followed by 30%， in the proximal tibia： 15-20%Less common locations： feet， pelvis. In the upper limb， humerus involvement is 10-20%. The less common locations are hand and scapula. The posterior elements of the spine are uncommon， but not rare， site for these tumours The risk of Malignant transformation of solitary osteochondroma is <1%； however， in the case of multiple hereditary exostosis， the rate is much higher (5%).

【5】Excision of such a pelvic lesion is required only if there are pressure symptoms. Pelvic osteochondromas can present as compressive neuropathy or compressive symptoms on the ure-thra， bladder or other vital structures and so on. On the contrary a pubic bone mass may need to be removed in young females， which might be prominent at labia for cosmetic reasons.

【6】Case report

【7】This case report is of a 55-years-old male presented to the ac-cident and emergency department after an incidental finding of growth on CT scan abdomen and x-ray pelvis. The patient initially presented to the physician with abdominal pain and loose stools not relieved with medication. The patient had a strong family history of cancer. CT scan abdomen was advised to look for the cause of abdominal pain， which showed big bony growth in the inferior pubic ramus. Physical examination was unremarkable.

【8】Radiographs

【9】On anteroposterior (AP) view of the pelvis ， well-circumscribed lesion in relation to the inferior ramus of right pubis with internal calcification. No associated periosteal reac-tion. Appearances are suggestive of osteochondroma. CT scan performed， which showed an Incidental note made of a 4.9x4.1x 3.2 cm cauliflower type exostosis arising from the body of the right pubis most likely consistent with an osteochondroma.MRI performed， which demonstrated an exophytic polypoidal lesion from the inferior ramus of the right pubis measuring around4.4 cm in maximum transverse dimension. The lesion does not demonstrate any post-contrast enhancement or restricted diffu-sion. The cartilaginous cap is within normal limits and measures up to 0.7 cm negating the possibility of malignant transforma-tion. The stalk of this polypoidal lesion measures around 1.2 cm in craniocaudal dimension.

【10】Surgery excision was performed in a supine position with a leg in the figure of four positions. A curved incision over the swelling was made. Operative time was 30 minutes， and blood loss was 50 mls. The fascia was incised longitudinally. Plane identified between Adductor muscles and swelling identified. The adductors were then partly detached from their origin from inferior pubic ramus. Osteochondroma excised in total， and hemostasis is achieved. The closure was done in lavers. His postoperative period was unremarkable， and he was discharged the next day. Pathologic sections showed fragments of tissue composed of mature bone trabeculae covered by fibrocartilage cap. No atypia or atypical mitotic activity seen in the sections examined， thus confirming non-malignant osteochondroma.

【11】Osteochondromas are usually thought to be benign bone tu-mours， although they are more correctly thought of as devel-opmental anomalies. They present as solitary (85% of cases) or multiple lesions in the context of multiple hereditary exosto-sis (in 15% of the case)， commonly in an autosomal dominant marner.

【12】Only a few case reports are reported in the literature. Prafulla Herode et al. 30 presented a similar case of osteochondroma of the pubic tubercle. The patient presented with swelling in the right groin， which was insidious and slow-growing. The patient consulted for cosmetic reasons，and en bloc resection was performed. The involvement of the pelvic bone is rare. Unlike limb involvement， in pelvic involvement， the symptomatology can change into an unusual course. Wang et al. reported pubic osteochondromas that cause bladder outlet obstruction. Carpintero et al.  reported another case with unusual symp-tomatology that caused discomfort during sexual intercourse. Contrary to that， our patient had no swelling， but abdominal symptoms and a CT scan were performed. On which osteochon-droma were incidental findings.

【13】 Historically and currently， most osteochondromas are incidental findings and are treated solely with observation. If they remain asymptomatic， they can be ignored. Lesions that create mechanical symptoms become painful， begin to enlarge， or cause growth disturbance have historically been treated with surgical removal， and this remains the mainstay of treatment. Biologic therapies for osteochondromas may be possible in the future.

【14】Osteochondroma is usually diagnosed clinically and radi-ologically. Multiple modalities such as radiographs， CT scan and MRI scan can be used. Diagnoses can be confirmed by histopathology. As in our patient， a patient CT scan was per-formed because of symptoms， and further confirmation was done after histopathology.

【15】In our case， primary en bloc resection was performed. The patient was followed up for one year to screen him for any recurrence.

【0】ABSTRACT The Middle East respiratory syndrome is a zoonotic viral disease caused by a novel Coronavirus named Middle East Respiratory Syndrome-Coronavirus (MERS-CoV). More than 1806 cases have been reported in human beings till the end of 2016 with a fatality rate of more than 30%. Majority of the cases have been reported from Saudi Arabia. Many healthcare-associated outbreaks have been reported with the most significant such outbreak being reported from the Republic of Korea in 2015， where 186 cases including 36 deaths occurred. MERS is a viral pneumonia with rapidly progressive respiratory failure leading to ARDS. It presented a wide range of clinical manifestations and associated with significant mortality rates in hospital admitted patients with comorbidities. Multiple surveillance and phylogenetic studies suggest a bat origin for this virus. A diagnostic real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) is done to detect MERS-CoV.Supportive treatment is the mainstay of management as no specific drug treatment exists for MERS. Resveratrol has shown to inhibit MERS-CoV infection and prolong cellular survival after virus infection. It is also inhibited by interferon type I in cultured cells. Adequate infection control measures are the mainstay in the management of MERS-CoV. Surveillance should be conducted on a large scale among humans and different animal species to determine the exact rate of spread of MERS-CoV.

【1】1.INTRODUCTION

【2】In June 2012， a new coronavirus was isolated from a male pa-tient in Saudi Arabia who was suffering from severe respiratory illness & later died in a hospital in Jeddah. This virus was ini-tially named as human coronavirus-EMC and later named as Middle East Respiratory Syndrome-Coronavirus (MERS-CoV). MERS-CoV is known to cause severe hypoxemic respiratory failure with multi-organ failure and often requires admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) . Since June 2012， multiple out-breaks have been reported in or been epidemiologically linked to the Arabian Peninsula . Till 27 September 2016， there were 1806 laboratory-confirmed cases reported by the World Health Organization (WHO)， which includes 643 related deaths. The majority of MERS cases are reported from Saudi Arabia . The continuous MERS epidemic in the Arabian peninsula is believed to be related to the failure to control the zoonotic sources. Many healthcare-associated outbreaks have been reported with the most extensive such outbreak being reported from the Republic of Korea in 2015， where 186 cases including 36 deaths occurred. The index case had a travel history to Arabian peninsula .

【3】2.GEOGRAPHICAL DISTRIBUTION

【4】MERS cases have been reported from 27 countries which in-clude few from European， Asian， North American and African continent. Majority of the cases have been reported from the endemic region of MERS which is the Middle East. Recent re-ports of MERS case from Korea indicated the rapid spreading potential of this virus & not checked by early detection and in-fection control measures . After Saudi Arabia， Korea has the second highest number of MERS cases (n=185) and United Arab Emirates (UAE) in third with 83 cases. There are at least 13 cases of MERS reported from UAE， Jordan， Philippines， Malaysia， Algeria， Egypt， Greece， Netherlands， Qatar， United States and Turkey which were reported to be spread via travellers who visited Saudi Arabia . Travel related MERS cases have also been reported from the United Kingdom，Italy， France， Germany， Tunisia & Iran . Patients reported outside the middle east， all had a history of travel to the middle east or had contact with a primary case .

【5】3.VIROLOGY

【6】Coronaviruses are large enveloped single-stranded RNA viruses. The glycoprotein spikes surrounding the spherical virion give the viruses its characteristic "halo appearance" on electron microscopy . Coronaviruses can infect and cause disease in many animal species including bats， mice， birds， dogs， pigs and cattle .

【7】Human coronaviruses belong to two genera： Alpha coron-aviruses and Beta coronaviruses. The genus Beta coronaviruses consist of 4 lineages， A， B， C and D. Severe acute respiratory syndrome(SARS-CoV) belongs to lineage B， but MERS-CoV be-longs to lineage C beta coronaviruses. Sequence analysis shows that MERS-CoV is closely related to the bat coronaviruses HKU4and HKU5. Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus(SARS-CoV) was also derived from bat coronaviruses. MERS-CoV has a similar phylogeny and is considered a cousin of SARS CoV but both have distinct biology， such as the use of different human receptors.

【8】Since the discovery， various names have been attributed to MERS-CoV like human coronavirus -Erasmus medical cen-tre (hCoV-EMC)， human beta coronaviruses 2c England Qatar， human beta coronaviruses 2c Jordan N3， beta coronavirus Eng-land 1 and novel coronaviruses (NCoV). Currently， the inter-national committee on Taxonomy and the coronaviruses study group (CSG) has decided the name to be Middle East Respiratory Syndrome-Corona Virus (MERS-CoV).

【9】4.VIRAL GENOME AND PROTEIN

【10】The genome structure of MERS-CoV is similar to that of other coronaviruses. The RNAs are capped and polyadenylated with the 5'two-thirds of the genome encoding the non-structural proteins (NSPs) involved in viral replication and the remaining3' third of the genome encoding the structural genes. The surface of virion has a heavily glycosylated， petal shaped，large protein known as spike (S) glycoproteins .

【11】Dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP4) is also called CD26 is a 766-aa type II transmembrane glycoprotein that has been shown to be the functional receptor for MERS-CoV in permissive cell lines . MERS-CoV can bind to DPP4 from several species. In addition to humans and camels non-human primates， rabbits， goats， sheep， and horses， among other animals， are thought to be susceptible to infection . DPP4 is expressed on the cell surface in the lungs， kidneys， small intestine， liver， parotid gland， spleen， testes， prostate and activated leucocytes. This explains the capacity of MERS-CoV to infect cells of these organs. MERS-CoV can also bind to bat DPP4 J.

【12】5.EPIDEMOLOGY

【13】MERS-CoV is considered as the second coronavirus after SARS-CoV that can cause a pandemic . Like many other coron-aviruses， MERS-CoV is believed to be originated from bats. This is based on the isolation of other lineage C beta-coronaviruses that are very closely related to MERS-CoV on phylogenetic anal-ysis. However， still， it is difficult to prove that bats are the direct source of human disease . Several other animal species like dromedary camels (Camelus dromedarius)， cows， goats and sheep have been assessed for serological evidence of MERS-CoV infection. MERS-CoV specific antibodies were only found in dromedary camels. The first detection of MERS-CoV was re-ported in dromedary camels on a farm in Qatar that had been linked to human cases of the disease.

【14】The investigation has revealed that dromedary camels are so for the only reservoir of MERS-CoV . Adult dromedary camels have almost 100% seropositivity against MERS-CoV while the virus is found mainly in dromedary calves. In con-trast to human infection， MERS-CoV causes no or mild disease in dromedaries . Evidence in literature shows that there is a possibility of transition from camels to human & camels are the only confirmed zoonotic source for human infectionT. MERS is a zoonotic viral disease that can be trans-mitted from dromedaries to human beings in which it causes severe respiratory disease with a high case fatality . Sero-prevalence of MERS-CoV antibodies was significantly higher in camel-exposed individuals than in the general population. Epidemiological and genomic studies of cases associated with hospital and household MERS outbreaks have confirmed human to human transmission with a high risk of infection seen in patients with immunosuppression or coexisting illnesses. The rate of secondary transmission among house-hold contacts of the patient with MERS-CoV has been approxi-mately 5%.

【15】Regarding seasonality， it was previously hypothesized from the high incidence of cases during spring and early summer months， and this has been postulated that this may be correlated to the camel birthing pattern； young newborn camels are en-countering MERS-CoV for the first time may get ill and transmit the virus to humans. However， this hypothesis was nullified after outbreaks of MERS were spotted in the latter half of 2015& early 2016 in other seasons. An international analysis of the difference in outcomes for MERS cases has shown different fa-tality rates based on location. African & Middle East countries showed a MERS fatality rate of 41% whereas in Europe it was47% & Asian countries showed an atypical 20.3% case fatality.

【16】A. CASE DEFINITION

【17】The case definition for confirmed and suspected cases have been defined by WHO， the US centres for disease control and preven-tion and the ministry of health (MOH) of Saudi Arabia . A confirmed case is defined as any person with laboratory con-firmation of MERS - CoV infection based on positive real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) of MERS - CoV in swab samples collected by MOH in addition to any one of the fol-lowing clinical definitions： Fever (>38C)， a cough， shortness of breath (SOB). A sore throat， vomiting， diarrhoea， hemoptysis， chest pain and infection， respiratory failure， loss of conscious-ness， runny nose， and any asymptomatic outpatients with a history of contact with positive symptomatic cases are tested positive .

【18】B. IMMUNITY， PATHOGENESIS AND PATHOLOGY

【19】MERS-CoV primarily infects the human respiratory tract. It can effectively replicate in the airway epithelium of humans.

【20】Pulmonary endothelial cells are also highly susceptible to MERS-CoV. Human epithelial cells are stimulated to produce antiviral and pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokine to eliminate the invading pathogens. MERS-CoV infection failed to elicit strong pro-inflammatory cytokines response in human primary respiratory epithelial cells and ex vivo respiratory tissues. The virus has evolved multiple antagonistic mechanisms to dampen or attenuate the host defence which contributed to the high pathogenicity in humans . Type Iinterferon (IFN) expression is a crucial component of this initial POI response and coronaviruses have developed strategies to prevent IFN induction. Type I IFN activates immune antiviral effectors such as natural killer (NK) cells，T CD8+ cells and macrophages， allowing viral clearance. There is evidence to suggest consistent responsiveness of interferon treatment in vitro for MERS-COV .

【21】The human immune cells that are involved in MERS-CoV infection are macrophages， dendritic cells and T lymphocytes. In contrast to the inability to elicit the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines in human respiratory epithelial cells， MERS-CoV can stimulate the induction of pro-inflammatory cy-tokines/chemokine in human macrophages and dendritic cells. MERS-CoV is characterized by their different patterns of dis-ease； Sporadic cases， interfamilial transmission and healthcare-associated infection . There is also evidence to suggest the extrapulmonary organ involvement upon MERS-CoV infection. MERS-CoV viral RNA could be detected in blood， urine and stool specimens of some MERS patients suggesting viral dis-semination. MERS causes an acute highly lethal pneumonia. Renal dysfunction or failure is common in patients . The pathogenetic understanding comes from studies of experimen-tally infected animals. Studies have used several animals like macaques， marmosets and camels. Infected marmosets develop severe interstitial pneumonia and are a useful model to study severe MERS， but their unavailability limits their utility. Neu-trophil and macrophage infiltration and alveolar oedema have been reported from affected lung tissue . MERS mouse models have been generated by prior transduction of adenoviral vector expressing human DPP4. In the MERS-CoV permissible animal models， viral RNA can be detected from multiple organs of the infected animals. However， there was a failure in the recovery of the virus in most extrapulmonary organs .

【22】C. CLINCAL FEATURES

【23】The clinical manifestations of MERS-CoV infection range from asymptomatic infection to severe pneumonia with acute respi-ratory distress syndrome， septic shock， and multi-organ failure resulting in death .

【24】Common symptoms at presentation include fever with or without chills and rigour， cough， shortness of breath and myal-gia. Gastrointestinal symptoms are also frequent which includes diarrhoea， vomiting and abdominal pain . The median in-cubation period for a human to human transmission is approxi-mately five days . Two patients from France presented with similar clinical features which included fever， chills， and myal-gia. Respiratory symptoms with a cough and dyspnea soon became the predominant clinical symptoms. Both the patients were required ICU admission .

【25】Patients needing ICU admission usually presented with fever， abdominal pain，sore throat and fatigue. Crackles， tachycardia and rhonchi were the most commonly identified initial physi-cal signs. Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates lobar infiltrates also reported . Among the pediatric age group， the MERS-CoV infection rate is low . There is little data available regarding the effect and the likelihood of MERS-CoV in pregnancy. Eight cases have been reported， and the outcome was favourable in the majority of cases . The Risk factors for severity of disease are an immune compromised state， comorbidities like obesity， diabetes， cardiac disease and lung disease . Severe cases of MERS-CoV infection have tended to be recorded in older pa-tients with underlying conditions， while milder cases have been recorded in younger persons .

【26】D. LABORATORY DIAGNOSIS

【27】Lower respiratory tract specimen such as bronchoalveolarlavage fluid， sputum and tracheal aspirates contain the highest viral loads， and hence they should be collected whenever possible for viral detection . Real diagnostic time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) is done to detect MERS-CoV .

【28】Laboratory findings of MERS include Leucopenia， particu-larly lymphopenia， high creatinine， lactate dehydrogenase and liver enzyme concentrations . A single positive target can also confirm the presence of viral nucleic acid with the sequencing of a second positive PCR product . In MERS cases confirmed by PCR， serial sampling for PCR testing from the upper and lower respiratory tracts and another body part (e.g. Serum， urine & stool) are recommended to understand viral replication kinetics and to guide infection control. Genotype sequencing based assays for both the RNA dependent RNA polymerase gene (RdRp) and the N gene has also been developed. A sim-plified and biological safe protocol for the detection of antibody response by immunofluorescence microscopy has been devel-oped using the convalescent patient serum. Report of a highly specific assay for the detection of antibodies against MERS-CoV using protein microarray technology has also been developed . For confirmation of infection by antibody detection， the paired serum sample should be collected 14-21 days apart with the first taken during the first week of illness. A positive screening assay(ELISA， immune fluorescence assay) should be followed by a confirmatory (neutralization) assay. It is advisable that serologi-cal result should be carefully interpreted because they might be confounded by cross-reactivity against other coronaviruses . A monoclonal antibody (MAb)-based capture Elisa for MERS-CoV nucleocapsid protein (NP) detection which is an antigen detection Elisa has been reported .

【29】Another detection method is by using reverse transcription-loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP)， which requires only a single temperature for amplification and can be completed in less than 1 hour .

【30】E. TREATMENT

【31】There are no guidelines on the treatment of MERS-CoV infec-tion. Treatment with Interferon-a2b (IFN-a2b\] and ribavirin significantly improves survival 14 days after the diagnosis of MERS-CoV infection whereas another study of 5 patients diag-nosed later in the course of disease did not show any benefit. Supportive treatment is the mainstay of management as no specific drug treatment exists for MERS. MERS-CoV in inhib-ited by interferon type I in cultured cells. Several drugs inhibit MERS-COV in cell culture， like cyclosporine and mycophenolic acid . The usefulness of these drugs in a patient is unknown and needs further research. Combined therapy using ribavirin and IFN-a2b should be further evaluated as it has shown tore-duce clinical outcomes in MERS-CoV infected rhesus macaques . Resveratrol in another drug which has shown to inhibit MERS-COV infection and prolonged cellular survival after virus infection .

【32】F. PREVENTION & INFECTION CONTROL

【33】The Saudi ministry of health (MOH)， WHO and the US Cen-ters for Disease Control and Prevention have recommended preventive measures against MERS-CoV. The main prevention and control measures are droplet precautions， by wearing a sur-gical mask within 1 meter of patients and contact precautions which can be taken by wearing gown and gloves on entering patients rooms and removing them on leaving. Eye protection to be used by health care workers treating & monitoring the patient. Personal protective equipment such as gowns， gloves， eye protection and special N95 masks are recommended .

【34】If any patient has been exposed to a potential or known MERS case， travel should be avoided. Infection control aspect of MERS has to do with preventing MERS exposures and minimizing person to person spread . Without the ability to prevent community infection， prevention of health care transition will remain a challenge .

【35】CONCLUSION

【36】MERS is zoonotic which is transmitted to a human from infected dromedary camels.MERS-CoV is closely related to bat viruses with an unknown reservoir. The origin of MERS-CoV might have been in bats and transmitted to dromedary camels at the same point of time in the past. The transmission of MERS-CoV to humans needs further studies to clarify the role of any ampli-fying hosts or whether the virus transmitted from bats to camels& then to humans. Large scale serological screening of human populations in areas of MERS-CoV endemicity in dromedary camels should be considered . Surveillance should be conducted on a large scale among humans and different animal species to determine the exact rate of spread of MERS-CoV. Epidemiologi-cal research for the deployment of new therapies and vaccines are essential for both human and camels. In the absence of a vaccine or specific treatment， prevention of viral transition through adequate infection control methods is the mainstay in the management of MERS-CoV outbreaks.

【0】Background：

【1】Severe depression has been associated with a high rate of recurrence and chronic course. However， little is known about the course of depression in the very long term.

【2】Case Report：

【3】This study presents case reports of two women who had been admitted with severe depression in the 1950s and 1960s. The women， who had been inpatients at the Department of Psychiatry， Lund University Hospital， Lund， Sweden， were interviewed， and the interviews were supplemented with studies of their case records. They were considered to have met the criteria for major depressive disorder with melancholic or psychotic features.

【4】Both of them had experienced different numbers of episodes without full inter-episode recovery. They had also made repeated suicide attempts， at least one being serious. Their depressed peri-ods without full recovery lasted 16 and 29 years respectively. They then recovered and remained well for 30 and 25 years respectively.

【5】Conclusions：

【6】A long-lasting full recovery is possible， even after a chronic course of severe depression with repeat-ed suicide attempts.

【7】key words： depression· melancholia ·psychosis · long-term follow up

【8】Few studies have focused on the very long-term outcome in depression. It has been concluded that depression is a seri-ous condition associated with a high rate of recurrence . Furthermore， high rates of recurrence have been found even after five years of recovery  or in some cases 12-15 years after first admission . The risk of recurrence appears to remain  or even be constant over the life span .The number of previous episodes appears to be a risk factor for recurrence as estimated by re-hospitalisation 

【9】It has been shown that severity of depression is related to both duration and recurrence ofepisodes . Psychotic features have been related to more long-lasting episodes  and poor functional recovery . Residual sub-threshold depressive symptoms appear to be the first stage of a more severe， relapsing， and chronic future course .Socio-de-mographic variables such as gender， age at onset， and mari-tal status act as risk factors for re-hospitalisation early in the course . Later however， the illness itself seems to follow its own rhythm regardless of prior predictors that a chron-ic course is likely to develop. This corresponds with a “sen-sitisation”process over time as postulated by some authors. Consequently， severe depression， without full in-ter-episode recovery， would be expected to take a chronic course in many cases. However， an 18-year follow-up ofone case of chronic depressien reported recovery after 15 years and， in a 25-year follow-up， four chronic patients with a major depressive disorder recovered after the same time. Finally， one case of depression lasting for 30 years with initial severe symptoms， followed by recovery for 8 years， was described in 1957 

【10】The present study shows a positive outcome in depression with melancholic or psychotic features despite relapses and residual symptoms in two cases in a very long-term fol-low-up， 46 to 50 years after first admission. The patients’own stories as well as summaries from their case records are presented.

【11】CASE REPORTS

【12】Case history 1

【13】Selfreport

【14】Ms A， 80 years， lives alone in an apartment without home-help services. She is divorced， has three grown-up children， grandchildren and great-grandchildren. Her activities are limited because of back problems and an arthrosis. She takes no other medication than painkillers. She has always been restrictive with alcohol and has never smoked.

【15】Ms A states that she had a happy childhood. She describes her parents as warm and forgiving. She felt loved， wanted and safe even though her father was away from home most of the time and her mother was anxious. Her mother could be very dominant， just like her older sister， and Ms A de-scribes it as feeling that she was always in a submissive posi-tion. This continued later when she married her husband. He was also very dominant and clearly had alcohol prob-lems. They met when she was about to start university but he took all her time so she did not continue. He was easily irritable and Ms A always had to be on her guard to avoid making it worse. The bad marriage was the cause of Ms A’s depression. The pressure at home was very trying； she was always sad and became more and more depressed. At the age of 34， Ms A came into contact with psychiatry for the first time. The family moved to another town and the situa-tion at home worsened. Far away from relatives and friends Ms A was totally isolated and， without their support， she be-came increasingly worried and anxious. This led to her first hospitalisation at the age of 35. A year later she was hospi-talised again. By now she was separated from her husband. The depressive symptoms had worsened. Ms A says that she often wished to die and had suicidal thoughts in almost all her depressive periods， worst in the mornings. Once she made a suicide attempt by taking an excessive dose of med-ication. This resulted in her last hospitalisation at the age of 36. She was given ECT against her will and she describes it as “awful". She was then prescribed and stayed on anti-depressants but her mood swings continued. Some years later Ms A started psychotherapy， and she feels that helped her the most. She stopped taking antidepressants and has not taken any since then. She also finished her education， started to work and the support from colleagues and rela-tives meant a lot. For about 30 years Ms A has now been free from depressive symptoms， except for a situation two years ago when she had a hip operation and the painkillers she was given made her feel depressed again. When she stopped taking the medicine the symptoms disappeared.

【16】Case record

【17】Context and triggering factor： A bad marriage with a dom-inant husband with alcohol problems triggered the first depression.

【18】Clinical condition： Her home had fallen into decay. She sat stiffly， had a sad， empty facial expression， showed delayed re-sponse， and spoke in a low monotonous voice. She was non-vital， had little energy， and was apathetic. She complained of morning depression， but otherwise she was a warm and shy person. She expressed life-weariness， and she attempted sui-cide by intoxication on two occasions. The second attempt was serious. She was deeply unconscious， did not react to pain stimulation， and had dilated non-reactive pupils. She said afterwards that she could not stand it anymore.

【19】Diagnosis： Severe depression/melancholia according to multi-axial prospective ratings.

【20】Evolution and therapeutic acts： A life-chart is presented in Figure 1. She was admitted seven times over a two-year period， ranging from a couple of days up to four months. She continued as an outpatient for another two years at the Department. At first she was given a monoamine ox-idase inhibitor (Catran). After a year she was given tricy-clic antidepressants (first Imipramine， then supplemented with Amitryptiline) more or less continuously for two years. The doses were up to 100 mg for almost a year， followed by 150 mg for one year. She underwent two series of ECT， one after two years (seven seizures followed by continuation treatment with antidepressants) and another after 2% years. The second series was interrupted after four seizures due to confusion and suicidal thoughts. She was given neurolep-tics as a sedative， and other sedatives. One month after the suicide attempt she stopped taking the medication due to side-effects. She was considered to be in partial remission， but basically unwell， whenever she was discharged， until the final occasion when she was clearly in partial remission. She was supported in her divorce and continued in psychother-apy for several years. After that she recovered.

【21】Unexpected result： A long-lasting full recovery (30 years) was achieved after 16 years of illn ess without full remission.

【22】Case history 2

【23】Self-report

【24】Ms B， 78 years， lives in an apartment with her husband. She has three grown-up children， two of them from a previous marriage. She manages the household without problems. She takes several drugs for physical ailments， but no psycho-pharmacological drugs. She has always been a modest drink-er and has smoked， but stopped twelve years ago.

【25】Ms B did not have a very happy childhood. Her parents fa-voured her brother and sister， and her father used physical punishment. She was the “black sheep” of the family and always felt inferior to her siblings， but does have recollec-tions of kindness as well. She always felt put down and was also bullied by a teacher， but her father defended and sup-ported her on that occasion. She always had good friends. She married at the age of 22， had her first child the same year， and a second five years later. Her first marriage end-ed in divorce， as her husband met another woman. She re-married at the age of 33 and gave birth to a third child. She is still married to her second husband， but they are emo-tionally distanced.

【26】At the age of 25 she was depressed for the first time. This was followed by repeated depressive episodes and， over a period of 20 years， she was admitted ten times for depres-sion. She clearly improved between the episodes， but did not recover. She saw problems with in-laws as a cause of her depressions. She sometimes wanted to die， though not in every depressive episode， and made two suicide attempts. Once she took an overdose， but her neighbour called an am-bulance. She had even written a suicide note. On another occasion she went to the harbour intending to drown her-self but was stopped.

【27】Why she later suddenly recovered she does not really know. Taking up art may have contributed a great deal， she thinks. She started to paint pictures and to throw pottery. She has not taken any psychopharmacological drugs since the late1970s， and she has not needed any. She has not been de-pressed at all during the past 25 years.

【28】Case record

【29】Context and triggering factor： There was no clear trigger-ing factor for her first depressive episode， but she did not have a very happy childhood and her first marriage end-ed in divorce.

【30】Clinical condition： Depressive thoughts with excessive and inappropriate guilt were reported. A loss of pleasure was noted. There was significant psychomotor retardation with slowness in speech and eye movements. A lack of reactivity was described. She also imagined spiders on the wall and was terrified though she knew they were not real. Furthermore， she was paranoid and feared that there was an intruder in her apartment. At the age of 44 she was admitted after a suicide attempt by intoxication， which was considered as se-rious by her care-providers. Afterwards， however， she said that the suicide attempt was not serious but a response to ls.”F voices that said， “Take the pills， take the pills!" Previous re-peated intoxications are noted in the records. She also con-sidered hanging herself.

【31】Diagnosis： Severe depression/melancholia according to multi-axial prospective ratings.

【32】Evolution and therapeutic acts： The life-chart is present-ed in Figure 1. She first came into contact with psychiatry at the age of 25 and was admitted seven times between the ages of 25 and 42 for depression. At the age of 43 she start-ed outpatient contact that lasted for two years before she was admitted again at the age of 44 after a suicide attempt. After one more year of outpatient admissions she had no contact with psychiatry until the age of 50， when she was admitted again for one month.

【33】The first seven depressive episodes were treated with insu-lin coma on admission， and the eighth (at the age of 44) was treated with antidepressants when they became avail-able. She was given a full dose of amitryptiline (150-225mg) for a couple of months followed by continuation treatment for 18 months， doses that would be considered adequate. She was in partial remission when she was discharged on that occasion. She also had appointments with a psycholo-gist practitioner. On the last (ninth) admission she was giv-en a benzodiazepine. Taking up art and developing her ar-tistic talent was considered to be very significant for her self-esteem and recovery. She was considered improved but not recovered on her final discharge. A few years lat-er she recovered.

【34】Unexpected result： A long-lasting full recovery (25 years) was achieved after 29 years of illness without full remission.

【35】DISCUSSION

【36】Both women were regarded as having had severe depres-sion/melancholia according to the prospective multiax-ial ratings performed at the Department of Psychiatry， Lund University Hospital， between 1956 and 1969 . Retrospective diagnostics on a subsample according to the DSM-IV  from symptoms in the case records revealed very good correspondence with the criteria for major depres-sive disorders with melancholic or psychotic features . No case was secondary to or complicated by alcohol abuse， and neither of the women developed a bipolar disorder.

【37】Both women had made repeated suicide attempts， with at least one being serious. Basically aptimal treatment was giv-en for the most severe episode with antidepressants， in one case ECT and fin ally psychotherapy. There was no full re-mission between the episodes and both women were only in partial remission at the time of the final contact， but re-covered several years later. Their chronic depressive peri-ods lasted 16 and 29 years， after which they stayed well for30 and 25 years respectively.

【38】It appears that recovery may occur even late in the course of depression， despite relapses and residual symptoms be-tween the episodes， when follow-up is long enough. It is possible that sensitisation over a long period of time may actually be reversible. It remains to be shown whether this is due to adequate somatic or psychological treatment， so-cial support or some tendency for depression to “burn it-PPOIT self out". To our knowledge， there have been three previous studies that have shown late recovery in chronic depression， all of which support the outcome in the present cases. Woddis  described an unbroken attack of depres-sive psychosis lasting at least from 1918 to 1949. However， that attack of illness started in the pre-treatment era anda long stay in hospital might have contributed to the chronic outcome. These conditions are not comparable with condi-tions today. The second study  was shorter， a 25-year lon-gitudinal follow-up， and dealt with major depressive disor-der， i.e. less severe cases. The study by Lee and Murray reported one case of recovery after 15 years of continuing symptoms. However， these studies followed their cases less than a decade after recovery. A risk for recurrence later than that has been shown， chronic course not taken into account. The present study is a longer follow-up showing an even more long-lasting recovery. Finally， none of the pre-vious cases reported had made any suicide attempt， less so a serious attempt. Suicide attempts might indicate a poor-er prognosis but a long-lasting recovery appears to be pos-sible despite serious suicidal behaviour.

【39】There are two major limitations in the present study. Firstly， findings from a case study are not to be generalised and，sec-ondly， the retrospective nature of the interviews may lead to a recall bias. However， there is basically good correspon-dence between the personal retrospects：tive reports and the case records written at the time， and none of the subjects has had contact with psychiatry since.

【40】CONCLUSIONS

【41】We describe two cases of major depressive disorder with mel-ancholic or psychotic features. They both showed a chron-ic course， with duration of illness lasting 16 and 26 years re-spectively， without full inter-episode recovery. Both made repeated suicide attempts， one regarded as serious. They now have experienced 30 and 25 years of recovery， indicat-ing a possibility of long-lasting recovery in chronic severe depression with suicide attempts.

【0】ABSTRACT Background： The development of a pseudocyst after mesh repair of an incisional hernia is a rare complica-tion. Both diagnosis and management pose a great challenge to the attending surgeon. Therefore， the need to report such an uncommon complication and its management in order to create awareness of this distinct though rare entity. Case report： A pseudocyst formation following an onlay mesh repair of an incisional hernia is reported. Contrast-enhanced CT scan was diagnostic. It revealed a well-formed cyst with no communication with the peritoneal cavity. Complete excision of the cyst was curative. Conclusion： Pseudocyst formation is a rare complication following mesh repair. Contrast-enhanced CT scan is essential for confirming the diagnosis. Complete surgical resection of the cyst is the mainstay of surgical treatment.

【1】KEYWORDS Abdominal， pseudocyst， mesh repair， diagnosis， management

【2】Introduction

【3】Repair of incisional hernia is a commonly performed procedure. The common complications are wound infection， neuralgias and recurrence. The development of a pseudocyst around the mesh is an extremely rare complication. The true incidence is unknown as most cases go unreported or are missed.  Pseudocyst following a mesh repair was first described by Waldrep et al. in 1993.  They reported a cyst with a mature fibrous wall following a marlex mesh hernioplasty. A case of a pseudocyst following onlay mesh repair for an incisional hernia is presented.

【4】Case report

【5】A 62-year-old male patient presented with a large swelling in the lower part of the anterior abdominal wall. The swelling had increased over a period of time and was irreducible. The patient had undergone exploratory laparotomy seven years ago.

【6】He developed an incisional hernia two years after the laparo-tomy. He underwent repair for the same with an onlay mesh repair. The patient developed swelling at the repair site six months after the surgery. He underwent multiple aspirations of the swelling. However， the swelling did not resolve. This continued for two years. He was subsequently referred to our unit. On physical examination， the swelling was cystic in consis-tency. The overlying scarred skin was thinned out . A contrast-enhanced CT scan revealed a large well-circumscribed cystic swelling with a thick wall measuring 12 cms in diameter. There was no communication with the peritoneal cavity.  The patient underwent surgery. An elliptical incision was made， encompassing the cyst.

【7】The cyst was completely removed . The external oblique aponeurosis and midline were clearly seen. However， the previous mesh was not seen. A negative suction drain was placed under the flaps， and the skin was approxi-mated.  The drain tube was removed after seven days， and skin staples were removed on the twelfth postoperative day. The cyst contained amber-coloured fluid， but it did not grow any organisms. The histopathology of the cyst revealed fibrous tissue and chronic inflammatory cells. The patient has been following up for the last 16 weeks with no symptoms of any recurrence. 

【8】Discussion

【9】Onlay mesh placement for anterior abdominal wall incisional hernia repair is common. This is invariably followed by oozing， leading to the accumulation of blood and eventually leading to a formation of a seroma. There is a high likelihood of infection， especially in cases where multiple aspirations are done to clear the seroma. Most seromas are dealt with either by multiple sessions of aspiration or are best prevented by a negative suction drain placed in the dead space at the time of surgery.  Other complications include neuralgias， surgical site infections， mesh migration and hernia recurrence.

【10】Pseudocyst formation is an end result of an incompletely treated seroma. A mature fibrous tissue wall is formed around the mesh. In the case presented， the mesh was not seen. There is the possibility that the thick fibrous cyst wall may have con-tained the mesh which had homogenously blended with the fibrous tissue. This is usually caused either by either a long-standing hematoma or a seroma. Awareness of this rare com-plication is essential to prevent mismanagement.  Repeated aspiration of the cyst is futile and increases theincidence of infec-tion. Complete surgical resection is the mainstay of treatment.

【11】Complete cyst excision is essential to ensure that the entire fibrous wall is excised meticulously.  If left behind acciden-tally， it can lead to the persistence of symptoms. Surprisingly the engulfed mesh is not always found in the lesion. There is a high likelihood of developing a hernia on the same side later. Pseudocyst with an intra-peritoneal extension can also be dealt with laparoscopically.  But for pseudocyst involving the an-terior abdominal wall only， an open approach is advisable. It ensures complete resection of the cyst wall and any residual fibrous tissue in the adjacent soft tissues. 

【12】Conclusion

【13】Pseudocyst development after mesh repair is a rare complication. Awareness of this entity is essential to avoid misdiag nosis and delay in treatment. A contrast-enhanced CT scan is diagnostic as it helps identify the exact site， extent and presence of any peritoneal communication. Complete surgical excision of the cyst is the mainstay of the treatment.

【0】Background：

【1】In patients with large colon polyps， late-onset bleeding may be more likely to occur because of the larger cut-ting surface. In these patients， hemostatic agents may be applied to prevent the late-onset bleeding. A total of7 patients developed hypofibrinogenemia caused by hemocoagulase following excision of colon polyps in our center from November to December 2015.

【2】Case Report： Seven patients underwent excision of colon polyps in our center from November to December 2015. The cut- ting face was large in these patients after surgery； therefore， hemocoagulase was used to prevent potential late-onset bleeding. Evaluation of clotting function showed that the fibrinogen level was normal before sur-gery in all 7 patients. Hemocoagulase was intravenously administered twice daily beginning from postopera-tive day 1. Hypofibrinogenemia of varying severity occurred 2-4 d later. Three patients also had lower-gastroin-testinal bleeding. After drug withdrawal and infusion of fibrinogen， blood fibrinogen level gradually returned to normal. In contrast， among 13 patients who had not received hemocoagulase treatment for preventing hemor-rhage following excision of colon polyps， detection of blood fibrinogen before surgery and 2-4 d after showed normal results.

【3】Conclusions： Routine use of Hemocoagulase For Injection for the prevention of late-onset bleeding is not recommended for patients who have undergone excision of colon polyps. Hemocoagulase following excision of colon polyps can cause hypofibrinogenemia and even lower-gastrointestinal bleeding.

【4】MeSH Keywords： Afibrinogenemia· Colonic Polyps· Gastrointestinal Hemorrhage

【5】Late-onset bleeding may occur after excision of colon polyps， with an incidence of 0.2-2%. In patients with large colon pol-yps， late-onset bleeding may be more likely to occur because of the larger cutting surface. In these patients， hemostatic agents may be applied to prevent the late-onset bleeding. Many snake-venom-based hemocoagu lase products are available， including Reptilase， Hemocoagulase Atrox For Injection (based on ven-om of Bothrops atrox)， Hemocoagulase For Injection (based on venom of Agkistrodon halys \[pallas\])， Slounase (based on viper venom)， and Haemocoagulase Agkistrodon For Injection. A total of 7 patients developed hypofibrinogenemia caused by hemo-coagulase (Hemocoagulase For Injection) following excision of colon polyps in our center from November to December 2015.

【6】Case Report

【7】Twenty patients underwent excision of colon polyps in our cen-ter in the 2 months from November to December 2015.Among them， the cutting face was large in 7 patients after surgery； therefore， hemocoagulase was used to prevent potential late-onset bleeding. Evaluation of clotting function showed that the fibrinogen level was normal before surgery in all 7 patients. Hemocoagulase was intravenously administered twice daily beginning from postoperative day 1. Hypofibrinogenemia of varying severity occurred 2-4 d later . Three patients also had lower-gastrointestinal bleeding. After drug withdraw-al and infusion of fibrinogen， blood fibrinogen level gradual-ly returned to normal.

【8】In contrast， among 13 patients who had not received hemoco-agulase treatment for preventing hemorrhage following excision of colon polyps， detection of blood fibrinogen before surgery and 2-4 d after showed normal results .

【9】Apparently， there was a significant difference between the av-erage of pre-operation fibrinogen (Pre-op Fg) and post-opera-tion fibrinogen (Post-op Fg) in 7 patients with hemocoagulase administration. There was no significant difference between the average of Pre-op Fg and Post-op Fg in 13 patients with-out hemocoagulase administration.

【10】Discussion

【11】Hemocoagulase For Injection is a mixture of thrombin-like and thromboplastin-like enzymes that are isolated， purified， and prepared from the venom of Agkistrodon halys (pallas). The hemocoagulase acts only on the bleeding site and does not affect intravascular coagulation status. Thus， it has good tar-geting capability and does not trigger thrombosis. Thanks to its low required dosage and high safety， hemocoagulase has been widely used for visceral bleeding in departments of di-gestive medicine， respiratory medicine and neurology， and for controlling bleeding in various surgical procedures in depart-ments of otolaryngology and head and neck surgery. Except for occasional mild allergic reactions， no other adverse reac-tion has been reported .

【12】The thrombin-like and thromboplastin-like enzymes in the he-mocoagulase are similar enzyme substrates. They can directly act on the third phase of blood coagulation， promoting platelet aggregation at the site of vascular damage. Also， they release a series of clotting factors and platelet factors to degrade the Arg16-Glyl7 scissional bonds in the amino acid chain of fibrin-ogen . They can release fibrinopepide-A to form fibrin monomer l， but do not degrade fibrinopeptide B or directly ac-tivate coagulation factor XIII (fibrin stabilizing factor). As a re-sult， only unstable fibrin monomers form. These monomers can quickly be broken down in normal vessels； therefore， the risk of thrombosis is low after intravenous injection of hemo-coagulase. At the site of vascular injury， however， the instable soluble fibrin monomer I can be aggregated into fibrin I poly-mer and thus promote platelet aggregation， and accelerate platelet aggregation and thrombus formation， finally achiev-ing hemostasis at the site of vascular injury .

【20】Conclusions
