Abscess formation， fistulation， and adhesion formation were some of the common compli-cations arising from clip migration to other tissue sites， as re-ported by most studies， and the time to presentation varied from 6 weeks to more than 20 years following tubal ligation .

【23】To date， there are more than 24 case reports of Filshie clip migration to various sites of the pelvis， including the blad-der ， anterior abdominal wall ， peritoneal cavity ， co-lon ， vagina ， perianal region ， and groin ， most of which required surgical removal， especially in cases of ab-scesses. The urinary bladder is one of the most common sites of migration， with 5 other cases reported to date. Three cases had spontaneous urethral expulsion of the Filshie clip ， while the other 2 required surgical removal .

【24】The mechanism of clip migration is still not well understood， given normal pelvic anatomy at the time of sterilization. It has been postulated that the Filshie clip， despite being made from an inert material， induces a low-grade inflammatory response within the peritoneum， with subsequent adhesion formation， allowing its eventual erosion into the bladder wall . This is also supported by early studies in primates， showing that Filshie clips can induce a foreign body inflammatory response ， and this is clinically evident in the increased risk of ectopic pregnancy after tubal sterilization due to tissue reaction .

【25】The present report adds to the small but growing literature showing that clip migration is a rare but significant late com-plication following sterilization. It may mimic a bladder wall ab-scess or a tubo-ovarian abscess， as in our case. Women should be adequately counselled about the early and late risks of this popular method of female sterilization， especially with the de-layed symptomatic presentation of clip migration years later.

【26】Conclusions

【27】In conclusion， Filshie clip migration should be considered as a source of sepsis in the differential diagnosis of pelvic pain and fever in women with a history of tubal ligation. Women should be counselled regarding the significant risk of clip mi-gration (up to 25%)， although most remain asymptomatic. They should also be made aware of the potential rare late compli-cation of clip migration across tissues and its serious morbid-ity such as abscess formation， which can occur years later.

【0】ABSTRACT The prostatic urethral lift (Urolift @) is a new and increasingly popular minimally invasive treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia which is being offered instead of ablative or cavitating therapy. The procedure serves to pin aside the prostatic lobes to improve lower urinary tract symptoms. In this patient with a history of extensive implants， MRI was requested as part of his evaluation for a raised PSA. It became clear that the Urolift implant created a signal void which made it difficult to assess the entirety of the prostate gland radiologically. Patients who have had the procedure done and in whom an MRI is being sought should be counselled on the potential limitations and radiologists should be made aware of the implants.

【1】Background

【2】Multiparametric MRI scanning is taking on a more significant role in prostate cancer diagnostics. It is now part of the rou-tine diagnostic algorithm in many institutions as it has been shown to outperform traditional transrectal biopsy and improve the detection of clinically significant cancers . At the same time， the prostatic urethral lift has also gained traction in the management of benign prostatic hyperplasia. The procedure serves to pin aside the prostatic lobes to improvelower urinary tract symptoms. These pins are designed with a combination of a stainless-steel tab and nitinol memory alloy tab linked to-gether by a nonabsorbable suture. They are inserted through the Dy prostate to hold the tissue clear of the urethra. Intermediate-term data have supported the safety and efficacy of the procedure which can be performed under local anaesthesia and is associ-ated with substantially more tolerable side effect profile when compared to other more invasive options ，L. It is there-fore probably inevitable that their paths would intersect.

【3】The manufacturers of UroliftQ indicate that the device is MRI compatible but acknowledge that the Urolift Urethral Endplate does create an imaging artefact 10-15mm from the device. While other authors have also acknowledged this。 the practical implications in actual patients have not， to the best of our know1-edge， been previously described.

【4】Case Report

【5】A 79-year-old gentleman， in excellent health for his age， pre-sented with a history of lower urinary tract symptoms for sev-eral years. He complained of four to five episodes of nocturia and poor flow which was affecting his sleep. His International Prostate Symptoms Score was 9 with a Quality of Life score of 4and medical treatment with tamsulosin and finasteride had been ineffective at managing his symptoms. Two years earlier he had undergone prostatic urethral lift and during the procedure， five implants being inserted.

【6】On examination， his abdomen was soft and non-tender with no palpable masses. Digital rectal examination revealed a mod-erately enlarged prostate with a cT2 prostatic nodule on the right lobe. His prostate specific antigen was tested and found to be 3.3 ng/ml which， when adjusted for the finasteride treat-ment， rose to 6.6 ng/ml. Given the suspicious nodule associated with an elevated PSA， he was sent for a prostatic MRI. MRI re-vealed a 94-cc prostate with several signal voids in the central zone， precluding full assessment . The largest of these artefacts measured 2.5 x0.6cm on T2 weighted imaging. On diffusion-weighted imaging， the artefacts were much more apparent with the largest measuring 3.9cmx2.5cm， and these obscured most of the prostate at this level. Identification of the nature of the signal voids challenged our radiologist until these were identified as PUL implants.

【7】Nonetheless， an area classified as PIRADS-3 was identified centrally. Following discussion with the patient， he opted for a repeat MRI instead of biopsy. He has declined further invasive procedures， choosing instead for prostatic artery embolisation.

【8】Discussion

【9】The manufacturers of the device acknowledge the occurrence of the artefact and that it is magnified， as it was in our case， on diffusion-weighted imaging. Artefact-reducing MRI protocols are in the preliminary stages of development (personal commu-nication).

【10】It is clear that the signal void created by the device would take on greater significance in smaller glands， i.e. when the signal size to gland volume ratio is higher. It is also clear that these signal voids would be located in the central gland on imaging， leading one to question the implications of these findings given that most cancers are found in the peripheral gland. However， up to 30% of cancers have been noted in the central zone ， and so it is imperative that this zone is thoroughly assessed.

【11】Our patient was older， had a large gland， a mildly elevated PSA and a PIRADS -3 lesion - all factors which contributed to his decision to forgo biopsy. However， we appreciate that a diagnostic dilemma may ensue in a patient with different characteristics，i.e. smaller gland， younger age and a higher PSA. One suggested strategy is to fusion biopsy the artefact zone， i.e. to treat it as a lesion. This has significant practical implications for both physician and patient.

【12】Conclusion

【13】We remind readers that a history of prostatic urethral lift should be actively sought at the initial visit and relayed to the reporting radiologist. Until artefact reducing protocols are described， pa-tients who are undergoing PUL， and particularly those at high risk of prostate cancer in the future and younger patients， or those who have undergone PUL should be counselled on the potential limitation of MRI in this population， albeit however small.

【0】Background：

【1】Stump appendicitis is not a common condition and the diagnosis is often delayed. In most cases， making a preoperative diagnosis is quite difficult except where adequate investigative facilities are available. The purpose of this case report is to present our experience with a case of stump appen-dicitis and to highlight the difficulties in making a preoperative diagnosis of stump appendicitis.

【2】Case Report：

【3】The case file of a patient who had earlier had appendicectomy done by a general medical practi-tioner， but who now presented with features of recurrent right iliac fossa pain was reviewed. At op-eration， an inflamed appendix stump about 4 cm long was found. Patient had stump appendicec-tomy and had an uneventful post operative period.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Stump appendicitis is a rarely considered clinical condition. Adequate history and use of adequate investigative facilities should help in making a preoperative diagnosis. General medical practitioners should not carry out surgical procedures； instead， they should engage the services of a trained sur-geon to carry out surgical procedures.This can go a long way in reducing the incidence of stump appendicitis.

【6】key words： appendix stump· stump appendicitis · delayed diagnosis

【7】Nigeria

【8】Acute appendicitis is a common clinical diagnosis with several differential diagnoses. With a good clinical his-tory， examination and investigations， the physician is of-ten times able to exclude other differential diagnoses and make a fairly accurate diagnosis of acute appendici-tis. However， stump appendicitis is a rare clinical entity and preoperative diagnosis is often difficult to make de-spite adequate history， examination and investigations. Stump appendicitis is an acute inflammation of the residual appendix following appendicectomy. The signs and symptoms of stump appendicitis are about the same with those of appendicitis. However， there is often a con-siderable delay in reaching a diagnosis of stump appen-dicitis because of history of appendicectomy in the pa-tient . In developing countries； this diagnostic enigma is even worse where computerized tomography scan (CT scan) is not readily available. In the developed countries where CT scan is readily available， a preoperative diagno-sis of stump appendicitis could be made . There are few cases of stump appendicitis in the World literature. We report the case of a 37-year-old lady who presented with a history and clinical features of acute appendicitis. She however gave a history of having had appendicec-tomy seven years earlier. At operation， she was found to have stump appendicitis.

【9】CASE REPORT

【10】Mrs. O.A. is a 37-year-old patient who presented to the hos-pital with a chief complaint of abdominal pain for seven days. She is been having recurrent right lower quadrant abdominal pain in the last six months. Each episode re-sponded to analgesic and antibiotics she obtained from a patent medicine store. However， the index episode became more severe and not responsive to analgesic and antibiot-ics. The pain is said to be localized in the right lower quad-rant of the abdomen. The patient complained of anorex-ia and nausea after the pain started. There was no history of vomiting or alteration in bowel habit. She had appen-dicectomy seven years earlier in a private hospital man-aged by a general practitioner. Temperature was 37.9℃， blood pressure was 120/80 mmHg， pulse rate was 88 beats per minute and a respiratory rate of 20 breaths per min-ute.Abdominal examination revealed a healed McBurneys surgical incision scar. There was marked tenderness with rebound tenderness in the right iliac fossa. There was as-sociated muscular guarding. Rovsing's， psoas and obtura-tor signs were positive. The full blood count showed leu-cocytosis with neutrophilia. The B hCG was negative. The abdominal ultrasound scan showed a normal abdominal scan. An assessment of right iliac fossa tenderness to rule out the cause was made. With an index of suspicion， a di-agnosis of stump appendicitis was considered as a possibili-ty in this patient. The patient had surgery and the findings were that of a markedly inflamed appendix stump about 4cm long. There were lots of adhesions around the appen-dix stump and the omentum formed part of the adhesions. The adhesions were released and the patient had appendi-cectomy. The stitches were removed on the 7th post oper-ative day and the patient was discharged. The patient has been followed up for about a year and she has remained symptom free.

【11】There are several complications of appendicectomy However， stump appendicitis is rarely considered as a complication of appendicectomy. The first reported case of stump appen-dicitis was by Rose in 1945 and since that time， some other cases have been reported . Uludag et al did a litera-ture review when they reported a case of stump appendici-tis and found that as at 2006， there were 36 cases of stump appendicitis in the world wide medical literature .

【12】The true incidence and prevalence of stump appendicitis are not known， but it is thought to be an underreported en-tity in the literature . The age range of patients reported to have stump appendicitis is between ll and 72 years while the time interval between initial appendicectomy to stump appendicitis range from 2 months to 51 years . Our pa-tient was 37 years old at the time of presentation and the time interval between initial appendicectomy and the pre-sentation now was 7 vears.

【13】The main risk factor for stump appendicitis is when a long appendix stump is left behind after appendicectomy. Several reasons have been adduced why a long appendix stump may be left following appendicectomy . A difficult appen-dicectomy， especially when there are lots of adhesions and particularly with the inexperienced surgeon is a major rea-son why a long appendix stump may be left following ap-pendicectomy. In the patient presented in this paper， the initial surgery was done by a general practitioner.

【14】The length of the appendix stump ranges from 0.6 to 6.5 cm. The length of the appendix stump in our patient was4 cm. Mangi and Berger reported that leaving an appendi-ceal stump less than 3 mm in depth with accurate visualiza-tion of the appendiceal base， can minimize the incidence of stump appendicitis .

【15】Burying the appendix stump in a caecal wall purse string with Lembert seromuscular sutures have been a matter of great controversy over the years. While some surgeons be-lieve that burying the appendix stump can reduce the in-cidence of stump appendicitis， others have a contrary view. Rao et al. showed that all cases reported in the lit-erature undergo simple ligation of the appendix withoutin-vagination of the stump， suggesting that simple ligation with failure to amputate the appendix close to its origin from the caecum is a prerequisite for developing stump appendici-tis . The appendix stump in the case we reported was not buried. In the review of 2185 of appendicectomies by Mangi and Berger， there was no correlation between simple ligation and stump appendicitis . The possible explana-tion for this is that to leave the stump long may cause diffi-culty with burying the stump and consequently， the length of the appendix stump may warn the surgeon.

【16】Presently， laparoscopic appendicectomy is now a widely ac-cepted surgical technique in treating appendicitis and some studies have indicated that this technique may increase the incidence of stump appendicitis . Some of the rea-sons adduced for this are related to the inherent limita-tions oflaparoscopic surgery such as smaller fields of vision， absence of depth perception and absence of tactile feed-back. A combination of these factors may result in a long stump being left behind. In the reported 36 cases of stump appendicitis， only 10 had stump appendicitis after laparo-scopic appendicectomy. However， no definite relationship has been established between laparoscopic appendicecto-my and stump appendicitis.

【17】There are a number of differential diagnoses for a right iliac fossa pain. Appendicitis is one of such differentials. However， after appendicectomy appendicitis is hardly ever considered in making a list of differential diagnosis. Consequently， making a diagnosis of stump appendicitis is often delayed and may only be detected at operation when there are already associated complications. The use of CT scan may however help in making a preoperative diagno-sis and so reduce the period of waiting before a diagng-sis is made 3.12. However， CT scan is not readily available in most developing countries and where available， most pa-tients are unable to afford the prohibitive cost. The use of ultrasonography has been used in few instances to make a preoperative diagnosis of stump appendicitis， but the diag-nostic accuracy is not as good as CT scan . Thus， in the developing countries， making a preoperative diagnosis of stump appendicitis will depend on a good clinical history and a high index of suspicion.

【18】CONCLUSIONS

【19】In conclusion therefore， it is to be noted that in a patient who has had appendicectomy， but now present with symp-toms and signs of appendicitis， stump appendicitis should be considered as a possible differential diagnosis； a normal abdominal ultrasound scan notwithstanding. General med-ical practitioners should not carry out surgical procedures. They should engage the services of a trained surgeon to car-ry out surgical procedures. This will go a long way in reduc- ing the incidence of stump appendicitis and its asseciated morbidity and mortality.

【0】Background： Peritoneal tuberculosis is very rare in European countries. However， its incidence is increasing due to the con-tinued immigration of people from endemic areas affected by tuberculosis.

【1】Case Report： The authors report a case of tuberculous peritonitis in a 46-year-old male patient from North Africa. The pre-senting symptoms of the disease were hiccups， dyspepsia， anorexia， and weight loss. Physical examination re-vealed an abdominal distension that suggested the presence of ascites. Subsequent investigations of ultraso und and computed tomography of the abdomen revealed the presence of massive ascites. A diagnostic laparoscopy went on to highlight a macro micronodular degeneration of the peritoneum. Histological examination showed the presence of epithelioid granulomas with typical Langhans cells with areas of caseous necrosis. The diagno-sis of tuberculous peritonitis was then made， and the ascites quickly disappeared in response to the anti-my-cobacterial therapy. The patient remained free of symptoms after 6 months of clinical follow-up. Conclusions： In this case the clinical diagnosis was complicated and delayed due to clinicians' suboptimal knowledge of and experience with this disease. This case demonstrates why laparoscopy with peritoneal biopsy should be the gold standard in any clinical suspicion.

【2】Key words： tuberculous peritonitis · hiccup and ascites \* ultrasound tomography and computed tomography scan· diagnostic laparoscopy \* ascitic fluid cytology Tuberculosis causes approximately 3 million deaths per year worldwide and is increasing in incidence in developed and developing countries. Abdominal tuberculosis， which may in volve the gastrointestinal tract， peritoneum， lymph nodes or solid viscera， constitutes up to 12% of extrapulmonary TB and about 3% of the total cases . The disease can mimic many conditions， including inflammatory bowel disease， malignan-cy，and other infectious diseases .

【3】Diagnosis is therefore often delayed， even though it is known that the peritoneum is one of the most common extrapulmo-nary sites of tuberculous infection .

【4】The clinical case presented here explains the clinical aspects and diagnostic problems with the management of patients with tuberculous peritonitis.

【5】Case Report

【6】The patient reported having suffered 4-6 months from a re-lentless hiccup，irregular dyspeptic illness， a lack of appetite， a tense (but not painful) abdomen， and weight loss. He did not report fever or sweating. The examination showed the pres-ence of hard， non-painful， bilaterally enlarged lymph nodes in the inguinal and axillary sites， and abdominal distension that suggested an ascitic fluid collection. No cardiovascular signs or symptoms were present. An abdominal ultrasound exami-nation  confirmed the presence of ascites， but there was no enlargement of the liver or the spleen. In summary， an ascitic fluid collection with no signs of portal hyperten-sion was present. The patient was admitted to the hospital， where further diagnostic procedures were performed includ-ing： an esophagogastric-duodenoscopy (OGD-scopy) showing signs of Helicobacter pylori and erosive gastritis， and colonos-copy showing a villous adenoma with low-grade dysplasia. A chest and abdomen CT scan  revealed bilateral api-cal scarring of the lung parenchyma and absence of hilar and mediastinal lymphoadenomegaly， and confirming the pres-ence of abundant ascitic fluid. No significant alterations were seen in the other organs. Blood tests showed normochromic and normocytic anaemia (Hgb 10.6 gr/dl)， low iron， and nor-mal ferritin. Transaminases were slightly high， and indexes of inflammation were consistently high， with CRP values be-tween 3.4 and 4.3 mg/dl， D-Dimer 1187 ng/ml， and ESR 42. A Mantoux intradermal reaction was positive (8 mm)， but an HIV test， tumor markers， and serologies for hepatitis were nega-tive. The following test results were normal： rheumatoid test (anti-nuclear antibodies)， antimitochondrial antibodies， anti-smooth muscle antibody， liver-kidney-microsome antibodies， and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmatic antibodies)， antiphospho-lipid antibodies， and circulating immunocomplex and comple-ment factors. Examination of the ascitic fluid was positive to alkaline reaction， and the Rivalta test showed a protein con-tent of 65.3 g/l. Microscopic examination of the sediment re-vealed the presence of erythrocytes， leukocytes with predomi-nantly mature lymphocytes (lymph：80%)， and a total amount of polymorphonuclear leukocytes of 1100 n°/mmc. Direct bac-terioscopy and cultures for mycobacteria were consistently negative. Cytological analysis for atypical cells was negative.

【7】The average albumin in the ascitic fluid was 3.2 g/dL， and the average albumin in the serum was 2.8 g/dl； therefore， the se-rum ascitic albumin gradient (SAAG) was 0.4 g/dl.

【8】M. tuberculosis PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)， performed in a laboratory at another local hospital， was negative. A biopsy of 2 small lymph nodes in the left inguinal side showed only aspecific reactive inflammation. The patient was discharged from the hospital after 32 days， with a diagnosis of“ascites of uncertain nature and signs of inflammation". Radiographic examination of the small intestine was negative. A laparos-copy with directed peritoneal biopsy， which is thought to be the best diagnostic procedure for tuberculosis peritonitis， was subsequently performed at another hospital. Laparoscopy of the abdomen revealed large macro-and micro-nodular degen-eration of the visceral and parietal peritoneum， and the pres-ence of plaques and omental thickening， interpreted macro-scopically to be similar to a massive peritoneal carcinomatosis.

【9】Histological examination of the peritoneal biopsies showed epithelial granuloma with the presence of Langhans-type gi-ant cells and a wide area of caseous necrosis， but without ac-id-fast bacilli Figure 3). Cytological examination of the ascitic fluid showed the presence of inflammatory cells， predomi-nantly lymphocytes， monocytes， and a small number of poly-morphonuclear cells， similar to Langhans cells . The patient was dismissed with a final diagnosis of massive peri-toneal tuberculosis. During the short period (15 days) of hos-pitalization in the Infectious Disease Department， the patient was started on a 4-drug regimen of isoniazid， rifampicin， pyra-zinamide， and streptomycin. During the final stay in the hospi-tal， direct examination and cultures of urine， feces， and sputum for mycobacteria were performed， but all results were nega-tive. After administration of the last treatment with strepto-mycin， the patient was dismissed in good general condition， with maintenance therapy and a follow-up protocol.

【10】Discussion

【11】Abdominal tuberculosis has diverse and non-specific symptoms. No single test is adequate for the diagnosis of abdominal tuber-culosis in all patients. Diagnosis of abdominal TB in non-HIV-positive patients remains an ongoing dilemma requiring a high index of clinical suspicion. Tuberculous peritonitis (TP) con-stitutes up to 1% of all causes of ascites. TP is an exceptionally rare disease in the Western world， but is still present in Africa and developing countries， where most young females are af-fected . Abdominal tuberculosis can be diagnosed by culture growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in the ascitic fluid， or the presence of caseating granuloma， with or without positive smear for acid-fast bacilli， in biopsy specimens obtained by laparoto-my. Laparoscopy with directed biopsy is currently the best way to make a rapid， specific diagnosis . A diagnosis of tubercu-lous peritonitis is highly probable if the patient responds to an-tituberculous drug treatment with no recurrence. PCR analyses for the M. tuberculosis complex in ascitic fluid is a rapid test to obtain a diagnosis， but with low accuracy. Ascitic fluid ade-nosine deaminase (ADA) activity has been proposed as a use-ful diagnostic test for abdominal TB with good accuracy .It is known that tuberculous peritonitis often manifests without any evidence of other sites of tuberculous infection . In our patient， the signs and symptoms observed were generally con-sistent with those of other reports on the presence of ascites. As reported in the literature， a positive result from the Mantoux test is another diagnostic sign . Moreover， the presence of pre-dominantly lymphocytes in the ascitic fluid and polymorphonu-clear leukocytes in amounts up to 250 cells/mm are evidence of infection. The majority of cases reported in the literature， like our report， were diagnosed via laparoscopy with directed bi-opsy of the peritoneum . Even though it is a relatively rare disease， abdominal tuberculosis requires a high index of clini-cal suspicion， particularly in case of ascites of uncertain nature without signs of portal hypertension  and cardiac insuffi-ciency， and in the presence of lymphocytes in the ascitic fluid and a serum ascitic albumin gradient (SAAG) of less than 1.1g/dl. A delay in diagnosis can be fatal . Abdomina. tuber-culosis must be suspected if the patient is from countries with a high prevalence of the disease， for example African countries such as Morocco . In accordance with our clinical report，the gold standard for diagnosis of peritoneal tuberculosis infection is laparoscopic surgery with peritoneal biopsy .

【12】This technique allows examination and exploration of the peri-toneum， and， particularly， the ability to obtain bioptic specimens for the subsequent histological examination (necessary for a definitive diagnosis and specific therapy ). The only treat-ment for peritoneal tuberculosis is pharmacological.

【13】The first-choice regimen is represented by 5 drugs： isonia-zid， rifampicin， pyrazinamide， ethambutol， and streptomycin. The efficacy of the therapy is determined by the resolution of symptoms and the disappearance of ascites. A delay in initi-ating therapy has been associated with higher mortality rates. Although the current recommendations on the duration of therapy suggest a pharmacological treatment of 6 months， other studies suggest continuing therapy for 12 months. The only study that has compared different times oftherapy (9 to12 months) found no difference in the outcome between the2 groups . After 2 months of treatment for tuberculosis， our patient showed a significant improvement in his general condition； markers of inflammation returned to normal and ascites disappeared almost completely.

【14】We are thus confident that， given the favorable evolution of the disease， the prognosis for our patient is now good. The treatment of our patient with standard antituberculous ther-apy for 6 months should lead to definitive recovery.

【15】Conclusions

【16】Peritoneal tuberculosis is particularly uncommon in European countries. However， its incidence is growing due to the contin-uous immigration of people from tuberculosis endemic areas.

【17】As a consequence， the diagnosis of this disease is not immedi-ate or easy in those countries where peritoneal tuberculosis is thought to have been eradicated. In the case report described， the clinical presentation of the disease is fairly original. In the first phase there was incurable hiccupping， which proved to be the main clinical sign of the course of the illness during treatment.

【18】It is clear that the diagnostic gold standard of non-specifical-ly diagnosed ascitic effusion is laparoscopy with a possible bi-opsy； however， in this case peritoneal tuberculosis might also have been hypothesized on the basis of anamnesis and as-citic effusion， and， above all， on the basis of the presence of lymphocytes in the exudates. Peritoneal biopsy was only per-formed in a second phase for diagnostic certainty， because during the first hospitalization no diagnosis had been made and the patient had been discharged with generic instructions and with no indications of any specific treatment.

【19】Conclusions

【20】In conclusion， this case study may be an example of the diffi-culty of diagnosing peritoneal tuberculosis， and explains why it should include laparoscopy with peritoneal biopsy as the gold standard in any cases of clinical suspicion. Furthermore， in the case considered， it is clear that the semiological marker was represented by the ascites and， above all， by the persisten-cy of the hiccuping， which gradually disappeared during anti-tubercular therapy and with the improvement of the ascites.

【21】Abbreviations

【22】TB -tuberculosis； TP-tuberculous peritonitis； CRP-C-reactive protein； OGD-scopy - esophagogastroduodenoscopy； ESR -erythrocyte sedimentation rate； SAAG -serum ascitic albumin gradient； PCR-polymerase chain reaction；ADA - ascitic fluid adenosine deaminase； HIV- human immunodeficiency virus.

【0】Background

【1】Lemierre’s disease， also known as the forgotten disease， post-anginal sepsis， or necrobacillosis， was first reported in 1890 by Courmont and Cade ， but it was Dr. Andre Lemierre， a pro fessor of microbiology， who described this disease in 1936.

【2】He published a case series of 20 patients with a syndrome char-acterized by a history of recent oropharyngeal infection， clini-cal or radiological evidence of internal jugular vein thrombosis， and anaerobic septicemia caused primarily by Bacillus funduli- formis (now known as Fusobacterium necrophorum). Lemierre’s disease is now a rare illness with less than 100 cases report-ed since 1974 . Fusobacterium species are responsible for majority of the cases. F. necrophorum is a gram-negative anaerobic rod that is a part of the normal oropharyngeal flo-ra . It is poorly understood what causes this typically non-invasive organism to penetrate mucosal surfaces， but it has been suggested that alteration of pharyngeal mucosa by viral or bacterial pharyngitis may play a role . Before the intro-duction of antibiotics， Lemierre’s disease was frequently en-countered and often fatal. The fatality rate in the pre-antibi-otic era was close to 90%， and has decreased to 15% in the current era of antimicrobials.

【3】Case Report

【4】A 25-year-old man with no past medical history and an unre-markable social history presented to the emergency depart-ment (ED) with complaints of scalp and cheek swelling for 2days. He was evaluated in the ED， prescribed oral antibiotics， and discharged home. He failed to get his prescriptions and4 days later presented again to the ED with new-onset neck swelling and pain.

【5】On admission， his temperature was 38℃， the heart rate was115 beats per minute (bpm) with a respiratory rate of 18 per minute and blood pressure of 140/79 mmHg. There was dif-fuse edematous swelling of the left side of the neck with min-imal tenderness. The oropharynx was not infected and there were no obvious dental caries or abscess. The uvula was cen-tral in position. The remainder of the examination was unre-markable. Initial investigation revealed a total white count of27 900/cmm， hemoglobin of 14.4 g/dl， and platelet count of140 000/cmm. An electrocardiogram revealed sinus tachycar-dia at 106 bpm with no acute ST-T wave changes. Blood cul-tures were drawn and the patient was empirically started on ampicillin/sulbactam. On day 1 of admission， a CT scan of the neck/soft tissues was obtained， which showed a retropharyn-geal hypodensity representing early abscess formation； near occlusive thrombus of left internal jugular vein extending from jugular foramen to C ； small non-occlusive thrombus in the right internal jugular vein at the C. level， and marked dural/epidur-al enhancement of the cervical spine. He was therefore also started on anticoagulation with unfractionated heparin (UFH). A CT chest/abdomen/pelvis was done， which revealed multi-ple bilateral pulmonary nodules with signs of early cavitation. Based on the clinical presentation and radiograph-ic findings， the diagnosis of Lemierre's disease was made.

【6】Despite antibiotics， the patient continued to have high-grade fever of 38.9℃ On day 2 of admission， blood cultures re-vealed Staphylococcus aureus， which was subsequently iden-tified as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Ampicillin/sulbactam was discontinued and patient was started on IV vancomycin (maintaining higher trough levels). A trans-thoracic echocardiography performed on day 2 of hospitaliza-tion did not reveal any valvular vegetation.

【7】The patient complained of persistent headache and back pain. He underwent brain MRI that revealed an ovoid region ofT， and T， prolongation， restricted diffusion， and peripheral enhance-ment measuring approximately 2.2 cm within the parietal ver-tex scalp with surrounding soft tissue enhancement sugges-tive of soft tissue abscess. A CT angiogram of the head/neck revealed focal aneurysmal dilatation of the left vertebral ar-tery at the C level， likely representing a mycotic aneurysm； prevertebral phlegmonous changes with nonocclusive throm-bus in the left internal jugular vein； and thrombus extending from left transverse sinus to left sigmoid dural venous sinus. Cervical thoracic lumbosacral spine imaging revealed a large circumferential epidural collection at C-C level with near complete effacement of the thecal sac and left ventro-lateral epidural abscess extending from T-T， level measuring8x14x31 mm with no evidence of spinal cord compression.

【8】Neurosurgery was consulted and suggested no acute inter-vention. At the time of discharge， vancomycin was continued for a total of 6 weeks via a peripherally inserted central cath-eter. UFH was changed to warfarin bridging with low molecu-lar weight heparin (LMWH) until INR was therapeutic.

【9】Discussion

【10】In his original case series， Lemierre stated “The appearance and repetition several days after the onset of a sore throat(and particularly of a tonsillar abscess) of several pyrexial at-tacks with an initial rigor， or still more certainly the occurrence of pulmonary infarcts and arthritic manifestations， constitute a syndrome so characteristic that mistake is almost impossi-ble” . Currently， Lemierre’s disease is rare. Its incidence has been estimated be approximately 3.6 cases per million per year . An increase in its incidence has been reported since the 1990s by several authors  due to increased aware-ness of the syndrome and more judicious antibiotic use for treatment of bacterial pharyngitis . It primarily affects pre-viously healthy children， adolescents， and young adults .

【11】Lemierre’s disease is characterized by a primary oropharyn-gealinfection associated with septicemia， internal jugular vein thrombosis， and metastatic septic emboli. The lung is the most common metastatic focus. The primary focus of infection in Lemierre’s disease is usually pharyngitis， and rarely other sourc-es like odontogenic infection， sinusitis，mastoiditis， and paroti-tis . The infection then invades the peritonsillar tiss ue and spreads to the lateral pharyngeal space (containing the jugular vein) via lymphatics causing septic thrombophlebitis.

【12】Diagnostic points favoring Lemierre’s disease are a primary source of infection in the oropharynx， positive blood cultures， radiographic evidence of jugular vein thrombosis， and at least one metastatic focus.

【13】The typical causative agent is the gram-negative anaerobic ba-cilli Fusobacterium necrophorum ， but other organisms like Streptococcus， Staphylococcus (as demonstrated in our case)， Eikenella， and Peptostreptococcus have also been found.

【14】Fusobacterium is a commensal organism of the oropharynx， di-gestive tract， and female genital tract . The cause of tran-sition from commensal to virulent phenotype could be a result of a viral or bacterial throat infection that diminishes local im-mune defense mechanisms in the oropharynx， thus allowing mucosal bacterial invasion. Subsequent to mucosal invasion， several factors， including hemolysin， lipase， and leukotoxin， contribute to bacterial pathogenicity j. Platelet aggregation is a virulent property of Fusobacterium that causes thrombo-cytopenia， disseminated intravascular coagulation， and fibrin deposition . Like Fusobacterium， MRSA also has the abili-ty to produce platelet aggregation. Analogy between Panton-Valentine leukocidin (produced by MRSA) and virulence factor(produced by Fusobacterium) is one of the probable explana-tions for the ability of both these organisms to cause Lemierre's disease. Spread of the bacteria to the cervical region results in thrombosis of internal jugular vein or one of its tributaries.

【15】Hematogenous seeding of the disease to distant sites occurs following involvement of the internal jugular vein. Lungs are the most common metastatic focus， presenting as necrotic cavitary lesions ， but cases with pleural effusion， lung ab-scess， and necrotizing mediastinitis have also been reported . The second-most common site of septic emboli-zation is the large joints： shoulders， hips， and knees . Although atypical， cases of splenic abscess， liver abscess， re-nal abscess， hemolytic uremic syndrome， and pericarditis have also been reported . Central nervous system (CNS) complications are rare because cerebral veins are located up-stream from the IV. Nonetheless， subdural empyema ， cerebral infarcts ， meningitis ， encephalop-athy ， and cavernous sinus thrombosis have been report-ed， with the probable mechanism being retrograde extension of lV thrombosis First described by Osler in 1885， mycotic aneurysms show a dis-tinct infectious pathologic process . They can develop as a result of： septic emboli， which tend to lodge at branching points of distal vessels， infecting and weakening the arterial wall ； contiguous inflammatory processes， which cause an infective aneurysm by involving the vasa vasorum and periarterial lym-phatics ； or following an iatrogenic vascular complication precipitating infection in the arterial wall . We did an ex-tensive literature search and， to date， mycotic aneurysm of the vertebral artery in association with extensive metastatic seed-ing secondary to Lemierre’s syndrome has never been reported.

【16】Use of anticoagulation in Lemierre's disease remains contro-versial . The risks and benefits of anticoagulation should always be individualized. Despite inconsistent results in ran-domized trials， our patient was successfully anticoagulated(thrombosis of cavernous sinus is regarded as an indication for anticoagulation， as demonstrated in our case ，with UFH and later with LMWH and warfarin. Surgical intervention

【17】Conclusions

【18】Lemierre’s disease is a rare and perplexing medical entity. Clinical suspicion should be high in previously healthy young adults presenting with fever and neck pain following oropha-ryngeal infection. It is quite possible that the initial oropha-ryngeal infection could have resolved by the time the patient presents to the hospital， or there could be few or no findings on physical examination. Hence， Lemierre’s disease should always be considered as one of the differential diagnoses in a patient with pharyngitis and neck pain， even without the presence of any obvious complications of Lemierre’s disease(UV thrombosis and pulmonary complications). Mycotic aneu-rysms develop as a result of septic emboli in Lemierre's disease. Prognosis of patients with Lemierre’s disease is generally good， provided prompt recognition and appropriate treatment.

【0】ABSTRACT Quality of life has been studied in its multiple aspects. This includes characteristics of populations， influence of health promotion and disease prevention. Considering that we have not yet reached a level of excellence with regard to the quality of life of the elderly， we have to point out the factors to overcome the negative aspect of the disease or illness. In this sense， the objective of the research was to evaluate the quality of life of the elderly， based on a combination of factors that overcome the negative aspect of the disease， emphasizing the relationship of psychological behavioral processes in a space that facilitates the practice of physical activity. Methodology： A descriptive， observational and quantitative study was carried out. The sample consisted of 90 elderly people， 74 (82.2%) female and 16 (17.8%) male. The inclusion criteria were： being 60 years old or older， having preserved cognitive ability and proven physical activity practices in the area of social support and health promotion and disease prevention from the Social Service of Industry， in the municipality of Sao Bernardo do Campo， Sao Paulo， Brazil， between January and December 2011， in the municipality of Sao Bernardo do Campo， Sao Paulo， Brazil. For data collection， the WHOQOL -Bref， the Socioeconomic Assessment Scale-ABIPEME and a questionnaire covering the aspects： physical (domain1)，psychological (domain2)， social relations(domain3)， environment (domain4)， socioeconomic level and sociodemographic data. The results achieved indicated that the quality of life of the elderly is related to several factors such as economic condition， education， social and leisure opportunities in spaces that facilitate the practice of physical activity.

【1】KEYWORDS Quality of Life； Health Promotion； Prevention of diseases

【2】Introduction

【3】Population aging is a trend in Brazil， since the number of people aged 60 or over represents about 11% of the total population . Recent projections indicate that Brazil will be the sixth world population with the largest number of elderly people， in Which brings with it numerous problems， in the scope of health services， since the challenges， diseases and restrictions of this population profile tend to be characterized by health problems，sadness， and by chronic， degenerative conditions and their association with constant， long treatments. Hospitalization and rehabilitation periods .

【4】Thus， in the context of old age， there are implications for self-care， making quality of life vulnerable due to physical capacity and the presence of pathological disorders. However， epi-demiological studies have shown that diseases and limitations can be prevented in the aging process .

【5】From these considerations， it is possible to reflect on health behaviors， based on an ecological approach that values the per-son's relationship with the world， or with their surroundings：cultural， social and physical， existing or perceived by the elderly . In this perspective， the present study evaluates the quality of life of the elderly and a combination of factors that overcome the negative aspect of the disease or illness so that aging in Brazil occurs as a positive experience.

【6】Methodology

【7】This study was developed through a descriptive， observational analysis， of the quantitative type composed by elderly people monitored in the area of social support and health promotion and disease prevention of the Social Service of Industry， in the municipality of Sao Bernardo do Campo， Sao Paulo， Brazil， be-tween January and December 2011， in the municipality of Sao Bernardo do Campo， Sao Paulo， Brazil. For this， 90 elderly peo-ple were evaluated，74(82.2%) of whom were female and 16(17.8%) using the following instruments I， II and ⅡII：

【8】I-WHOQOL-Quality of Life Bref of the World Health Or-ganization (WHO)， to measure Quality of Life. It consists of 26questions to assess the global Quality of life (QVB)， divided into four domains， namely： physical (gift 1)， psychological(gift 2)， social relations (gift 3) and environment (gift 4) . ⅡI-Socio-economic Evaluation Scale of the Brazilian Association of Market Research Institutes- ABIPEME. II-Questionnaire for the Characterization of the Sample， which included gender， education， frequency of use of the area of social support and health promotion and disease prevention of the Social Service of Industry -Brazil.

【9】Statistical analyzes

【10】For data interpretation， statistical analyzes were performed us-ing the SPSS -Statistical Package for the Social Science， version15.0 for Windows. Descriptive statistical measures of quanti-tative variables and tables were used to describe the sample studied. Sociodemographic variables， global quality of life and the four domains that make up quality of life were analyzed using the anova test and the Tukey test. ANOVA is a table of analysis of variance for comparisons between groups and the Tukey test is the verification of the internal consistency of each group of variables.

【11】Results

【12】Ninety elderly people were interviewed， most of them were female (82.2%) and only 17.8% were male. Of the total sample，35.5%(n=32) had complete primary education and the small-est part of the elderly had university education 4.4% (n=4)， followed by primary education 5.5%(n=5).

【13】The remaining answers can be distributed as follows： 30.0%did not study complete high school and 24.4% studied until complete high school.

【14】There is no reference to economic class， most of the elderly38.9% belong to class E and class D 32.2%. The smallest part of the elderly 3.3% belongs to class B， followed by class C 25.6%.

【15】Regarding physical activity， the data show that 27.8% practice fitness and the least 8.9% use water aerobics. As for the others，21.1% practiced walking and 18.9% did recreational activities，13.3% did gymnastics and 10% did stretching. In addition， it was observed that 67.8% prefer to attend the Social Service of Industry - Brazil， in the morning and 32.20% prefer to attend the place in the afternoon. It is worth mentioning that there was no response during the night.

【16】As for the reason that leads the elderly to attend Social Ser-vice of Industry-Brazil， the data revealed that the majority of the elderly 51.2% go to the place to promote health and prevent diseases. The second biggest reason 23.3% is the proximity / ac-cessibility of the place. The smallest part of the elderly frequents the place due to the physical environment and other reasons7.7% followed by the condition of use 17.8%. These indexes may suggest a local brand as a source of health promotion for the elderly. The scores of the sociodemographic characteristics of the elderly in each criterion are defined in table 1.

【17】Through the analysis of the collected data， it was possible to verify the factors that lead the elderly to perform physical exercises among the socioeconomic classification .

【18】The data， presented in table 2， suggest that people who be-long to classes D and E attend Social Service of Industry -Brazil， for the pleasure of being in the place. Class C people， on the other hand， attend Social Service of Industry -Brazil， to prevent diseases. 【27】Discussion

【28】The recommendation made by Patrick； Deyo ， that the definition of the concept of quality of life and the possibility of evaluation is not only qualitative， it can also be quantitative， using instruments for evaluating quality of life， capable of eval-uating indices in a wide variety of populations.

【29】Considering the sociodemographic characteristics of the sam-ple studied， it can be said that the main reason that lead the elderly to attend Social Service of Industry -Brazil is the pre-vention of diseases and health promotion. The analysis of the data found suggests that the Social Service of Industry-Brazil is being valued by the elderly who attend it， as spaces that pre-vent diseases， promote well-being， health and social support. Therefore， among other options， when the elderly attend Social Service of Industry - Brazil， they can practice physical activities that delay the onset of diseases (primary prevention)， for those already sick， avoid complications of chronic diseases (secondary prevention). In addition， the location is favorable for rehabilita-tion， in cases where it was not possible to prevent the disease from worsening and the appearance of sequelae .

【30】The analysis of the global quality of life and domains shows that the elderly in domain2 (psychological) of the elderly is bet-ter than domain4 (environment). The fact that the elderly are better in the domain2 (psychological)， means that： the elderly are better in terms of positive feelings； thought；learning； memory； concentration； self esteem； body image； appearance； negative feelings； spirituality； religion and personal beliefs. However， the elderly are worse in terms of domain4 (environment)， which means they are worse in terms of： physical security； protection； home environment； financial resources； health and social care(availability and quality)； opportunity to acquire new informa-tion and skills； participation in recreation /leisure opportunities； physical environment (pollution / noise / traffic / climate)and transport.

【31】These data refer to the placement of  that an adequate physical environment has a positive in-fluence on the quality of life of the elderly. This may suggest that for the elderly population studied， the lack of an adequate environment is influencing the perception of the quality of their lives. To analyze these data， it is worth remembering the consid-eration of   that when making any kind of subjective assessment of quality of life in the elderly， it is necessary to consider the feeling and the meaning of the changes， gains and psychological losses that occur in the different stages of aging， ranging from physical changes to devaluation Social.

【32】For   the simple possibility of the elderly being active makes them more satisfied with life and， con-sequently， better quality of life， than those elderly people who often do not go out alone and therefore end up easily subjected to isolation and depression. This means that the elderly partic-ipating in this research， because they attend the Social Service of Industry-Brazil， may have a better quality of life than those elderly people who do not perform physical activities or are in nursing homes. In addition， quality of life is the result of several measures based on"biopsychosocial" indicators. Therefore， it encompasses many aspects， such as population characteristics； influence of health promotion and disease prevention at primary， secondary and tertiary levels. From the analysis of these results， it can be said that the fact that the elderly can attend the Social Service of Industry-Brazil， whether for physical or recreational activities， is representing the possibility of social network and affective support， which according to  ， it is very important for people who are in old age. This means that attending Social Service of Industry -Brazil， can enable the elderly to have contact with people， which generates emotional support and reinforces the capacity for self-assessment， that is， it is providing new social contacts， of important significance， since it allows the elderly maintain a social identity. These results may suggest the theoretical consideration of  ， that not only the concept of physical health is linked to quality of life. This means that for the elderly population studied， when assessing their quality of life， they take into account aspects such as： working conditions， economic resources，education， access to health services， family relationships， housing conditions， food， leisure， that is， they evaluate aspects of physical health， mental health， social functions， role performances and general percep-tion of health  . In this sense， in this study， it seems that factors such as： role performance， mental health， social adaptation， and the general perception of health influenced the assessment of the quality of life of the elderly  . With regard to the overall quality of life， the data did not reveal a statistically significant difference in relation to the economic class， that is， having a good financial situation does not guarantee mental health and does not influence the perception of quality of life. This means that the socio-economic condition does not seem to directly influence the perception of well-being and the general satisfac-tion with the lives of the elderly who responded to the survey. Analyzing the results achieved， the proposal by   that the quality of life reflects much more the percep-tion of individuals about whether their needs are being met or if the opportunity for self-realization is being denied， than the state of physical health or social and economic conditions.

【33】These results also correspond to that described by Diener，  that although society is experiencing the era of materialism， studies have shown that there is little significant relationship between the acquisition of goods and the individual's general satisfaction with life.Thus， it seems that the results found in this study suggest that material rewards are not enough for a person to be happy， while factors such as： having family life， having friends， time for reflection， are much more related to the feeling of happiness and consequently the quality of life  .

The data identified that all domains correlate positively and sig-nificantly with the overall quality of life. 【0】ABSTRACT Objective： Avascular Necrosis happens to be one of the most common diseases in patients presenting with a chronic painful hip. We have evaluated these patients in the background of demographic details. Material and Method：Prospective study evaluating 319 patients using conventional X-ray and MRI. Imaging findings were evaluated， and staging of AVN was done on both modalities. Demographic details were documented in the background of clinical settings. Results： 10.6% of the cases were diagnosed on X-Ray (34 patients). Sequential MRI examination picked up 21%MRI (68 patients). X-ray was missing the diagnosis of AVN in nearly 50% of the cases. 46% of the cases (147 patients) were from age groups ranging from 20-40 years， followed by older patients. It is comparatively rare in young and， if present， is associated with other systemic diseases. 60% of the patients were male， and 40% were females. Bilateral hip pain was present in 31% of the cases (100 patients). Right side involvement (37%) was slightly more common than left (32%) in cases with unilateral hip pain. Commonly encountered imaging findings associated were femoralhead marrow ooedema in 59 patients (87%)， double-line sign in 54 patients (79%)， subchondral cysts in 42 patients (62%)， followed by joint effusion， joint space reduction， femoral head altered contour， femoral head fragmentation with collapse. Conclusion： X-ray alone can miss up to 50% of the cases of Avascular Necrosis of the femoral head， especially in milder and potentially salvageable cases. Correct imaging interpretation and grading make the role of MRI pivotal.

【1】KEYWORDS Chronic non-traumatic hip pain， AVN， X-ray， MRI， Bone Marrow Oedema.

【2】Introduction

【3】Avascular necrosis of the femoral head or Osteonecrosis of the femoral head is the cellular death of the bone cells due to compro-mised blood supply. High-risk asymptomatic patients should be screened to detect earlier stages of AVN to facilitate early treat-ment and prevention of subsequent bone destruction. Apart from establishing the presence of AVN， MRI also determines the percentage of involvement of the femoral head weight-bearing surface . MRI uniquely shows bone marrow signal alterations in patients with a wide variety of musculoskeletal complaints . MRI is essential for the overall evaluation of hip pain，cover-ing both bony and soft tissue causes， and it can more precisely pick up articular cartilage pathology . The ever-evolving diag-nostic role of MRI in hip osteonecrosis is widely accepted. AVN is successfully managed by early treatment prior to sub-chondral fracture and cartilage damage . Unluckily， radiography of-ten fails to demonstrate the disease until a substantial portion of the weight-bearing surface of the femoral head is involved. By that time， pathophysiological ischemia of bone marrow and eventual death of trabecular bone becomes inevitable. Screen-ing of asymptomatic， high-risk patients may enable early inter-vention . In 5% to 25% of cases， a history of corticosteroid use was present. The classic presentation was Deep， throbbing Groin pain which was worse with activity. Range of motion was decreased， predominantly in cases of effusion. C sign-pain is described by a cupped hand placed above the greater trochanter. MRI has a Specificity of 98% and sensitivity of 97% in differenti-ating AVN from a non-AVN disease of the femoral head.

【4】This study attempts to estimate the proportion of Avascular Necrosis patients with painful hip， study the spectrum of find-ings， and detect AVN at an earlier stage. We included patients presenting with non-traumatic hip pain (acute or chronic) and all age groups of both sexes. Patients with trauma， frank contraindi-cation to MRI (MRI incompatible implants， Metallic foreign body in situ)， or a history of claustrophobia were excluded.

【5】Pathophysiology of Avascular necrosis of the proximal fe-mur is a disease process which is complicated and initiated by an interruption of blood supply to the femoral head， causing bone tissue death. AVN varies in presentations depending upon the stage. Osteochondritis dissecans is said when an infarction affects the local segment of bone. This is most often seen in weight-bearing bones. When infarction affects an entire epiph-ysis in a growing child， it is called epiphyseal ischemic necrosis. The proximal femur is the most common location for this occur-rence . The aetiology of femoral head avascular necrosis is diverse. Though avascular necrosis can develop idiopathically， most conditions that disrupt the blood supply to a segment of bone can be divided into three categories： Conditions that re-sult in external blood vessel compression or disruption near or within the bone， such as infection or steroid administration. Conditions that result in blood vessel occlusion because of thick-ening of the vessel wall， such as radiation therapy， systemic lupus erythematosus， or giant cell arteritis. Conditions resulting in blood vessel blockage from thromboembolic processes， su chas alcoholism， diabetes， or sickle cell disease .

【6】Radiographic Findings in evaluation in the initial stages of AVN may appear normal for several weeks. One of the first radiographic signs， seen as early as 4 weeks post-injury is a radi-olucent crescent image， representing the collapse of the necrotic subchondral bone of the femoral head. This crescent sign is seen parallel to the superior rim of the femoral head， subjacent to the articular surface. Sclerosis and cyst formation at the femoral head are other characteristic signs of the initial necrotic processes and healing attempts. These radiographic signs can be differen-tiated from the similar characteristic signs of osteoarthritis by the normal preservation of the radiographic joint space， which is not involved in the necrotic process. In advanced stages of AVN， the femoral head will collapse or be flattened because of structural weakness and impaired ability to withstand weight-bearing forces .

【7】The entire femoral head and neck will become more radio-dense because new bone attempts to heal the trabeculae micro fractures and calcification of necrotic marrow. Eventually， the progressive collapse of the femoral head will change joint sur-face congruity and involve the acetabulum. At this advanced stage， joint space will be markedly compromised. Radiologists identify the stages of disease progression by the presence of the foregoing signs. The plain film does not detect stage0 and 1AVN. Between the onset of symptoms and the appearance of radiographic abnormalities delay of 1-5 years may occur. There-fore， normal radiographic findings do not necessarily mean that the disease is not present. A staging system using radiographic findings has been developed by Ficat and Arlet and has been used widely for treating avascular necrosis. This has been sup-planted by the classification system of Steinberg et al.， which incorporates MRI and scintigraphic findings .

【8】Magnetic resonance imaging has recently emerged as the most sensitive， specific， and widely used diagnostic tool for avascular necrosis of the femoral head. In most reports， MRI can diagnose very early lesions with a greater than 90 percent specificity and sensitivity . Asymptomatic， high-risk patient screening may enable early intervention. Imaging findings have been that signal intensity bands or lines within the femoral head are seen surrounding the area corresponding to ischemic bone onT1-andT2-weighted images. The band is thick onT1-weighted images and is thinner and with a second inner band of high signal intensity on T2-weighted images. The appearance on T2-weighted images is known as the “double-line sign"and is considered highly specific for AVN. This band is supposed to represent the reactive interface that separates normal marrow from infarcted marrow .

【9】The signal intensity of central infarcted bone corresponds to areas of bone necrosis seen at histologic examination. High signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images are seen within areas of necrosis when viable， and fatty marrow is still present with prolonged ischemia and necrosis， the necrotic bone has a signal intensity pattern re-sembling that of fluid， with low signal intensity on T1-weighted images and high signal intensity on T2-weighted images. When fibrosis and sclerosis of the involved bone occurs， it is reflected by low signal intensity on bothT1-and T2- and weighted images. Secondary signs and sequelae of AVN can also be seen at MR imaging. The joint effusion or cartilaginous thinning may be present. AVN progresses to the instability of the femoral head with fragmentation and eventual collapse . In the early stages of the disease， there may not be any alteration of the nor-mal signal intensity of the femoral head. The first sign of AVN is nonspecific： diffuse areas of decreased signal intensity are noted in the normally high-signal-intensity fatty marrow on T1-weighted images. This is supposed to be due to ooedema within the marrow. Focal findings along the anterosuperior aspect of the femoral head are more specific： a low-necrotic segment of bone.

【10】Materials and methods

【11】It is a Cross-sectional observational and descriptive study con-ducted in a tertiary care center. Data is analyzed using propor-tions.

【12】All patients underwent MRI with anterior surface coil imag-ing. Oblique imaging planes were used for optimizing the demonstration of normal and abnormal hip anatomy . Long T2 of free water makes detection of body fluids easy T2- in which the fluids have an intense signal relative to solid tissues . True coronal and axial planes give symmetric， bilateral images， which are important in diagnosis and time factors， especially for the femoral head， neck， and intertrochanteric region. Supporting lig-aments， musculature and articular space are better appreciated on axial MR images .

【13】All the MRI examinations， including the image mentioned above， were carried out either on a 3Tesla MRI machine or a1.5Tesla machine. In addition， x rays were carried out on CR/DR system of 1000mA. The presence or absence of joint fluid was analyzed qualitatively， which had an intense high signal cor-responding with that of fluid. Before starting radiographic ab-normalities， mostly increased joint fluid presents， and signal intensity becomes highest after loss of femoral head contour， revealing MRI helps in detecting fluid in the hip joint highly sensitive .

【14】Radiographs were taken with 1000mA X-ray machine of MED-ITRONICS in the department. MR imaging was done with a3Tesla MRI machine or 1.5Tesla machine using abdominal sur-face coils as they allow increased signal-to-noise ratio and im-proved spatial resolution. Radiograph views are taken： Pelvis with both Hips-AP. The patient was given a supine position， and both feet were internally rotated at an angle of 15°. The posi-tion helps in reducing the normal 25 to 30° femoral anteversion， making the femoral neck more clearly visible .

【54】Discussion

【55】Even though marrow oedema affecting the hip is not a specific diagnosis， it is encountered in various hip disorders due to different etiologies. Furthermore， the strong correlation between Also， pain improvement usually parallels the resolution of oedema. Similar associations of marrow oedema with bone infarct have also been suggested . When the clinical exam-ination is suspect for hip disease and plain radiographs are normal or equivocal； MRI is the modality of choice. Early di-agnosis and treatment are important in many disorders. MR provides coronal， sagittal， and axial images in three different planes. The coronal plane is best for comparing one hip with the other. The sagittal plane is most accurate at evaluating the volume of pathology. Finally， the axial plane helps examine the surrounding structures of the femoral head.

【56】In cases with multiple coexisting pathologies，radiographs of the hip could either detect only a single lesion or give negative findings. Thus reinforcing the sensitivity of MRI to avoid miss ing other pathologic foci of importance. Bone marrow signal intensity alterations， which may represent pathology occult to plain radiography of the hips， are easily picked up on MRI. In patients with persistent hip pain presenting with negative radio-graphy findings， not only for diagnosis but also for treatment planning， a timely performed MRI of the hips is important.

【57】A.J.Khanna et al. proved excellent agreement between the full and screening MR examinations for detecting and determin-ing the extent of AVN. The study evaluated the percentage of femoral head involvement that acts as a weight-bearing surface and subsequently followed up for osteonecrosis-positive hips on both images. MRI demonstrated that femoral head collapse did not occur when less than 25% of the weight-bearing surface was involved. In nearly half of the patients， the femoral head col-lapse occurred when 25%-50% of the surface was involved， and occurred in 87% of the hips when more than 50% of the femoral head weight-bearing surface was involved. As X-ray diagnosis is difficult in the early stages of AVN，MRI is nearly always used. Apart from being performed rapidly， MR hip screening protocol is also potentially inexpensive in patients with clinical suspicion of AVN， thus enabling its more widespread use in patient care. Due to time factors in screening，training technologists to po sition patients by palpating the greater trochanter and quickly centering the images at that level with precision becomes im-portant. A set of coronal T1-weighted scout images was then obtained. They used a body coil for both radiofrequency trans-mission and reception.

【58】The femoral head typically contains focal or diffuse abnor-mally low or intermediate signal on T1- weighted imaging se-quences， the T2-weighted/STIR imaging sequences are capable of showing variable signal intensity， including areas of increased signal thought to represent bone marrow oedema. Subchondral T2-weighted curvilinear signal hyperintensity and T1-weighted signal hypointensity may be observed in the anterosuperior aspect of the femoral head， referred to as the “crescent sign"(or Caffey sign)， is best seen on coronal and sagittal images and suggests the presence of a subchondral fracture. Hypo in-tense signal in epiphysis on all imaging sequences， including contrast-enhanced sequences， points towards advanced necrosis and confirms microfractures' presence. In addition， abnormal thickening and altered femoral head articular cartilage signal intensity characteristics can be seen due to nutrition derived from synovial fluid .

【59】To determine the amount and appearance of fluid in the joint， Donald G. Mitchell et al. studied hip MR images of 36 patients with documented AVN and 80 hips without evidence of joint disease and examined the relationship of joint effusions to AVN. The joint fluid was graded from 0 to 3， which had an intense signal higher than fat. MR images of all AVN cases showed characteristic focal defects in the weight-bearing portion of the femoral heads. The hips with AVN were staged according to the Steinberg modification of the radiographic classification de-scribed by Arlet. Normally， small amounts of fluid are present in both hips， and it is present in significant quantities in patients with avascular necrosis. Increased joint fluid in AVN may be present even before radiographic abnormalities occur， but fluid quantity is greatest after there is a flattening of the femoral head. High sensitivity MRI for detecting fluid in the hip joint makes it the method of choice， whereas radiography lags in sensitivity and specificity . In our study， we have staged 66 patients with no traumatic osteonecrosis， one malignant bone lesion pa-tient with superimposed AVN and one sacroiliitis patient with Coexisting AVN， according to Ficat and Arlet classification and had qualitatively described the presence or absence of joint effu-sion when the fluid present was sufficient enough to surround the femoral neck. In 18 patients， AVN of the femoral head af-fected only one hip. While rest 50 cases showed bilateral femoral head involvement. Necrotic trabecular bone collapse leads to femoral head flattening in advanced cases combined with resorp-tion. Mechanical deformity of the femoral head can also result in additional ischemic episodes and an increased percentage of necrosls.

【60】A strong correlation of hip pain affected by AVN of the femoral head with bone marrow oedema has been proven by Guo-Shu Huang et al. Effects of bone marrow oedema are fur-ther enhanced by joint effusion. The above findings became most noticeable as the severity of AVN increased and the likelihood of increasing when the patient had pain. They evaluated a total of 110 hips were evaluated in this study， of which 98 patients presented with pain. Bone marrow oedema and joint fluid were evaluated on MR images. Bone marrow oedema was identified as an ill-defined area of T1 hypointensity with the corresponding hyperintense signal on T2-weighted or inversion recovery im-ages. The most common locations encountered in bone marrow oedema include the femoral head， neck， and intertrochanteric region. The amount of joint fluid was graded from 0 to 3，and AVN was staged using Steinberg classification. Bone marrow oedema severity was directly proportional to the grade of AVN， and maximum occurrence was seen in stage ⅢI disease (72%). The odds ratio for marrow oedema in stage III was seven times greater than that for stage I in AVN femoral heads. Joint effusion also followed a similar pattern， and effusion of grade greater than or equal to 2 was seen most commonly in stage III disease(92%). In the presence of effusion， bone marrow oedema was12.6 times greater when the patient had hip pain than when it was not. Hence a peak for both bone marrow oedema and joint effusions co-existed with stage Ⅲ disease. Bone marrow oedema probably has a stronger association with pain in AVN of the femoral head than joint effusion .

【61】The extent of the collapse of the femoral head as well as the angular span of involvement is better seen on sagittal imaging and predicts future risk of collapse. Perfusion of the proximal femoral epiphysis is assessed by contrast-enhanced imaging. The earliest indicator of LCP disease is hypoperfusion of the proximal part of femoral epiphysis. Diffusion restriction appears immediately after ischemic insult. Both diffusion restriction and apparent diffusion coefficients (ADCs) increase hours a few days later. Intraarticular contrast material in MR arthrography allows detailed evaluation of the articular cartilage surface， the fibrocartilaginous labrum， and congruency of the femoral head with acetabulum .

【62】Conclusion

【63】MRI has gained paramount importance in the medical evalua-tion of chronic hip pain by detecting other co-existing patholo-gies that could be missed on plain radiography. All the patients in our study underwent radiographic examination， followed by MRI. Proper positioning of patients is essential for both. There-fore， the construction of a proper imaging protocol with attention to the specifications of the MR examination technique is a must. From a total of 68 cases of AVN on MRI， 34 were detected on X-ray. AVN was more frequently missed on X-rays， with a milder form of the disease. With the increasing severity of the disease， the findings become more obvious on X-rays.

【64】MRI is important for detecting common associated subtle findings of hip joint effusion， bone marrow oedema， and altered cartilage signal intensity. In addition， in diagnosed cases on X-ray (AVN)， MRI provides a stage of pathology， associated soft tissue changes， fluid collection and bone marrow involvement， thus providing complete evaluation.

【0】Background：

【1】Atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) is a congenital heart disease and usually accompanied by wide range of cardiac and extracardiac congenital anomalies. A concomitant portal vein fibrosis anomaly with AVSD and also suffered from esophageal varices bleeding due to portal hypertension has never been reported.

【2】Case Report：

【3】A 15 years old junior high school girl suffered from hematemesis due to variceal bleeding. A history of AVSD during her neonatus period was obtained from her father (a neurologist). The first episode of variceal bleeding was happened at 14 months old three days after AVSD closure surgery and treated with endoscopic variceal sclerotherapy. The variceal bleeding never recurr until age 15 years old. She has no history of clinical signs of infection during neonatus . Recentliver function test was normal and hepatitis viral serological examinations， HBsAg and Anti-HCV， were negative. Ultrasound study at her teen-age showed normal liver with very small diameter and wall thickening ofthe portal vein， low portal flow velocity(9.2 cm/s)， splenomegaly and also cavernous transformation of the portal vein. Recent endoscopy examination revealed moderate enlargement of the esophageal varices and endoscopic variceal ligation was performed to prevent further episodes of bleeding. Echocardiog raphy showed normal wall motion and ejection fraction without signs of pulmonary hypertension.

【4】Concluslons：

【5】To our knowledge this is the first report of variceal bleeding due to extrahepatic portal hypertension in a patient with portal vein fibrosis and history of atrioventricular septal defect in which these anomalies were concomitantly congenital in origin.

【6】Key words：
