【8】BACKGROUND

【9】Atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) is a congenital disease which commonly associated with Down syn-drome trisomy 21 andusually accompanied by other cardiac and extracardiac congenital anomalies . Esophageal varices is commonly formed in relation with portal hypertension due to liver cirrhotic or non cirrhotic disease. Studies of 301 cases in The United States  and 103 cases in India  did not mention about venous anomaly including portal vein anomaly as an extracardiac anomaly of AVSD. We report a case with history of AVSD and esophageal varices during neonatus with recurrent variceal bleeding in her teen-age.

【10】CASE REPORT

【11】Sk， a 15 years old junior high school girl has a history of AVSD in her neonatus period and according to her parent (her father is a neurologist) the disease was diagnosed when she was 9 months old. Surgery for closing the AVSD was done at 14 months old and she suffered from severe hematemesis three days later.Esophageal varices was diagnosed as a cause of the gastrointestinal tract bleeding and she followed many sessions of sclerotherapy treatment which obliterated the varices and no bleeding epi-sode was reported until 14 yearslater. Unfortunately her medical record during neonatus was not avail-able anymore. She was hospitalized at age 15 years old due to hematemesis and melena episode and received packed red cell transfusions and also oc-treotide infusion. The bleeding stopped after 24hours oftreatment.Esophagogastroduodenoscopy examination revealed two bluish column of grade F2esophageal varices without significant abnormalities in the stomach and duodenum. Actually we discussed this patient with a vascular surgeon and decided to plan splenorenal shunt surgery but her father did not approve yet because he still unsure about the risk and the result of the surgery and endoscopic variceal ligation was chosen for temporary further bleeding prevention. Ultrasound study showed normal liver parenchyma echostructure and hepatic vein， however spleen enlargement was found. Paraumbilical vein dilatation and ascites were not detected. Doppler ultrasound examination of the portal vein showed narrowing of the extrahepatic portion of the portal vein lumen into very small diameter and difficult to examine due to portal vein wall thickening (severe extrahepatic portal vein fibrosis). Cavernous trans-formation of the portal vein was found. Thrombus sign was not found in the patient portal vein. The portal vein flow study showed hepatopetal flow with velocity 9.2 cm/sec indicated portal hyperten-sion and might be due to portal flow obstruction. Recent echocardiographic study showed normal heart function with ejection fraction 78%， normal wall motion， and without signs of pulmonary hypertension. Only right bundle branch block and episodes ofventricular extrasystole were found from her electrocardiographic examination. No history of omphalitis and other abdominal infection during neonatus and also there was no problem with her mother pregnancy based on her father information. The patient has normal body growth. Liver function test was in normal range. HBsAg and Anti-HCV were negative.

【12】DISCUSSION

【13】The cardiac and extracardiac congenital anomalies are common in AVSD such as outflow tract anoma-lies， complete heart block， cleft lip and cleft palate， multicystic dysplastic kidney and can involve the gastrointestinal system as well . Two studies with more than one hundred cases of AVSD did not mention about venous anomalies， particularly portal vein fibrosis，as a concomitant extracardiac anomaly of AVSD. The portal vein fibrosis of this case was accompanied by cavernous transformation. The pathogenesis of cavernous transformation of portal vein can be congenital malformation that replace nondeveloped portal vein， hemangioma of portal vein or the end product of portal vein thrombosis . The esophageal varices formation in this case related with extrahepatic portal hyper-tension due to the extrahepatic portal vein fibro-sis. Intrauterine infection with the inflammatory process was recognized as the etiology of extrahepatic portal hypertension and portal vein fibrosis， however there were still many cases with obscure etiology that were categorized as "idiopathic”. A necropsy study in a 20 months old male child with pulmo-nary hypertension due to congenital porto-caval shunt found complete old fibrotic occlusion of the extrahepatic portal vein and multiple old and florid occlusions of fetal vessels with focal lymphoplasmo-cytic inflammation indicate intrauterine infection as the cause of complete closure of the portal vein\[\]. Angiographic study in the extrahepatic portal obstruction in 38 childhood including 22 idiopathic cases showed that 37 patients suffered from com-pletely occluded portal vein with varies of site and extent of occlusion， from only the occlusion of the terminus of the portal vein at the hepatic hilum until the entire length of the portal vein， espe-cially in 11 out of 12 patients with inflammatory etiology .

【14】The idiopathic extrahepatic portal hypertension in children was more common than omphalitis or sec-ondary umbilical vein catetherization causes and the concomitant congenital cardiac anomalies that ever reported were atrial septal defect (ASD)， ventricular septal defect (VSD)， Fallot’s tetralogy， and mitral valve prolaps .AVSD has not been reported be-fore. Some extrahepatic portal hypertension may be congenital in origin. To differentiate the non inflam-mation congenital causes of extrahepatic portion of portal vein fibrosis from the intrauterine inflamma-tion process is rather difficult without post mortem histological examination. Study in six infants with calcified portal vein thromboemboli (CPVT)， and only three of the infants have chromosomal abnor-malities， showed concomitant ventricular septal defect(VSD) in one infant， and post mortem study in one other infant revealed fibrotic process in the CPVT Our AVSD with portal vein fibrosis and extrahepatic portal vein hypertension patient is still alive with nor-mal social life without growth retrardation， history of omphalitis， or intraabdominal infection during neonatus.

【15】Furthermore， based on several reports which have been mentioned earlier， the congenital cardiac anom-alies can be associated with extrahepatic portal vein hypertension and in addition the common extracar-diac anomaly in AVSD， we suggest that the portal vein fibrosis and extrahepatic portal vein hypertension in this case were congenital in origin as concomitant anomaly with AVSD. The only possiblility of etiology that we can not be confirmed is the intrauterine infec-tion causes， however usually intrauterine infection， such as toxoplasmosis and cytomegalovirus infection， cause multiple organ abnormalities and bad prognosis in early life. A case study of post mortem congenital toxoplasmosis in neonatus showed widespread organ involvement with normal portal vein . A similar result was also showed in a congenital cytomegalo-virus infection case study .

【16】The more important thing is the prognosis of this pa-tient. The possibility of variceal rebleeding episodes or portal hypertension-related pulmonary hypertension that can be experienced even in non cirrhotic portal hypertension ，will influence her quality of life in the future . These complications could be hap-pened in her adulthood if the portal hypertension is not corrected permanently. Studies in extrahepatic portal vein obstruction-related growth retardation， especially in childhood， showed conflicting results and might be associated with concomitant liver diseases. Our patient has normal body growth.

【17】Eventhough the patient has been suffering from portal hypertension almost 14 years， pulmonary hy-pertension signs， such as triscupid insufficiency， right ventricular hypertrophy and finally right heart failure， were not detected by physical and echocardiog raphy examinations. Early closure of the AVSD has possibly reduced the risk of pulmonary hypertension in this patient. The splenorenal shunt surgery has been chosen medically as the treatment of choice， however her father still not approve and the variceal ligation treatment was only for temporary treatment. By comparing with the variceal sclerotherapy result that has resisted for 14 years we hope that the vari-ceal ligation will also give long-term variceal bleed-ing prevention.

【18】To our knowledge this is the first report of AVSD patient with extrahepatic portal vein fibrosis-related extrahepatic portal hypertension which consequently increased the portal pressure and resulted in variceal bleeding episodes. Portal vein fibrosis in non-congeni-tal cardiac diseases is actually not rare complications. A study in autopsied patients showed that portal vein fibrosis were common in cardiac diseases especially severe congestive heart failure and arterial thrombosis and also the incidence was increased with age . The variceal bleeding episodes has also ever been reported in 48 years old female with Fallot’s tetral-ogy due to splenic vein thrombosis . The impact of AVSD repairing surgery to variceal bleeding epi-sode three days after AVSD closure in this patient was unknown， however it might be only coincidence because the AVSD closure itself will not increase the portal pressure.

【19】CONCLUSIONS

【20】In conclusion， this is the first report of a patient with history of AVSD and esophageal varices during neo-natus with recurrent episode of variceal bleeding in her teen-age due to extrahepatic portal vein fibro-sis-related extrahepatic portal hypertension which was congenital in origin as concomitant anomaly with AVSD.

【0】Background

【1】Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) accounts for less than 5%of all thyroid malignancies. ATC accounts for nearly 50% of all deaths attributed to thyroid cancers . ATC is a rare entity and there is a paucity of reports in the published literature. In most reported cases， patients suffer from pressure-related symp-toms that occur due to local progression of the disease. Thus， palliative approaches， such as a tracheostomy， are required.

【2】ATC is commonly observed among patients who are between 60to 70 years old with an average median survival of 5 months. Nearly 20% of patients with ATC survive for a little over 12months after one year of diagnosis .

【3】The American Joint Committee on Cancer defines all the stages of ATC as stage IV due to its extremely aggressive behavior. ATC staging is divided into 3 sub-stages： Va， lb，and Mc. The staging is dependent on the extension of the primary tumor， the presence of any lymph node involvement， or the presence of distant metastases. In the past 6 decades，the survival rate has not increased significantly. Multimodal treatment including surgery， chemotherapy， radiation， and/or targeted therapy can be considered as a superlative strategy for improving outcomes in patients with ATC .

【4】There are a few risk factors attributed to the development of ATC. In a prospective study conducted by the American College of Surgeons Commission on Cancer， 25% of patients were found to have a history of thyroid goiter， while 10% had a fa-milial history of goiter .

【5】Patients with ATC present with local symptoms at the begin-ning， such as central neck mass， noticeable dysphagia， hoarse ness or voice change， and stridor. Patients may also present with regional symptoms， such as a noticeable lymph node mass and/or neck pain. Some of the most common systemic symp-toms include weight loss， anorexia， and shortness of breath. Metastases is common in patients with ATC. As per a recent review， nearly 50% of patients have metastases at the time of presentation while nearly 25% develop metastasis during the course of the disease . Lung， bone， and brain are the most common sites of metastasis . We report here an unusual case of ATC with gastrointestinal metastasis.

【6】Case Report

【7】A 72-year-old euthyroid female with hypertension presented to the clinic with swelling of the neck and breathlessness. The patient had a family history of cancer. Her uncle was di-agnosed with lung cancer.

【8】A neck sonography revealed a 6.8x5.4x4 cm heterogeneously hypoechoic lesion with moderate internal vascularity in the left lower lobe of the thyroid. The lesion caused lateral displace-ment of the left common carotid artery and internal jugular vein with moderate luminal narrowing to the adjacent part of the left internal jugular vein. A fine needle aspiration cytology revealed colloid goiter in the left thyroid.

【9】A whole-body positron emission tomography-computed tomog raphy scan was performed. A large hypermetabolic lobulated mass lesion arising from the left hemi-thyroid was observed. The lesion caused a mass effect on the trachea， displacing it on the right side. The lesion was observed to have reached the mediastinum up to the aortic arch level as well as the prevas-cular region with loss of fat planes . Hypermetabolic lymph nodes on the left side were present. A metastatic nod-ule was observed in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe of lungs . The stomach and bowel loops were unremarkable and showed physiological uptake of F-18fluorodeoxyglucose.

【10】The lesion was observed to have laterally splayed the strap muscles on the left side. A histopathological correlation was required at this stage to confirm malignant etiology. Intraoperatively， a big hard mass was seen that almost replaced the entire left node of the thyroid gland. It was displacing the trachea on the right side but could be dissected free from it. The patient underwent a total thyroidectomy and left modi-fied radical neck dissection.

【11】The histopathology report was suggestive of anaplastic carci-noma of the thyroid with capsular invasion and extra thyroi-dal extension. Three out of 22 lymph nodes dissected on the left side showed the presence of disease without any extra-capsular extension. The pathologic stage was confirmed to be pT3bN1bM1. As per the eighth edition of the American Joint Committee on Cancer staging manual， the patient had stage Ic anaplastic thyroid carcinoma.

【12】A follow-up ultrasonography revealed an ill-defined septated collection at the left thyroid bed.

【13】Prophylactic external beam radiotherapy (60 Gy in 30 fractions) was given to the patient covering the neck and superior me-diastinum. During adjuvant radiation therapy， the patient pre-sented with persistent nausea and vomiting. The patient did not respond to proton pump inhibitors. Post-radiation therapy， the patient underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy，where7 to 8 large polypoidal lesions were observed in the stomach. No active bleeding was observed. Biopsy results confirmed the metastasis was from ATC. The length of survival of the patient was 2.5 months from the date of presentation. The patient died due to hemorrhagic shock.

【14】Discussion

【15】ATC is an uncommon， rapidly growing neoplasm. It is charac-terized by a poor prognosis with a mean survival time of 4 to7 months . An estimated 20-50% of patients who present with early tumor dissemination report to be positive for distant metastases， while 90% report to be positive for adjacent tissue invasion at the time of presentation . Based on current ev-idence， the most common site of metastases in patients with ATC include the lung and the bone. However， in some cases， the adrenals， heart， pleura， pancreas， or even kidneys could be involved . In a hallmark paper， common metastases sites of ATC were observed in adrenals (24%)， heart (18%)， pleura(29%)， pancreas (4%)， and kidneys (13%) . The frequency of metastases was as follows： gastric (4%)， mesentery or peri-toneum (13%)， and jejunum (2%) .

【16】A case of ATC with isolated metastasis to the gastrointes-tinal region is extremely rare with only 2 cases reported in the PubMed database . In the patient case reported by Hernandez et al.， there was no gross extra thyroidal exten-sion observed .

【17】ATC presents with local symptoms as was observed in our pa-tient case. In the context to distant metastasis， 50% of patients would present at the time of diagnosis， while 25% would de-velop metastasis during the course of the disease. It is through hematogenous spread that early distant metastasis of the tu-mor occurs in patients with ATC.

【18】In our patient case， sheets and islands of undifferentiated cells with eccentric nucleus were observed . Immunochemistry was suggestive of ATC with thyroid tran-scription factor 1 (TTF-1)， cytokeratin， Pax8， and C53 pos-itive while calcitonin and thyroglobulin were negative. Immunohistochemistry can complement histopathology for accurate diagnosis of uncommon tumors . Radiation therapy is a well-tolerated treatment approach with or without sur-gery or chemotherapy in the context of loco-regional control for patients with ATC . Multimodal treatment comprised of surgery and combined with radiation when feasible is recom-mended . As per the American Thyroid Association guide-lines， there is no specific data from randomized control trails for the treatment of patients with ATC. The treatment recom-mendations should be based on the experience of non-ran-domized trials， case series， or epidemiological databases .

【19】Conclusions

【20】ATC still remains a fatal solid tumor and has the most aggres-sive progression among thyroid malignancies. Prognosis has been reported to be better in younger patients and in those without distant metastasis. In this study， we reported a pa-tient case of ATC with gastrointestinal metastasis. Patients with ATC metastasis have a poor prognosis despite multimodal therapy. This is the first case of ATC with gastrointestinal me-tastasis reported in India.

【0】Background： The COVID-19 pandemic is an ongoing cause of the current global healthcare crisis. Several vaccines were approved for use by emergency vaccination campaigns worldwide. At present， there are very few reports of COVID-19 vaccine-induced immune-thrombotic thrombocytopenia， a variant of heparin-induced thrombocyto-penia (HIT)， in comparison to the massive number of vaccinated people worldwide.

【1】Case Report： A 59-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department with a 3-day history of sudden-onset left leg pain 7 days after receiving her first dose of BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 (Pfizer-BioNTech). She was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) and found to have a positive HIT screen with optical density (0D) of 0.6 via ELISA test. She was hospitalized for 4 days and discharged home with an oral anticoagulant \[rivaroxaban).

【2】Conclusions： This case report describes a possible link between BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 (Pfizer-BioNTech) vaccination and thromboembolism. However， further data are needed to support such an association.

【3】Keywords： COVID-19·COVID-19 vaccine· Pulmonary Embolism ·Venous Thrombosis

【4】The COVID-19 pandemic continues to be a major healthcare crisis worldwide. Several vaccines have been developed and approved for use by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and others by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) through an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) . While vaccination programs are ongoing in most nations， multiple questions have been raised regarding their safety profiles. EMA reported 222 cases of newly developed thrombosis and throm-bocytopenia shortly after vaccination with ChAdOx1 nCoV-19(AstraZeneca)； most of the reported cases were in females un-der the age of 55 years .Among 54 million recipients of the Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA vaccine， 35 possible cases of central ner-vous system thrombosis were reported  and there was only1 case of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) among 3010 vaccinated health workers in Italy . Also， there have been a few reports of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis among more than 7 mil-lion recipients of the Johnson & Johnson/Janssen vaccine and5 million recipients of the Moderna mRNA vaccine . The pro-posed mechanism in vaccination with the ChAdOx1 nCoV-19vaccine is named vaccine-induced immune-thrombotic throm-bocytopenia (VITT)， a variant of heparin-induced thrombocy-topenia (HIT) . We report extensive thromboembolism in a59-year-old woman that occurred 7 days after receiving the first dose of the BNT162b2 Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA vaccine.

【5】Case Report

【6】A 59-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department(ED) at Sultan Qaboos University Hospital (SQUH) with a 3-day history of sudden-onset left leg pain. There was no history of trauma， immobilization， surgical intervention， local injections， fever， weight loss， miscarriages， or skin rash. Her medical back-ground included type 2 diabetes mellitus， osteoarthritis， and COVID-19 pneumonia in September 2020， which required hos-pitalization in the general ward for 1 week， with no residual complications. Her regular medications were metformin 1000mg 2 times daily and ethinylestradiol 30 mcg+levonorgestrel150 mcg， a combined oral contraceptive pill (OCP)， with no in-terruption of therapy for the past 20 years. She received her first dose of BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 (Pfizer-BioNTech) 7days before her current symptom's onset and approximately7 months after her diagnosis of COVID-19 pneumonia.

【7】On physical examination she appeared alert and oriented. Her vitals were as follows： temperature 37.1℃， blood pres-sure 161/99 mmHg， heart rate 106 bpm， respiratory rate 24bpm， and oxygen saturation 98% on ambient air. The left leg was swollen and warm with calf tenderness. Chest ausculta-tion revealed bilateral vesicular breath with no added sounds. Other systematic examinations were unremarkable. Laboratory findings are presented in Table 1. Results of a full blood count including plate lets count， coagulation profile， and renal param-eters were normal. However， D-dimer was markedly high at24 mg/L FEU. Twelve-lead electrocardiography (ECG) showed sinus tachycardia with no significant ST-segment or T-wave changes. Troponin T and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic pep-tide (ProBNP) were 9 ng/L and 583 pg/mL，respectively. Duplex ultrasonography of the lower limbs showed acute DVT involv-ing the common femoral， superficial femoral， popliteal， poste-rior tibial， anterior tibial， and deep calf veins of the left lower limb. Due to tachycardia， the patient underwent computed pul-monary tomography angiography (CTPA)， which showed saddle thrombus in the bifurcation of the pulmonary trunk and 40 ex-tensive bilateral main pulmonary arteries emboli extending to the lobar segmental and subsegmental branches .

【9】APTT - activated partial thromboplastin time； CRP - C reactive protein； Hb- haemoglobin； HIT - heparin induced thrombocytopenia； eGFR - estimated gomeurlar filtration rate； PT - prothrombin time； ProBNP-N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide.

【10】The pulmonary embolism (PE) severity index was 59， with the absence of right ventricular (RV) strain， elevated ProBNP，and negative troponin. Therefore， she was managed initially with enoxaparin 1 mg/kg 2 times daily， and she remained hemo-dynamically stable after the initiation of anticoagulation， with a temperature of 37.0℃， blood pressure 130/70 mmHg， heart rate 90 bpm， respiratory rate 19 bpm， and oxygen saturation97% on ambient air. In view of the close time interval be-tween the COVID-19 vaccine and the onset of her symptoms， a blood sample for HIT ELISA was collected on the 2nd day of admission and was reported positive on the 4h day . Given the positive HIT test， enoxaparin was ceased， and the patient was started on rivaroxaban 15 mg twice daily for 21days， followed by rivaroxaban 20 mg once daily for a total of3 months， and she will be followed in the thrombosis clinic.

【11】Discussion

【12】BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 (Pfizer-BioNTech) is currently used for SARS-CoV-2 massive vaccination campaigns worldwide. A medium of 2 months safety profile in 43 252 participants was provided by the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine trial， which showed safety profiles similar to those of other viral vaccines. Of note， only 4 reported adverse drug reactions (ADRs) were considered serious， and they included： ventricular arrhythmia， axillary lymphadenopathy， leg paresthesia， and shoulder inju-ry. Other ADRs were mild to moderate local or systematic re-actions . Also， hypersensitivity-related ADRs were observed in 0.63% of vaccinated people， including few anaphylaxis re-actions . Recently， many cases of VITT have been reported， with incidence apparently between 1 in 125 000 and 1 in 1mi llion， with most of them attributed to the ChAdOx1 nCoV-19Vaccine ， and only 1 reported case of DVT was linked to the BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccine .

【13】VITT usually presents as new onset of thrombocytopenia and confirmed venous or arterial thrombosis within 4 to 16 days af-ter receiving COVID-19 vaccination . The typically shared lab-oratory findings were： platelet count less than 150x10°/L， raised D-dimer， and inappropriately low fibrinogen level. The proposed mechanism of VITT is linked to the presence of antibodies to platelet factor 4-polyanion complexes (PF4)， which induce a mas sive platelet activation via the Fc receptor， similarly to the cases of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) that are detected by HIT ELISA assay . In our patient， HIT ELISA was positive with optical density (OD) of 0.6， and the patient had normal platelet counts， which is similar to some previously reported cases of HIT.Unfortunately， the HIT functional assa y- Serotonin Release Assay (SRA) or Heparin-Induced Platelet Aggregation (HIPA) -is not available in Oman； therefore， it was not sent for confirmation.

【14】Chronic sequelae of COVID-19 resulting in immune-thrombot-ic changes can cause a wide range of clinical manifestations， which have been linked with severe COVID-19 courses requir-ing hospitalization， and typically occurring 30 to 90 days after discharge .Thus， for those 2 reasons， the likelihood of COVID-19-related VTE in our patient was low.

【15】It is well known that estrogen-containing OCPs increase the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) by effacing hemosta-sis pathways. VTE association with OCP has been observed with higher doses of estrogen (> 50 mcg). Moreover， the risk is higher with early use， specifically in the first 6 to 12 months of initiation . Our patient reported using a combined OCP for the past 20 years with no interruption， and she was on a small dose of estrogen in the form of ethinylestradiol 30 mcg only.

【16】Clinical assessment of our patient was not suggestive of oth-er autoimmune diseases or occult malignancy as a precipitat-ing factor for VTE. In the absence of an obvious explanation for the extensive DVT and bilateral PEs， and the proximity of COVID-19 vaccination， we believe that our patient's presen-tation is probably related to a rare ADR of BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 (Pfizer-BioNTech).

【17】This case demonstrates a rare occurrence of extensive throm-boembolism in 59-year-old woman， 7 days after receiving the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine， with no other possible explanation for her VTE. At present， there are few reports of thrombosis among millions of COVID-19 vaccine recipients， supporting the association of COVID-19 vaccines and spontaneous HIT as a possible new rare vaccine-related ADR. However， further data are needed to support such an association.

【0】ABSTRACT Chemical toxicology is a rapidly evolving field that targets various types of cancer cells. The strategies are based on"glucose metabolism"， "mechanisms of cell death"，“bioactivation" and “enzyme induction". Cancer cells heavily rely on abnormal glycolysis， which involves overexpressed hexokinase II (HKII). This catalyzes the first step of glycolysis， therefore， therapeutically targeting HKII. This allows it to change critical metabolic pathway in cancer cells. Abnormal glycolysis coverts large amount ATP to promote growth， so， another attractive target for tumor therapy is apoptosis induced by glucose deprivation. Cancer cells not only consume glucose， but also require glutamine， another major nutrient. Specifically， glutamine which is precursor of intermediates of Krebs cycle. As a result， glutamine starvation may also be a future strategy that researchers could use for cancer therapy. Even though glucose metabolism is one of the major cancer therapy targets in chemical toxicology， some reactive metabolite byproduct of glycolysis has become a hot topic for treating cancers， such as methylglyoxal will reacts with glutathione (GSH) in non-enzymatical condition to form lactoylglutathione (LGSH). This could accumulate to a high concentration level of tumor cells and promote tumor growth. This allows the argument to be made that methylglyoxal inhibits the detoxification of reactive metabolites is， as it suppresses the growth of cancer cell.

【1】KEYWORDS glucose metabolism， mechanisms of cell death， bioactivation， enzyme induction， Warburg effect

【2】Introduction

【3】Chemical toxicology is a rapidly evolving field that targets vari-ous types of cancer cells. The strategies are based on “glucose metabolism"，“mechanisms of cell death"，“bioactivation"and“enzyme induction". Cancer cells heavily rely on abnormal gly-colysis， which involves overexpressed hexokinaseⅡ(HKII). This catalyzes the first step of glycolysis， therefore， therapeutically tar-geting HKII. This allows it to change the critical metabolic path-way in cancer cells. Abnormal glycolysis coverts large amount ATP to promote growth， so， another attractive target for tumour therapy is apoptosis induced by glucose deprivation. Cancer cells not only consume glucose but also require glutamine， an-other major nutrient. Specifically， glutamine which is the precur- sor of intermediates of the Krebs cycle. As a result， glutamine starvation may also be a future strategy that researchers could use for cancer therapy. Even though glucose metabolism is one of the significant cancer therapy targets in chemical toxicology， some reactive metabolite byproduct of glycolysis has become a hot topic for treating cancers， such as methylglyoxal will react with glutathione (GSH) in non-enzymatical condition to form lactoylglutathione (LGSH). This could accumulate to a high con-centration level of tumour cells and promote tumour growth. This allows the argument to be made that methylglyoxal inhibits the detoxification of reactive metabolites is， as it suppresses the growth of cancer cell.

【4】Review of Warburg effect

【5】Otto Hinrich Warburg， an oncology researcher， made the first observation of mode of action of the respiratory enzyme and dis-covered that： cancer cells up-regulate key enzymes of glycolysis and rely on glycolysis for ATP production regardless of oxygen tension. This is called the Warburg Effect. Cancer cells tend to use glycolysis to obtain energy， even in aerobic conditions. This indicates that tumour cells use mitochondria in a very differ-ent way compared to normal cells. This can lead researchers to believe that dysfunctional mitochondria in a cancer cell may be one of the reasons that there is a high rate of glycolysis in tumour cells， as well as a reason for the growth of cancer.

【6】In normal cells， the metabolic pathway can generate 36 ATP or 2 ATP by anaerobic glycolysis. Glycolysis burning glucose generates 18 times more energy than anaerobic glycolysis. There-fore， normal cells only use anaerobic glycolysis under the condi-tion of lacking oxygen. On the contrary， cancer cells are known to use glycolysis rather than phosphorylation (electron trans-fer chain or OxPhos pathway) to generate energy. This finding applies to various tumours and has become a marker of cancer. Only about 5% of pyruvate been used in the more efficient mi-tochondrial pathway of OxPhos， and up to 85% of pyruvate is used in fermentation as a source of energy  This mechanism is shown in Figure 1. Glucose deprivation and glycolysis kinase enzyme become common targets of cancer therapy due to the Warburg effect.

【7】In 1955， Harry Eagle noted that cancer cells also require a large amount of glutamine. The reason that cancer cell con-sumes glutamine varies. A change in glutamine could lead to changes in the ratio of NADH/NAD+ orFADH/FAD+ and lead to the regulation of gene transcription. Proto-oncogene MYC gene cancer cells make more of the enzyme which could convert glutamine into its downstream products. Glutamine could also regulate the Krebs cycle intermediates， and furthermore regu-late transcription and tumorigenesis. In summary， cancer cells require glucose， but also need glutamine.

【8】Chemical Toxic Strategies

【9】The effect of 3-bromopyruvate

【10】The Warburg Effect observed that cancer cells heavily rely on glucose metabolism regardless of oxygen tension. Therefore， HKII has become one of the major targets in oncology research. HKII catalysis is the first step in most glucose metabolism path-ways， 3-brromopyruvate (3-BP) has been an effective glycolytic inhibitor which targets HKII signalling axis， and has been shown to have strong anti-cancer ability. Based on a chemical view， 3-BP is an analogue of pyruvate with a bromine group and is easy to attack a nucleophilic group such as reduced glutathione (GSH). The mechanism is shown in Figure 2 (B)， which also indicates it's good detoxication ability. 3-BP is unstable in water， and it also pH-dependent. It could have two different mechanisms of action to release a bromo radical under different pH environ-ment  . After bromo radical is released， it could be covalently modified to many enzymes or proteins， which demonstrates the potential of 3-BP regulates HKII. HKII has been reported to up-regulate many tumours expressing. The activity of HKII is regulated by the protein kinase Akt/PKB sig-nalling pathway， due to the protein kinase B (Akt) is able to phos-phorylate residue of HKII at Thr-473 to form an anti-apoptotic effect ， but this mechanism requires mitochondrial-bound HKII.3-BP can dissociate HKII from mitochondria to inhibit the anti-apoptotic effect， thereby reducing ATP production. Disso-ciation of HKII from mitochondrial could also free up binding sites which were occupied， allowing apoptosis regulators such as BCL-2-like protein 4 (BAX) and BAD to promote the expres-sion of cytochrome c into the cytosol to form ROS and eventually induce cell death.

【11】Recent studies of 3-BP on human colorectal cancer(CRC) cells have demonstrated：  HKII expression has illustrated a corre-lated relationship with 3-BP sensitivity.  3-BP could induce CRC cell death depends on the dosage.  3-BP could rapidly phosphorylate Thr-308 residues of Akt to increase expression of3-phosphoinositide-dependent protein kinase-1 (PDK1)； this is also a dose-dependent mechanism.  The sensitivity of 3-BP has been increased under normal glucose condition and conse-quently increases the expression of HKII.  Knockdown， the HKII in CRC cells， will not affect the sensitivity of 3-BP， which reveals that changes in HKII expression will not lead to altered AKT phosphorylation which is induced by 3-BP. In summary， since the expression of HKII is a marker that shows the func-tion of the rate of glucose consumption， altering the glucose condition will lead to changes in HKII expression and alter the sensitivity of 3-BP. Therefore， in CRC cells， under normal glu-cose condition， high expression of HKII displayed an increase of 3-BP sensitivity， which illustrate 3-BP is a promising anti-cancer agent， as it is able to induce the loss of ATP rapidly and eventually cause cells to die.

【12】Metformin's anticancer actions

【13】An increase of dependency on the Warburg effect is a way to keep cancer cell immortal， The metabolic reprogramming from mitochondria demonstrates that the use of microenvironment of glucose deprivation could be another strategy to dealing with cancer cells.

【14】AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) agonist-metformin as one of stress-energy mimicker could produce synthetic metabolic lethality in a glucose deprivation environment. This is adverse to cancer growth in vivo， but under high glucose conditions， metabolic process will cause the cell cycle to arrest. In breast cancer， oncogenes HER2 could protect breast cancer cells under low glucose condition. This mechanism is mainly to protect cancer cells from glucose deprivation-induced apoptosis. Once the metformin is introduced into the glucose-starved breast cancer cell， it displays a dramatic increase in sub-G1 apoptotic cells. Metformin is also dose-dependent， as the concentration of metformin increases under glucose-starved condition. When the metformin dose was increased to 10 mmol/L， the breast cancer apoptosis rate also increased， and the breast cancer cells were killed. Also， AMPK could activate glucose deprivation. Therefore， activation of AMPK could mediate an increase in metformin's anti-cancer ability.

【15】In a recent research study， the effects of metformin-induced tumour cell death are drastically increased in breast cancer-initiating CD44+ CD24-/low cancer stem cell (CDC). Since CD44+ CD24-/low is a non-kinase transmembrane glycoprotein， and it's overexpressed in breast cancer CDCs， it has been re-ported that it could be activated by binding ligand which results in the activation of cell signalling pathways to induces breast cancer cell proliferation. Therefore， this suggests that met-formin is extra sensitive to the glucose-dependent phenotype of CDCs， which confers proliferation advantage to cancer cells. This research indicates that metformin is not only dosage and glucose microenvironment dependent， but also targets cancer cells in a selective scenario.

【16】Targets reactive metabolite production

【17】Clinically targeted metabolic alteration of cancer has been chal-lenging. One new method is to target the detoxification of reac-tive metabolic pathways. Methylglyoxal is a reactive metabolite byproduct of glycolysis that could react with GSH to form lac-toylglutathione (LGSH). The clinical evidence displays LGSH is elevated in human non-small cell lung cancers (NSCLC). This argues that the accumulation of LGSH could be one prominent phenotype of NSCLC.

【18】Formation of LGSH is a detoxification mechanism of methyl-glyoxal. In chemical toxicology， there are two types of conjuga-tion during phase two metabolism of detoxification. Type one conjugation involves： conjugating ligand transferred to function-alized xenobiotic from high energy or activated carrier (in simple term is a xenobiotic conjugating with reactive ligand to form a less toxic conjugated product). In the second type conjugation， conjugating ligand does not need to be activated first. It requires electrophilic xenobiotic to react with conjugating ligand to form the less reactive product. Detoxification of methylglyoxal be-longs to the second type of conjugation mechanism. It requires GSH and methylglyoxal detoxification enzyme glyoxalase 1 (Glo1) to accomplish the process. In NSCLC， GSH was significantly elevated due to increased glucose uptake and metabolism of cancer cells. Increased glycolysis produces a large amount of byproduct -methylglyoxal. Therefore， a high concentration of GSH has been expressed to reduce the toxicity of it. The reason why tumour cells have as detoxification mechanism to methylglyoxal is that the high level of methylglyoxal induces cytotoxicity and irre-versibly reacts with proteins and nucleic acids to form advanced glycation end -products (AGEs). Accumulating of AGEs will reduce tumour growth， therefore， inhibiting detoxification of methylglyoxal. This could become a new approach to killing cancer cells. In other word： preventing GSH from reacting with methylglyoxal inhibits Glo 1 become a crucial point to think of.

【19】Based on the detoxification mechanism of methylglyoxal， which is described above， there are few clinical kinds of research that have been reported. They suggest：  GSH depletion has a more substantial impact on promoting sensitive of methylgly-oxal， and an increase of formation of AGEs eventually leads to inhibition of tumour growth. inhibition of Glo 1 could also occur and cause the same effect as GSH depletion to decrease cancer cell proliferation and viability.  Glo 1 is required for NSCLC tumour growth. Compared to Glo 1 deleted NSCLC cells， Glo1- deficient cancer cell shows evidence of inhibition of tumour growth. This is also confirmed in point 2， which argues that Glo 1 promotes NSCLC tumour growth.

【20】Glutamine deficiency induces apoptosis

【21】Glutamine is a well-known nutrient used by tumour cells for proliferation. The deficiency of glutamine could induce cell apoptosis by depletion of the Krebs cycle intermediates.

【22】As the Warburg effect describes， tumour cells use glucose through glycolytic pathways to produces ATP and metabolic in-termediates for proliferation. However， glucose is only a source of carbon supplement for biosynthesis. It could not supply amino acids (AA) to increase cancer growth. Glutamine is one of the most abundant AA in blood and has been utilized for gener-ating energy for cancer growth. It also acts as a precursor for in-creased proliferation in cancer cells.  Glutamine metabolism also provides a nitrogen source for nucleic acids synthesis， which is required for rapidly proliferating cancer cells. Therefore， most cancer cells are dependent on glutamine and can not sur-vive without it. This effect has also been called “glutamine addiction".

【23】Glucose depletion is toxic not only in cancer cells but also in normal human cells. Therefore， deficiency in glutamine to induce apoptosis of cancer cells can become a new research approach. A recent study reported that glutamine depriva-tion induces apoptosis selectively in cells with activated proto-oncogene MYC， which is a family of regulator gene. What causes apoptosis under glutamine deprivation environment?

【24】Several hypotheses have been developed：  Glutamine deple-tion affects the apoptotic machinery directly. Lack of glutamine will eventually lead to a deficiency of nitrogen sources and regu-late the activity of mTOR. Lack of nitrogen sources will against cell proliferation because cell proliferation and other processes require nitrogen. Kinase enzyme， mTOR， controls protein syn-thesis. The regulation of mTOR activity could introduce an anti-tumour effective in cells. However， mTOR only actives in the absence of exogenous glutamine， so the research indi-cates that inhibition of mTOR does not affect cell viability. The research also demonstrates that apoptosis is not caused by a deficiency of glutathione and ATP， but a deficiency of the intermediates of the Krebs cycle.

【25】Glutamine provides carbon chain for the synthesis of amino groups， AA， and nucleotides. In the Krebs cycle， which is shown in Figure 4， pyruvate and oxaloacetate are less likely involved in glutamine deficiency-induced apoptosis because they do not contain a nitrogen group. The apoptosis is most likely asso-ciated with alpha-ketoglutarate / 2-Oxoglutarate， which is an intermediate of the Krebs cycle. The main purpose for the Krebs cycle is to supply NADH and FADH for the electron transport chain which provides ATPs for multiple metabolic pathways. As a result， once the deficiency of glutamine occurs， the Krebs cyvcle will lack intermediates to form NADH and FADH. This change in the ratio of NADH/NAD+ and FADH/FAD+in mi-tochondria will have a huge impact on the regulation of gene transcription. Therefore， Glutamine function is a precur-sor of intermediates， which catalyze redox reactions. In addi-tion， some of the intermediates， such as alpha-ketoglutarate， succinate， and fumarate can also function as messengers and cofactors to regulate the activity of enzymes which regulate gene transcription and tumorigenesis.

【26】Conclusion

【27】Treatments that are based on chemical toxicology are rapidly evolving in cancer research. 3BP has become a promising anti-cancer agent which induce cancer cells' ATP loss and apoptosis.3BP inhibits the function of HKII to reduce ATP production. Alteration of glucose concentration also affects HKII and 3BP sensitivity. In summary， 3BP alternating metabolic pathways primarily target HKII， which largely impacts cancer cells. Met-formin interacts with the metabolic checkpoint target HER2 to eliminate the tolerance of breast cancer cells. This also illustrates the poisoning of mitochondrial respiratory enzyme activity and has also become a new approach for cancer treatment.Methyl-glyoxal reacts with GSH to form LGSH to decrease the accu-mulation of AGES to promotes NSCLC cell proliferation. This displays an interesting point in the ability of GSH detoxification not always to benefit organisms in oncology. Glutamine depri-vation has a large impact on the Krebs cycle and provides an anti-tumour effect. This has shown that cancer treatment is not only limited in targeting glycolysis pathways， but also limited when there is a deficiency in the Krebs cycle. It could cause apoptosis of cancer cells. In conclusion， toxic chemical strategies targeting various types of cancer cells will represent the fruitful ground for future anticancer treatments.

【0】Background： Lymphoma complicated with hemophagocytic syndrome and tuberculosis has been rarely reported. The clini-cal and radiological presentation of these potentially fatal conditions can be easily confused and there is a po-tential for misdiagnosis.

【1】Case Report： We present a 58-year-old Hispanic female who was admitted to the hospital with dizziness and fever. Her ini- tial admission diagnosis was severe sepsis secondary to community acquired pneumonia. She was started on intravenous antibiotics. Due to mediastinal lymphadenopathy， lymphoma was considered as a differential diag-nosis for which she underwent bronchoscopy and endobronchial ultrasound-guided sampling of her mediasti-nal lymph nodes. Lymph node aspirate was suggestive of lymphoma. Initial cultures were negative. Her clinical course was complicated with respiratory failure， cytopenia， and rapidly progressive cervical lymphadenopa-thy. The patient underwent cervical lymph node excision and bone marrow biopsy. The pathology of the lymph nodes confirmed T cell lymphoma， and bone marrow revealed hemophagocytosis. The patient was started on chemotherapy but she continued to deteriorate and died on day 20 of her hospital admission. Post-mortem results of cultures from a cervical lymph node biopsy and PCR were positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

【2】Conclusions：

【3】We suggest an aggressive tissue diagnosis with staining for acid-fast bacilli for early diagnosis in patients pre-senting with hemophagocytic syndrome secondary to lymphoma as coexisting tuberculosis is a consideration. Tuberculosis re-activation should be considered in patients from an endemic region who present with lympho-ma and a deteriorating clinical condition.

【4】MeSH Keywords： Lymphohistiocytosis， Hemophagocytic · Lymphoma·Tuberculosis

【5】The presence of lymphoma and tuberculosis in the same pa-tient is not an unusual event. The incidence of tuberculosis in patients with lymphoma has been reported to range from0.9% to 13.2% and the presence of miliary tubercu losis in ma-lignant lymphoma has been reported to be 35 times higher compared to the general population. Askling and Ekbom re-ported that the risk of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) follow-ing tuberculosis has been increasing .

【6】Hemophagocytic syndrome， also called hemophagocytic lym-phohistiocytosis (HLH)， is a rare， under recognized hyperinflam-matory syndrome. It can be primary (familial) or secondary to several conditions such as hematological malignancies， infec-tions，and inflammatory or autoimmune disorders. Lymphoma is the most common malignancy and Epstein Bar virus (EBV) is the most common infectious etiology implicated in HLH. Infections， including tuberculosis， have been linked to patho-genesis of HLH； it is recommended that once the diagnosis is established， screening for infections such as miliary tubercu-losis， EBV， cytomegalovirus (CMV)， parvovirus B19， human im-munodeficiency virus (HI)， and human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) should be considered .

【7】HLH is a fatal condition， and it often leads to rapid multi-or-gan failure. The finding of HLH， lymphoma， and tuberculosis in the same patient is very unusual . We present a case of middle aged female with T-cell lymphoma， HLH， and tubercu-losis likely unmasked as a result of fludarabine immunosup-pression therapy.

【8】A 58-year-old Hispanic female with history of hypertension was admitted to the hospital with fever of five days duration and dizziness. She denied dyspnea， cough， chills， night sweats， headache， or gastrointestinal symptoms. There was no histo-ry of anorexia or weight loss. She was born in the Dominican Republic and moved to New York City about 20 years ago. She denied use of tobacco， alcohol， or recreational drugs. On ex-amination， the patient was febrile 39.5℃ (101.4°F) and hypo-tensive with blood pressure of 88/40 mm Hg.

【9】Very small， non-tender， soft cervical lymph nodes were pal-pable. Minimal bilateral rhonchi were heard on chest auscul-tation. Her abdominal， neurological， and cardiac examination was unremarkable. No organomegaly was found and her skin was intact. Chest radiograph revealed diffuse bilateral infil-trates . The patient was admitted to the intensive care unit with the impression of severe sepsis secondary to pneumonia. Laboratory parameters were significant for leu-kopenia (3.2 K/uL)， thrombocytopenia (144K/uL)， and elevat-ed serum lactate dehydrogenase (1，142 U/L). Other laborato-ry results are summarized in Table 1.

【10】The patient received intravenous (lV) fluids， ceftriaxone， and azithromycin for presumptive community acquired pneumo-nia. She had persistent fever with blood， urine， and respira-tory cultures including negative acid-fast bacilli (AFB) stains； her antibiotics were changed to V piperacillin-tazobactam and Ⅳ vancomycin. Transthoracic echocardiogram was nor-mal. Computed tomography (CT) of chest revealed bilateral infiltrates with mediastinal and sub carinal lymphadenopa-thy . There was mild splenomegaly noted on CT of abdomen. The patient underwent flexible fiber optic bronchos-copy (FFB) with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL)， transbronchial biopsies and endobronchial ultrasound transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) on day 6 for high suspicion of malig-nancy. All cultures from FFB including aerobic， AFB， fungal，and viral， were negative. Pathology from TBNA of the lymph node revealed T cell lymphoma. The following markers were posi-tive CD4， CD3， CD43， and BCL-2. CD20，CD10，CD79a and PAX5were negative . Tests for T-cell lymphotropic vi-rus-l (HTLV 1) and EBV were not performed.

【12】Her clinical condition continued to deteriorate with devel-opment of hypoxic respiratory failure requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation on day 15 of admission. A cervi-cal lymph node excisional biopsy was performed for worsen-ing cervical lymphadenopathy and persistent fever to further evaluate lymphoma. Patient developed tumor lysis syndrome with acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis and rasburi-case. Cyclophosphamide and vincristine for treatment of lym-phoma were started on day 19. The patient continued to de-teriorate and died on day 20 after admission.

【13】Cultures for AFB from cervical lymph nodes were report-ed positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex identi-fied by direct molecular detection real-time PCR； pathology

【14】Discussion

【15】The presence of lymphoma and tuberculosis in the same pa-tient has been reported in the literature . Tuberculosis and lymphoma could represent a diagnostic challenge as they share many clinical and radiological features. Fever， night sweats， constitutional symptoms， and weight loss as well as bilateral lung infiltrates and lymphadenopathy can be found in both conditions.

【16】Tissue biopsy remains the most specific and sensitive diagnos-tic procedure when there is a need to differentiate both con-ditions. Necrotizing granulomas typical of tuberculosis can be found in both Hodgkin lymphoma  and NHL . Therefore， positive cultures for mycobacterium or the presence of acid fast bacilli in a biopsy further analyzed by specific molecu-lar diagnostic testing can be used for confirmatory diagnosis.

【17】In patients from endemic countries， diagnosis of a lymphoma may warrant further work-up to ensure ruling out co-exist-ing tuberculosis. Ruiz-Arguelles et al. concluded that the inci-dence of tuberculosis in NHL patients is 35 times higher than in the general population . Interleukin 10 (IL-10)， which is increased in patients with NHL， has been implicated in the re-activation of tuberculosis . The serum concentration of IL-10 has been found to be higher in patients with NHL， which may lead to decreased cell mediated immunity resulting in ac-tivation of latent tuberculosis . It has been hypothesized that the risk of NHL is increased in individuals with history of tuberculosis ， though there are studies which found no association between NHL and tuberculosis . There is no experimental data available to support the role of merely la-tent tuberculosis as an etiological factor for NHL.

【18】HLH is an aggressive and life-threatening syndrome of exces sive immune activation which is observed in the children and adults of all ages. The history of this disease dates goes back to 1939 when Scott and Robb-Smith described it as "histiocyt-ic medullary reticulosis" with features of erythrophagocytosis by proliferating histiocytes. It can be genetic or acquired. The genetic form of HLH is divided into two subgroups depending on whether it is associated with immune deficiencies or not：the familial form has clinical features of HLH only， and the form associated with immune deficiency syndromes has addition-al distinctive clinical features， e.g.， Chediak-Higashi syndrome， Griscelli syndrome， and X-linked proliferative syndrome . Familial forms of HLH were first described in 1952 with con-secutive deaths of involved family members . The famil-ial forms of HLH usually manifest within the first year of life. HLH is associated with several genetic mutations e.g.， PRF1， MUNC13-4，STX1， and STXBP2. Since these mutations are in-herited in an autosomal recessive manner， there is often a neg-ative family history； they are found in only about 40% of fa-milial cases . The familial forms are diagnosed at an early stage， while secondary HLH can occur at any age. A variety of causes are associated with secondary HLH， including， in order of their prevalence， viral infections， malignancies， rheumato-logical disorders， and immune deficiency syndromes . The presence of infection was initially thought to differentiate fa-milial forms from acquired forms of HLH； however， it is now clear that most cases of genetic HLH are triggered by infec-tions as well. In secondary HLH， individuals are mostly healthy before the onset of symptoms， while familial forms might be associated with similar prior episodes .

【19】Among the infectious causes， virus-associated HLH was first described by Risdall et al. in 1979； most of the described pa-tients were immunocompromised . EBV is the most com-mon viral pathogen linked to HLH and is associated with worse prognosis. Mortality associated with HLH secondary to EBV is even higher if the treatment is not started in a timely fash-ion . Other viruses commonly described in association with HLH include cytomegalovirus， human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)， and HIV . Since HIV and HLH share several clinical and laboratory features， diagnosis is often delayed in these pa-tients and autopsy studies have confirmed that the condition is underdiagnosed in patients with HIV .

【20】HLH associated with tuberculosis has been described in the literature. Brastiano et al. reported a comprehensive literature review . Other infectious organisms， including several bac-terial agents， and parasites like leishmania and malaria， can also have causal association with HLH. Fungal infections e.g.， Candida， cryptococcus，Pneumocystis， or Aspergillus cause HLH usually in the setting of AIDS， lymphoma， or other immuno-suppressed states .

【21】Malignancy is responsible for more than 50% of cases of HLH and hematological malignancies， specifically lymphoma， are the most common cause of malignancy-associated HLH. There is limited evidence as to whether the malignancy itself or in-creased risk for infections triggers the syndrome in these pa-tients . Patients with autoimmune conditions including systemic lupus erythematosus， mixed connective tissue dis-order， dermatomyositis， and systemic sclerosis can develop HLH at any time during the course of disease . A specific term called“macrophage activation syndrome" (MAS) is of-ten applied to HLH occurring in the context of rheumatolog-ic diseases. Regardless of etiology， exaggerated inflammatory response and hypersecretion of cytokines also known as“cy-tokine storm"appears to be the underlying mechanism .

【22】HLH constitutes an urgent condition to treat and as its presen-tation is nonspecific， there is a possibility for it to go unrec-ognized. Prolonged fever， hepatosplenomegaly， and cytopenia are cardinal symptoms of HLH. Less frequently lymphadenop-athy， rash， or neurological symptoms are seen. Characteristic laboratory features include elevated serum triglycerides and ferritin， hyperbilirubinemia with mild to moderate transami-nitis， and a low fibrinogen level .

【23】The diagnostic criteria initially proposed in 1991  and lat-er updated in 2004  was derived from pediatric patients’studies only. The diagnosis can be established by identifying a mutation in the HLH gene or if five out of eight criteria are fulfilled； which include fever， splenomegaly， cytopenia affect-ing at least two of three cell lineages， hyperferritinemia， hy pertriglyceridemia，hemophagocytosis in bone marrow， spleen， lymph node or liver， low or absent natural killer cell activity， and increased soluble CD 25 concentration. Many patients fit only two or three criteria and yet have clinical evidence requir-ing treatment of HLH. Our patient had fever， cytopenia affect-ing at least two cell lineages， hyperferritinemia， hypertriglycer-idemia，hemophagocytosis in bone marrow， and splenomegaly on abdominal imaging. In patients with an established genetic abnormality (e.g.， familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocyto-sis (FHL) mutation)， the diagnosis can be established without meeting the other criteria . In addition， the diagnostic cri-teria do not apply to macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) because of the overlap of clinical findings between HLH and autoimmune diseases . Moreover， the criteria have been questioned when applied to critically ill patients . Combining these facts with the lack of gold standard tests， makes the diagnosis of HLH an elusive effort even in suspected cases.

【25】Pathophysiological mechanisms for HLH stems from research of primary HLH. The main feature is inappropriate secretion of cytokines by activated cytotoxic T-cells， natural killer cells and macrophages. In patients with T cell lymphoma， cytokines secreted by tumor cells may be a trigger for HLH. Janka et al. postulate that opportunistic infections in immunosuppressed patients may act as a trigger. Either tuberculosis or lymphoma may have acted as trigger  in our patient.

【26】The prognosis of HLH without prompt treatment is poor. For genetic forms， the median survival is one to two months， and less than 10% probability of survival for three years. Acquired forms of HLH are variable in severity and prognosis， with worse outcomes in malignancy-associated HLH； overall reported mor-tality for acquired HLH surpasses 50%.

【27】The treatment of HLH focuses on suppression of hyperinflam-matory response， treatment of existing triggers， and in famil-ial cases， correcting defect in immune system. Treatment for genetic and acquired HLH and is aimed at suppression of ex-aggerated immune response with immunosuppressive agents. Histiocyte Society recommends induction therapy with corti-costeroids， etoposide， and cyclosporine for eight weeks  and selected cases may need stem cell transplant. However in patients with secondary HLH identifying and treating the trigger seems rational. The role of immunosuppressive ther-apy is not clear .

【28】Our patient represents a very unusual case of HLH presenting as sepsis， later diagnosed as rapidly progressing lymphoma complicated by HLH and M. tuberculosis infection with a dismal outcome. We found only one report in the English literature of these three conditions presenting simultaneously. Ruiz et al.  described a 31-year-old female with stage l high grade NHL who developed fatal HLH， the patient developed miliary tu-berculosis after receiving fludarabine. The authors proposed evaluation for tuberculosis and/or consideration of anti-tuber-culosis prophylaxis in selected patients treated with chemo-therapy. A comparison of our patient with the one described by Ruiz et al. is presented in Table 2.

【29】Conclusions

【30】We report this patient case not only for its rarity， but to remind clinicians that the presence of one disease may eclipse another. In patients from endemic countries， diagnosis of a lymphoma may warrant further work-up to ensure ruling out co-existing tuberculosis especially if the patient's clinical status is deteri-orating. In a critically ill patient with an unclear etiology， more extensive testing of tissue， such as AFB and fungal cultures， should be performed. Tuberculosis should be considered as part of the differential in patients with lymphoma when treatment seems to be failing or there are other signs and symptoms that could be considered"atypical" for the condition， like the rapid-ly growing cervical lymphadenopathy in our patient. HLH is an uncommon and under diagnosed condition with high mortali-ty. It should be considered in critically ill patients if one or two criteria are met and further diagnostic tests， including bone marrow biopsy， should be performed for diagnosis.

【0】Background：

【1】Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1 (APS-1) is an extremely rare autoimmune disorder with an auto-somal recessive inheritance pattern. Its manifestations present in chronological sequence of the components mucocutaneous candidiasis， Addison disease， and hypoparathyroidism. Vascular calcification is a very rare man-ation of the disease， and it may be severe， causing critical lower-limb ischemia and significant morbidity.

【2】To the best of our knowledge， this is the first such case to be reported in Jordan and the Arab region.

【3】Case Report： We present the case of a 29-year-old patient diagnosed with autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1(APS-1). He has Addison disease， hypoparathyroidism， and mucocutaneous candidiasis. He presented with fea-tures of critical lower-limb ischemia and bacterial infection of the left foot. The patient underwent a successful angioplasty and received management of his bacterial and fungal infections and the chronic endocrinopathies.

【4】Conclusions：

【5】Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1 (APS-1) is a very rare disorder. Recognizing its syndromic nature will facilitate an active search for the component diseases and the possible complications， which would allow early diagnosis and management. This applies to the rare vascular complications， which can lead to significant morbidity.

【6】MeSH Keywords： Addison Disease · Angioplasty · Candidiasis， Chronic Mucocutaneous· Hypoparathyroidism·Peripheral Arterial Disease ·Polyendocrinopathies， Autoimmune

【7】Abbreviations：

【8】APS-1 - autoimmune polyglandular (or polyendocrine) syndrome type 1； APECED- autoimmune polyen-docrinopathy-candidiasis-ectodermal dystrophy； AIRE gene - autoimmune regulator gene Autoimmune polyglandular syndromes (APS) are rare syndromes diagnosed by the coexistence of at least 2 autoimmune endo-crinopathies. In addition， nonendocrine autoimmune manifes tations may be present . Autoimmune polyglandular syn-drome type 1 (APS-1) is defined by the coexistence of at least2 of 3 major component diseases： chronic mucocutaneous can-didiasis， autoimmune adrenal insufficiency， and primary hy-poparathyroidism，or only 1 if a sibling has the disease . The syndrome is a rare disorder with an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern . Vascular calcification is a rare manifestation of the syndrome ， and it can be severe， caus-ing significant lesions and ischemia . We present the case of a young patient with mucocutaneous candidiasis and mul-tiple endocrinopathies who presented with features of criti-cal lower-limb ischemia.

【9】A 29-year-old male patient presented with acute left-foot red-ness， swelling ， and chronic dystrophic nails of hands and feet with discoloration . The distal pulses were diminished， with monophasic signals on Doppler examination， and he previously had amputation of left fourth toe due to gan-grene. He was a known case of adrenal insufficiency and hy-poparathyroidism， taking hydrocortisone，fludrocortisone， and calcium supplements and alphacalcidol. The patient had no in-termittent claudication or resting pain， he was not diabetic， and he was a non-smoker. Treatment was started with an intrave-nous antibiotic (Piperacillin/Tazobactam) and antifungal med-ications (intravenous Fluconazole and Miconazole ointment). Bacterial and fungal cultures showed Morganella morganii and Candida albicans sensitive to the given medications. Lab inves-tigations showed elevated WBC count 21.3/mm，elevated ESR and CRP， low parathyroid hormone 1.2 ng/l (N 13-54)， hypo-calcemia Ca 1.7 mmol/l(N 2.1-2.6)， and hyperphosphatemia P1.69 mmol/l (N 0.8-1.6). Otherwise， he had normal kidney， liv-er， and thyroid function tests， and normal adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)， follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)， prolactin， and testosterone levels.

【10】A CT angio showed diffuse calcified atherosclerotic changes of the abdominal aorta and lower-limb arteries， with significant stenosis of the left popliteal artery and poor bilateral distal run off . He underwent an angioplasty with drug-eluting balloons for the left popliteal and tibial vessels. He lab test re-sults and clinical condition improved， and he was discharged after a hospital stay of 2 weeks， with prescription of oral med-ications (prednisolone， fludrocortisone， calcium supplements， alphacalcidol， and voriconazole) in addition to miconazole oint-ment. On follow-up， he had improvement of lower-limb vas-cularity and the bacterial and fungal infections were cured.

【11】Discussion

【12】Polyglandular autoimmune syndromes are a rare heteroge-neous group of genetic diseases of the immune system lead-ing to multiple endocrinopathies. Three types are described in the literature： type 1 (juvenile type)， type 2 (adult type)， and type 3 (the rarest). APS-1 is also known as Whitaker syndrome and autoimmune polyendocrinopathy-candidiasis-ectodermal dystrophy (APECED) . It is a very rare disorder inherited in a sporadic autosomal. recessive pattern and caused by genetic mutations affecting the autoimmune regulator (AIRE) gene on chromosome 21 . Studies have demonstrated the pres-ence of various circulating tissue-specific autoantibodies that cause dysfunction of the target endocrine glands . Also， the mutations lead to defective T cells and neutralizing auto antibodies against IL-22， IL-17A， and/or IL-17F， leading to the immunodeficiency underlying candidiasis .

【13】The syndrome clusters in certain ethnic populations， includ-ing Iranian Jews， Sardinians， and Finns . The highest prev-alence was reported in Iranian Jews with 1 case per 9000， Sardinians with 1 case per 14 400， and Finns with 1 case per25 000 . Low incidences (1： 90 000 to 1： 200 000) had been reported in Norway， Sweden， Poland， Slovenia， Slovakia， Russia， Great Britain， Ireland， and Italy . To the best of our knowledge， the present case is the first to be reported in Jordan and the Arab region. It is suspected that this disorder is underdiagnosed because of a lack of knowl-edge of the condition， the long intervals between the devel-opment of manifestations， the variability of disease severity， and the wide spectrum of clinical presentation .

【14】In APS-1， which is the focus of the present report， 2 out of 3 main components are sufficient for diagnosis，or only 1 if a sibling has the disease . In our patient， all 3 components were present：chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis， hypoparathyroidism， and ad-renal insufficiency or Addison disease. Classically，these compo-nents occur in chronological order， with mucocutaneous candidi-asis usually occurring earliest， followed by hypoparathyroidism， then adrenocortical failure . Additional endocrine and nonen-docrine manifestations may be present， including diabetes type1， hypothyroidism， gonadal failure， alopecia， vitiligo， nail dystro-phy， enamel hypoplasia， pure red cell aplasia. pernicious anemia， asplenia，malabsorption， and autoimmune hepatitis .

【15】Vascular calcification is an extremely rare manifestation of the syndrome. Our patient presented with critical lower-limb isch-emia due to significant stenosis of popliteal and tibial vessels and diffuse calcifications of the abdominal aorta and lower-limb vasculature. Vascular calcification in general is an active cellular process that occurs in response to metabolic insults causing disturbance in the balance between inhibiting and pro-moting factors of vascular calcification . It is suggested that certain cells in the vessel wall can be triggered to differen-tiate into osteoblast-like cells， including vascular smooth mus-cle cells， stem cells， and pericytes . Proposed triggers include oxidative stress， hyperphosphatemia， bone morpho-genetic protein， vitamin D， and parathyroid hormone . Proposed inhibitors include fetuin， osteotegrin， osteopontin， and pyrophosphate .

【16】Vascular calcification is usually associated with ag-ing， atherosclerosis， diabetes mellitus， and chronic kidney disease . One study found coronary artery calcifica-tion in 3 out of 30 cases of sporadic idiopathic hypoparathy-roidism . There are few reported cases in the literature of aortic and/or lower-limb arterial calcification associated with APS-1 ， and only 2 of them had critical lower-limb ischemia . Shikata et al.  proposed the progressive vascular calcification as a peculiar non-random part of APS-1. Also， Ohga et al.  proposed that progressive vascular calci-fication will eventually be recognized as a rare， unexplained， but grave component of APS-1.

【17】The management of our patient included a revascularization procedure for limb salvage， and correction of serum calcium and phosphate disturbances. In APS-1， hypocalcemia is due to hypoparathyroidism and the gastrointestinal manifestations of the syndrome， including intestinal malabsorption， pancre-atic exocrine failure， celiac disease， and intestinal lymphangi-ectasia. Calcium levels should be monitored on follow-up and maintained in the low-normal range .

【18】Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 1 (APS-1) is a very rare disorder. Recognizing its syndromic nature will facilitate an active search for the component diseases and possible compli-cations， which would allow early diagnosis and management. This applies to the rare vascular complications， which can lead to significant morbidity.
